# Playball — Pre-Release Audit (v1.0.0, commit `eb8203b`)

*Audit date: 2–6 October 2026 · Branch `playball` · Scope: the whole repository at HEAD*

---

## PLAYBALL AUDIT SUMMARY

### Verdict: **not ready for production**

Playball is technically ambitious and, most of the time, works. The engine produces sound baseball:
box scores balance, schedules hold their invariants for all three season lengths, double-elimination
brackets are structurally correct across hundreds of simulated Junes, and 25-season careers survive
save → kill → load round trips without ID collisions or NaNs. The interface is far more consistent
than most mobile sports sims.

It is **not shippable today**, for five reasons:

1. **The release build is broken at HEAD (B1).** The 2 Oct overlay commit re-introduced a deleted interview feature's test.
   `tsc` fails, so `npm run build`, `npm run apk` and `npm run aab` all fail from a clean checkout. The vitest suite is red too (1 failed / 2,170 passed).
2. **Actions are not gated by game phase.**
   - A standing job offer can be accepted mid-game, mid-June or on an offseason step. That records a game twice, moves draftees between schools and books a season to the wrong school (C4).
   - God Mode edits run during the postseason or with an empty rotation corrupt the season or produce an autosave that will not load (C2, C3, H3).
3. **The live game loses a resumed game.** The resume anchor and crash journal are voided or overwritten by the most ordinary Android flow: back out of the dugout, then the OS kills the app (H2 and its merged duplicates).
4. **Several delegation switches are broken or do nothing.**
   - Delegated recruiting, the Casual default, signs only uncontested one- and two-star recruits, so the coached program collapses (C1).
   - Delegating the portal switches off the transfer market for all 95 other programs (H1).
   - "Coaching points", "Draft conversations", "Captains", GYM RAT and the "Hitting guru" background do nothing when used.
5. **Android polish gaps that a Play reviewer or first-week player will hit.**
   - The whole league simulates on the UI thread (multi-second freezes; H4).
   - The orientation is not locked.
   - Status-bar icons are invisible when the in-app theme differs from the system theme.
   - Haptics are dead: there is no VIBRATE permission.
   - Fonts load from Google at runtime, which contradicts the privacy policy, and app start blocks on that request.
   - Store screenshots show the old UI.
   - There is no in-app privacy link.

None of these needs a redesign. Most are guards, one-line permission or config changes, or moving work
off the main thread. The **Must fix** list below is roughly two to three weeks of focused work.

### Numbers

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Specialist areas audited | 35 (26 planned + 8 "what did I miss?" gap areas + lead's own findings) |
| Findings reported by specialists | 373 |
| Refuted by adversarial verifiers (dropped, listed in Appendix C) | 7 |
| Merged as duplicates of another finding | 34 |
| **Kept** | **332** — BLOCKER 1 · CRITICAL 4 · HIGH 10 · MEDIUM 108 · LOW 174 · POLISH 35 |
| Copy changes with Current → Recommended text | 360 (Appendix A) |
| Automated-test gaps identified | 203 (Appendix B) |

Every finding was challenged by an independent verifier told to refute it. Every BLOCKER, CRITICAL and
HIGH finding was then reproduced a second time, from scratch, by a third agent that did not trust the
first two. All 15 kept findings at those severities were reproduced (or, for device-only behaviour,
confirmed in code).

### Areas inspected
Engine (schedule, standings, RPI, realignment, postseason, double elimination, game sim, pitch model,
fatigue, injuries, depth chart/AI lineups, recruiting, scouting, development, ratings, badges, traits,
morale, habits, captains, draft, portal, eligibility, redshirts, program/board/prestige/jobs, economy,
staff projects, pipelines, coaching carousel, retirement, alumni pro careers, Hall of Fame, records,
achievements, wire, inbox, God Mode); store (all ~200 actions across 10,450 lines); persistence,
codec, crash journal, migrations; navigation and the native back plugin; every screen, overlay, sheet and
dialog; CSS architecture and accessibility; all player-visible copy (UI and generated); Android shell,
manifest, billing, privacy, security; performance and bundle; code quality and the test suite.

### Areas runtime-tested
- **Headless (tsx), driving the real store actions:**
  - 25+ season careers with a save → kill → load round trip every season.
  - Schedule invariants for 34/45/56-game worlds.
  - 30+ full postseasons per specialist.
  - Hundreds of box-score invariant checks.
  - Recruiting cycles, offseason rail walk-backs and reloads at every step.
  - Job changes in every phase, and God Mode edits.
  - Balance measured over 20+ seasons and 3+ seeds.
- **Playwright on a phone-sized Chromium:**
  - Viewports: Pixel 7, 360×640, 320×568, tablet and landscape; light and dark; in-app "Larger" text; emulated Android text zoom.
  - Every tab, overlay and room, the live managed game in 2D and 3D, June and the offseason.
  - Reload-as-process-kill at about 26 UI states, back-gesture sweeps, rapid double taps.
- **Build:**
  - `npx vite build`.
  - A real Capacitor 8 debug APK built from this commit (with `tsc` bypassed) and inspected with `aapt2`.

### Areas only code-reviewed
- **Native Android only:** BackPlugin on a real device, edge-to-edge insets on Android 15/16, WebView suspend behaviour in the background, Play Billing purchase/refund flows, haptics, the system font scale at the OS level, low-memory kills.
- **WebGL context loss and an old-WebView fallback:** reasoned from Capacitor/Chromium source.

### Tests / build commands run
| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm ci` | OK (340 packages) |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | **FAIL** — `tests/interview.test.ts(96,46) TS2367` |
| `npx vitest run` (full) | **FAIL** — 118 files, 2,172 tests: 2,170 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed (`interview.test.ts`), 836 s |
| `npx vite build` | OK — JS 1,400 kB (482 kB gz), CSS 678 kB, Diamond3D chunk 912 kB, worker 103 kB |
| `npx cap add/sync android`, `capacitor-assets generate`, `./gradlew assembleDebug` | OK — `app-debug.apk` 13.2 MB, `com.playball.dynasty`, versionCode 10000, versionName 1.0.0, min 24 / target 36 |
| `aapt2 dump badging / xmltree` | permissions INTERNET, BILLING, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE; no `screenOrientation`; `allowBackup=true` |
| `npm run soak -- 30`, calibration and climb probes | ran; findings in the engine sections |
| `npm audit` | flags vite ≤ 6.4.2 (GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff, high; dev server only, Windows paths) — see the android-release LOW findings |

### Limitations of the testing environment
- **No KVM, so no Android emulator.** Nothing was run on a real Android WebView. Every Android-specific behaviour is either emulated in Chromium (viewport, touch, text zoom, reload-as-kill, `history.back` as the back gesture) or reasoned from the Capacitor and Chromium sources. **A device pass is still required** before release (see Must fix, item 14).
- **Google Fonts are blocked in the sandbox,** so screenshots use fallback fonts. That is roughly what an offline phone shows (finding M2).
- **Usage limits.** The run was interrupted by a weekly usage limit on 2 October and resumed on 6 October. Nothing was lost: every interrupted agent was re-run.
- **Process kill was emulated** as a page reload, which is what Android's renderer kill looks like to the page. It does not cover a kill landing in the middle of an IndexedDB transaction.

### 3. Recommended improvements
- **Rendering cost:** memoise the RPI on Today and the recruiting-board sort; stop kept-alive screens re-rendering on every `version` bump; stop deserialising every save just to list them (M48, M49, M50, M51).
- **Leaks and determinism:** fix the `simClient` 7 MB-per-season retention (M47); persist the player-name pool so a reload doesn't change the future (M42).
- **Bundle:** about 55% of the 678 kB stylesheet is dead (Appendix D, performance). The three.js chunk is evaluated 3 s after launch, even on 2D-field devices.
- **Code health:** split `store.ts` (10.4k lines; `rollYear` is about 780 lines) along its natural seams (season, June, winter, live game, god). Remove the 8 unreferenced source files. Collapse the duplicated mood rule (M11) and the 4-vs-5-man rotation assumptions (M12).
- **Tests:** add the invariant suites in Appendix B, starting with save round-trip at every phase, phase-gating of every mutating action, and bracket integrity across all three season lengths.

### 4. Visual / copy polish
All 360 wording changes in Appendix A (British spellings, pluralisation helpers, units, capitalisation),
plus the 35 POLISH findings: segmented-control contrast, the crash screen on the legacy skin,
destructive buttons styled as primary, a clipped stage rail on 360 dp, and the line-score dot.

### 5. Future enhancements
- Ship the held-back Scouting feature properly.
- A visible "world rules" summary in Settings.
- Save export/import (also the cure for the single-slot risk).
- A landscape/tablet layout if you decide not to lock orientation.
- Rival AI programs using major recruiting actions (M66).

## FINDINGS BY SEVERITY

IDs (B1, C1, H1, M1 …) are stable within this report and used by the Master Fix List. Each finding notes its area, how it was evidenced, the verifier verdict, and any other areas that reported the same root cause.


### BLOCKER (1)

#### B1. Release build is red at HEAD: an interview test the 21 Sep commit deliberately left out came back in eb8203b and fails typecheck and vitest

*Area: lead-findings · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes***

- **Issue:** Release build is red at HEAD: an interview test the 21 Sep commit deliberately left out came back in eb8203b and fails typecheck and vitest
- **Location:** tests/interview.test.ts:96 and :100; src/engine/interviewResult.ts; src/data/interview.ts; package.json "build"; scripts/apk.cjs:58,70
- **Problem:** `npm run build` is `tsc --noEmit && vite build`, and tsc fails on tests/interview.test.ts. scripts/apk.cjs runs `npm run build` through execFileSync, which throws on a non-zero exit, so `npm run apk` and `npm run aab` stop before Gradle runs. `npm test` / `npm run check` also exit 1 because one test in the same file fails.
- **How to reproduce:** cd /home/user/Playball && npx tsc --noEmit  -> exit 2; npx vitest run tests/interview.test.ts -> 1 failed / 15 passed. Then npx tsc --noEmit -p <scratch>/tsconfig.noint.json, which is the repo tsconfig with the three interview files excluded -> exit 0.
- **Expected behavior:** A clean checkout of the release commit passes typecheck and its own test suite, so the APK/AAB script can build.
- **Actual behavior:** tests/interview.test.ts(96,46): error TS2367: 'BadgeSource' and '"interview"' have no overlap (tsc exit 2). The vitest run fails 'the pool > votes only for badges that exist, and only interview ones' with 'bunt-down-one votes for unknown badge grinder'.
- **Root cause:** The 2 Oct overlay commit eb8203b added src/data/interview.ts (+1137 lines), src/engine/interviewResult.ts (+149) and tests/interview.test.ts (+210). These are stale files from the copy folder. The previous overlay commit c58f762 says in its message that it left them out on purpose: "Left out: ... the interview (deleted in d04347b) ... The interview test was the only failure and the only type error; without it, typecheck is clean". The current BadgeSource union has no 'interview' and the 'grinder' badge no longer exists. Only the test imports interviewResult.ts, and only interviewResult.ts and the test import data/interview.ts.
- **Recommended fix:** Delete tests/interview.test.ts, src/engine/interviewResult.ts and src/data/interview.ts, as c58f762 intended. Excluding them already makes tsc exit 0. As a guard, add a CI step (there is no .github/workflows) that runs `npm run check` on every commit.
- **Files affected:** `tests/interview.test.ts`, `src/engine/interviewResult.ts`, `src/data/interview.ts`, `package.json`, `scripts/apk.cjs`
- **Risk:** No signed release AAB/APK can be produced from the tagged commit without manually bypassing tsc. Anyone who bypasses it loses the typecheck safety net for the whole release.

### CRITICAL (4)

#### C1. Delegated recruiting ('Staff runs it', the casual default) only ever suggests and signs uncontested one- and two-star recruits, so the coached program collapses

*Area: balance-realism · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes***

- **Issue:** Delegated recruiting ('Staff runs it', the casual default) only ever suggests and signs uncontested one- and two-star recruits, so the coached program collapses
- **Location:** src/engine/staffRecruiting.ts:464-511 (suggestStaffList; pool filter `!lostCause(p, team, pitch.stars, week)` at :468-469), src/engine/recruiting.ts:1736-1744 (lostCause), src/state/store.ts:4220 and :6092 (seedRivalInterest(…, false), so the coached program is never seeded), src/state/store.ts:299-313 (suggestedStaffList), src/ui/screens/NewGame.tsx:131 (casual defaults to 'staff')
- **Problem:** Before week 1, seedRivalInterest gives the 95 rival boards two passes of interest, which together court 713-719 of the 720 prospects. Since 2026-09-30 the coached program is never seeded ('a staff works only the coach's list'). suggestStaffList, which is what 'Use these' on the Board (Board.tsx:369) and the Season plan (SeasonPlan.tsx:161) star, drops every prospect for which lostCause() is true. lostCause returns true whenever anybody else has points and the coached program has none: (best−0)/best = 1, which clears any chase cut. So in week 1 every courted prospect is struck out, and the list is the handful nobody seeded, almost all one-stars. planStaffWeek then spends the staff's week on that list. A new casual career runs recruiting this way by default (NewGame.tsx:131: `recruitBy ?? (mode === 'casual' ? 'staff' : 'me')`). This re-creates the pairing defect §78.3 fixed: lostCause assumes a board that has been seeded.
- **How to reproduce:** cd $D && npx tsx delegate-why.ts. For seeds 5000, 4242 and 12161 it takes the strongest 5★, a 3★ and a 1★ chair, casual mode with overrides {recruiting:false}, and at week 1 counts pursuable, courted and lostCause-struck prospects and the 'Use these' list. Then: SEED=5000 npx tsx delegate-week.ts (the staff list is reset to suggestedStaffList every week, BAY 5★). Then the multi-season store runs: SEED=5000 STARS=5 USER_MODE=delegate YEARS=25 npx tsx bal2.ts; SEED=27999 STARS=1 USER_MODE=delegate; SEED=20080 STARS=3 USER_MODE=delegate.
- **Expected behavior:** A delegated staff signs roughly what its tier's AI boards sign: 5★ boards sign 8 men, mostly 4-5★; 1★ boards average 5.6-7.6 men a year. §78.2 promises that the delegated handicap is only the size of the week.
- **Actual behavior:** Week 1, seed 5000, BAY (5★, prestige 78): 720 prospects pursuable, 717 already courted by a rival, 717 struck by lostCause, and 'Use these' suggests [1,1,1]. BAY signs three 1★ recruits, while the other two 5★ AI boards sign 8 each (stars 55444433 and 55554443). Across 9 chairs and 3 seeds, the week-1 suggestion was 1-8 men, all 1★ except a single 2★. Over full careers, seed 5000's PIE (5★, 78) goes 55-2 and wins the title, then 44-12 and Omaha, then signs only 1-2★ classes every winter. It falls to 10-35 by year 7 and 11-34 by year 15, its strength rank goes 1 → 80 → 70 of 96, and its prestige goes 78 → 45, which is two stars. Seed 27999's 1★ PSA signs one to eight 1-2★ men a winter for 25 seasons, never plays a regional, and sits at strength rank 74-96 throughout. Over the same span, 34% of the AI programs that started at 1★ reach 3★ (pooled-20.txt).
- **Root cause:** Three changes combine. The coached program is excluded from rival seeding (store.ts:4220, :6092: seedRivalInterest(season, userTeam, false), dated 2026-09-30). suggestStaffList's pool filter applies lostCause even when the program has no interest of its own (staffRecruiting.ts:469). lostCause (recruiting.ts:1740-1743) treats 'somebody else has points, I have none' as lost: `if (mine >= best) return false; return (best - mine) / best >= chaseCut(...)`.
- **Recommended fix:** In suggestStaffList, and anywhere else the staff list's candidates are filtered, apply lostCause only when the coached program already has its own interest (mine > 0). planStaffWeek's `givenUp` already follows that rule. Another option is to rank courted men by winScore instead of excluding them. Or restore §78's seeding for a delegated board (seedRivalInterest(season, userTeam, true, userPitch)) at start(), at the year roll and in staffTakesTheBoard. Then add a test: at week 1 a delegated 5★ program's suggestion contains 4-5★ men, and its signed class over a cycle is within about two men of its tier's AI mean. *(Verifier's note: Root cause as stated. Smallest fix: in suggestStaffList (and staffReplacement's lost-cause steps), apply lostCause only when (p.points[team] ?? 0) > 0, matching givenUp. Rewrite season-plan-fixes' five-star test to read suggestedStaffList from a store career after start(), when seedRivalInterest has already run, rather than from a bare createSeason.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/staffRecruiting.ts`, `src/engine/recruiting.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Board.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/SeasonPlan.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/NewGame.tsx`
- **Risk:** By default every casual career, and any delegated full career, sees the coached program decay to the cellar within about five seasons, whatever it started as. A 5★ job turns into a 1★ roster while rival 5★ programs hold their tier.
- **Lead auditor's note:** Raised to CRITICAL: delegated recruiting is the default for Casual careers, so a large share of players see their program collapse without having done anything wrong.

#### C2. A god move or cut of a transfer-portal player leaves him in the portal pool, and at portal close another program signs him: the same player ends up on two rosters for good (a cut man comes back to life)

*Area: god-mode · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes***

- **Issue:** A god move or cut of a transfer-portal player leaves him in the portal pool, and at portal close another program signs him: the same player ends up on two rosters for good (a cut man comes back to life)
- **Location:** src/engine/godMode.ts:316-345 movePlayer/cutPlayer; src/state/store.ts:9567-9583 godMovePlayer/godCutPlayer; src/state/store.ts:3422-3490 closePortal (releaseFrom(season.teams[m.from]) at 3469/3486); also store.ts:9585 godSignPortal -> godMode.ts:348 signPortalMan
- **Problem:** During the offseason portal step, the store's `portal` object lists men by reference with their original `from` program (portal.available = rivals' transfers, portal.leaving = your own). godMovePlayer/godCutPlayer change rosters but never touch `portal` and never clear the man's `inPortal` flag. When the step closes, closePortal still treats every listed man as in the pool: it runs releaseFrom on `m.from`, which does nothing because he is no longer there, and staffWorksPortal then signs him onto a rival. So a man you moved now plays for two programs, and a man you cut ('Cut, he leaves the world') is signed by a rival. Moving a portal player onto your own program, the obvious god-mode way to take him, creates the duplicate. The duplicates survive the year roll and a save/reload: assertSeason only checks for repeats inside one team's unit.
- **How to reproduce:** Script: scratchpad/agents/god-mode/p4b-portal.ts (run `npx tsx --import ./register-window.mjs p4b-portal.ts` in that dir). It starts a sandbox career (seed 31337, team 7), sims the season and June through the store, then steps the rail to 'portal'. Using the store calls the Player editor's Move/Cut buttons make: (A) godMovePlayer moves a rival's portal arm to a third program; (B) godMovePlayer moves another portal arm to MY program; (C) godCutPlayer cuts a third portal arm; (L) godMovePlayer sends one of my own leavers elsewhere. Then nextPhase('portal'), the step through signing, the year roll, and a reload.
- **Expected behavior:** After a god move a man is on exactly one roster and out of the portal. A god cut removes him from the world for good. Closing the portal never signs a man who has already left the pool.
- **Actual behavior:** p4b-portal.log: 'A Cole Hatteras now on [DLT, JAX]', 'B Wyatt Pena now on [BIL (mine), SEL]', 'C Efrain Hollingshead (cut) now on [ATF]', 'L Angelo Carnahan now on [VER, MOJ]'. 'men on two rosters in the new season: p0d0nnd5:DLT+JAX, p05il7gw:BIL+SEL, p15loww8:VER+MOJ'. After reload: the same three duplicates.
- **Root cause:** The god roster actions mutate team arrays only. Portal membership lives in the store's `portal` (available/leaving lists of PortalMan with a stale `from`) plus the player's `inPortal` flag, and neither is updated. closePortal (store.ts:3432-3488) and signPortalMan (godMode.ts:354-356) both assume the man is still on season.teams[m.from]. releaseFrom is a silent no-op when he is not, and signFromPortal pushes him onto the new team regardless.
- **Recommended fix:** In godMovePlayer/godCutPlayer (and godTwoWay), when get().portal is set, remove the man from portal.available and portal.leaving, delete `inPortal`, and set the trimmed portal back into the store. Make closePortal and signPortalMan defensive as well: release the man from whichever team findPlayer() finds him on, and skip any entry whose player is no longer on season.teams[m.from]. Add a store invariant check (each player id on at most one team) to the god actions and to loadSlot. *(Verifier's note: godSignPortal has the same flaw when the man was already moved: signPortalMan's releaseFrom(m.from) does nothing and signFromPortal adds a second copy. The simplest robust fix: closePortal and signPortalMan should skip any PortalMan whose player is no longer on season.teams[m.from] (check with findPlayer), and godMovePlayer/godCutPlayer should prune get().portal.available/leaving and delete inPortal.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/godMode.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/portal.ts`
- **Risk:** A sandbox career is permanently corrupted: the same player bats or pitches for two programs, his stats merge under one id, and an edit to him changes both teams. 'Move him to my program' during the portal step, the most natural god action there, triggers it. Nothing on screen reveals it and nothing repairs it.

#### C3. God mode can leave a team with no starting pitcher (a two-way man as the last starter, then toggled off, cut or moved): every day sim then throws, and the autosaved career is refused on load

*Area: god-mode · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes**; also reported by store-flow-C*

- **Issue:** God mode can leave a team with no starting pitcher (a two-way man as the last starter, then toggled off, cut or moved): every day sim then throws, and the autosaved career is refused on load
- **Location:** src/engine/godMode.ts:410-417 unmakeTwoWay; godMode.ts:321-322 and 337-338 (two-way man checked with canLeave, not canLeaveArm); store.ts:9649 godTwoWay, 9567 godMovePlayer, 9576 godCutPlayer; crash at engine/game.ts:366-367; load refusal at store.ts:2329 assertSeason
- **Problem:** canLeaveArm keeps the rotation non-empty only for pure pitchers. A two-way bat in the pen counts as 'a man in the pen', so the last real starter may be cut or moved, and fillRotation promotes the two-way man to be the only starter. After that, three god actions each empty the rotation: (1) Two-way player toggle off, because unmakeTwoWay filters him out of the rotation with no guard and no fillRotation; (2) Cut him and (3) Move him, because movePlayer/cutPlayer treat him as a hitter (`type !== 'pitcher'`) and apply canLeave (lineup rule) instead of canLeaveArm. Each action autosaves.
- **How to reproduce:** scratchpad/agents/god-mode/p6-norotation.ts (also p2-adversarial.ts). In a sandbox career (seed 777, team 3): Player editor > Status > Two-way player ON for a bench hitter. Player editor > Move > 'Cut him' (two taps) for each of the 10 pure pitchers; every cut is accepted. Then either Two-way OFF for that man, or Cut him, or Move him. Then press Play (advanceDay), then reload the career.
- **Expected behavior:** The last starting pitcher cannot leave (the edit refuses and says why, as it already does for hitters), so the world always has a playable rotation.
- **Actual behavior:** All three variants: final edit -> true. 'advanceDay threw: "Thibodaux State Herons has no starting pitcher"; results 48 -> 51 -> 54 (dayIndex stuck at 3)': every retry plays and records the same earlier games of that day again. 'reload: ok=false loadError="Thibodaux State has no starting pitcher." needsTeam=true'. The career cannot be opened again.
- **Root cause:** unmakeTwoWay (godMode.ts:412-413) removes him from rotation and bullpen without checking that the rotation stays non-empty. movePlayer/cutPlayer branch on `found.player.type !== 'pitcher'` (godMode.ts:321, 337), so a two-way rotation arm only gets the lineup check. createGame throws on an empty rotation (game.ts:367), and assertSeason refuses any in-play save without one (store.ts:2329).
- **Recommended fix:** In movePlayer/cutPlayer run canLeaveArm whenever the man is in the rotation or pen (isTwoWay included), not only for type 'pitcher'. Make unmakeTwoWay refuse, or call fillRotation and refuse if it stays empty, when he is the last rotation arm. In the store god actions, validate the edited team (lineup >= 9, rotation >= 1 while the season is in play) before saving and roll back with an editor note if not. Also wrap simNextDay in advanceDay/simWeek so a throw does not leave a half-recorded day. *(Verifier's note: Guard by station, not by type: in movePlayer, cutPlayer and unmakeTwoWay, run canLeaveArm whenever the man is in the rotation, and make canLeaveArm count only men who will remain arms (exclude the leaving man, and for unmakeTwoWay exclude him from the pen too). The half-recorded day on a throw (results growing on each retry) is a separate store issue: simNextDay should be atomic, or advanceDay should catch the throw and roll back.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/godMode.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/game.ts`
- **Risk:** A paid sandbox career becomes permanently unloadable through ordinary editor taps. Before the reload, every retry duplicates the results already played that day.

#### C4. Taking a job offer while a managed game waits, or during the winter, corrupts the season: the game is recorded twice, the new team loses a game, and the old school's draftee joins the new roster

*Area: store-flow-A · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes**; also reported by career-program, store-flow-B*

- **Issue:** Taking a job offer while a managed game waits, or during the winter, corrupts the season: the game is recorded twice, the new team loses a game, and the old school's draftee joins the new roster
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:7095-7199 acceptOffer (no live/phase/busy guard); store.ts:8715 endManagedGame `simNextDay(season, { hold: userTeam })`; store.ts:4969-4977 keepPlayer `reinstate(season.teams[userTeam].team, …)`; UI: Program.tsx:368-374 BoardRoom callout 'N programs want to talk' -> JobMarket.tsx:126-132 'Take the X job' / 'Tap again'
- **Problem:** Offers posted at the year roll (from schools the coach approached or job-watched) stay on the desk for the whole next season and the whole next winter. acceptOffer only checks that the offer is on the table. It can be confirmed while a regular-season managed game is waiting (Android back during a game = leaveGame, nav.ts:53, which keeps `live`) or on any offseason step. It swaps `userTeam` mid-flow, and the code that finishes that flow then uses the new chair.
- **How to reproduce:** UI (Playwright, pixel7, dev server): seed 4242, team 5, full mode. In year 1, approach the 3 weakest schools and watch 6 more jobs, then finish the year (store fast-forward) -> year 2 opens with 6 offers. Then, by DOM: Today 'Play ball' -> Android back (page.goBack) -> Office tab -> Board -> '6 programs want to talk' -> 'Take the Rawlins job' -> 'Tap again' -> Today 'Back to game' -> finish the game (autoFinish + endManagedGame, the dugout's own calls). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Playball/f986342b-e697-5fb0-a121-7921d265dffe/scratchpad/agents/store-flow-A/pw-accept-midgame.cjs. Store-level equivalents: t-accept-midgame.ts and t-accept-offseason.ts (draft step: accept the offer, then keepPlayer the cheapest case) in the same dir.
- **Expected behavior:** Accepting is refused (or deferred) while a game, bracket or offseason step still belongs to the old chair. Failing that, the managed game is recorded once and the new team's own fixture that day is played.
- **Actual behavior:** UI run: day-1 fixture (home 5 vs away 90) is in season.results twice ['4-10','5-16'], and the new team's own fixture that day has 0 results. Store run: the same fixture is recorded as '0-10' and '4-6'; after day 1 the old team shows 2 games played and the new team 0. Offseason run: after accepting on the draft step, keeping the old school's draftee Wander Shipley ('role' case, 22 points) leaves him with outcome 'stayed' on the NEW team's roster (onNew true, onOld false): a free cross-program transfer.
- **Root cause:** acceptOffer (store.ts:7095) has no guard for live, liveStarting, pendingGame, busy, bracket/myBracket or phase !== null. endManagedGame holds out the CURRENT userTeam (store.ts:8715) rather than the team that played the managed game, so simNextDay simulates the managed fixture and then recordResult (8717) records it again, while the new chair's fixture is skipped for good. keepPlayer reinstates into season.teams[get().userTeam] (4969-4977) whoever's draft board it is.
- **Recommended fix:** In acceptOffer, return early (and disable 'Take the job' with a reason in JobMarket/BoardRoom) when `live || liveStarting || pendingGame || busy || bracket || myBracket || phase !== null`. Alternatively, let a winter acceptance record a pending move and apply it in rollYear. Separately harden endManagedGame: `const managed = live.managing === 'home' ? liveMeta.home : liveMeta.away; simNextDay(season, { hold: managed })`. keepPlayer/keepFromPortal/closePortal should act on the program that owns the board or portal, not on get().userTeam.
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/JobMarket.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Program.tsx`, `src/state/nav.ts`
- **Risk:** Permanent, saved corruption of standings, RPI, conference seeding and records: one program gets an extra game, two get one fewer. Rosters get cross-program moves. Reachable from the most common Android gesture during a game, and in the winter (the natural time to change jobs) by anyone holding offers.

### HIGH (10)

#### H1. Delegating the coach's own transfer portal switches off the transfer market for the other 95 programs

*Area: balance-realism · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes**; also reported by roster-lifecycle*

- **Issue:** Delegating the coach's own transfer portal switches off the transfer market for the other 95 programs
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:5192-5216 (nextPhase, draft→portal, delegated branch: `set({ portal: { leaving: mine, available: [], spent: 0 } })` at :5213) and src/state/store.ts:3422-3497 (closePortal; pool built at :3451-3454)
- **Problem:** When the coach does not run the portal (casual mode by preset, since `portal` is `casual: false` in depth.ts, or a full career with 'The transfer portal' switched off in Settings), the draft→portal step lets the coach's staff sign from `theirs`. It then stores `available: []`, which throws away every other program's entrant. closePortal() builds both the pool the other 95 staffs shop from and the list of unsigned men it releases from `portal.available` plus `portal.leaving` only. So in a delegated career, every rival entrant the coach's own staff did not sign is never offered to anyone and never leaves. He stays on the roster he asked to leave, and his `inPortal: true` flag is never cleared, so the flags pile up year after year. The comment above the branch says the opposite should happen: 'In casual the staff works it… the men still leave, the pool still exists, and somebody competent still shops it' (store.ts:5131-5133).
- **How to reproduce:** cd $D (= /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Playball/f986342b-e697-5fb0-a121-7921d265dffe/scratchpad/agents/balance-realism) && SEED=4242 YEARS=2 npx tsx portal-ab.ts. The script runs the same seed and chair (VER) in casual mode twice. Run A uses the default depth, so the portal is delegated. Run B adds overrides {portal:true}, so the coach works the portal and signs nobody. Each year it plays the season (playSeason), June (playPostseason + simBracket/advanceBracket) and the offseason rail (nextPhase). Across all 96 rosters it counts inPortal flags after the portal opens, men who change program between the draft step and signing day, and men who disappear (left college baseball).
- **Expected behavior:** The 95 rival staffs shop the national pool and the unsigned men leave, whoever works the coached program's own portal. Run B shows this: 75 entrants → 74 moved, 1 left, 0 flags remaining (2027); 50 → 49 moved, 1 left (2028).
- **Actual behavior:** Run A: 74 entrants in 2027 → 2 moved (both signed by the coached program's own staff), 0 left, and 73 inPortal flags still on 52 rosters at signing day. 2028: 117 flags (69 left over from the year before plus the new ones), 1 moved, 0 left. All my casual-mode multi-season runs show 1-6 portal moves a year for the whole country. A rival man named in a 'Word is X wants out' wire rumour (store.ts:5180) stays at his school unless the coached program's own staff happens to sign him.
- **Root cause:** The delegated branch writes `available: []` (store.ts:5213) so that Portal.tsx shows the 'Your staff is working it' empty state (Portal.tsx:124-129). But `available` is also the remaining national pool that closePortal reads (store.ts:3451-3454). The delegated path therefore deletes the pool before the other 95 programs ever see it. The non-delegated branch (:5215) and the old-save fallback (:10287) keep `theirs`.
- **Recommended fix:** Keep the unsigned remainder. In the delegated branch, store `available: theirs.filter((m) => !took.includes(m))`. Make Portal.tsx choose the 'Your staff is working it' state from `!runsPortal` rather than from an empty list, and make takeFromPortal/keepFromPortal refuse when !handles(depth,'portal'). Alternatively, give PortalPool a dedicated `pool` field that closePortal reads in both branches. Also clear `inPortal` on anyone who stays, and add a casual/delegated variant of release-audit.test.ts's 'an unsigned portal man has left college baseball'. *(Verifier's note: Fix as proposed: keep `available: theirs.filter(m => !took.includes(m))` in the delegated branch, choose Portal.tsx's 'staff is working it' state from !handles(depth,'portal') instead of an empty list, and add a casual/delegated variant of release-audit's 'unsigned portal man has left college baseball' test. The old-save fallback at store.ts:10287 keeps `theirs` and is not affected.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Portal.tsx`, `tests/release-audit.test.ts`
- **Risk:** In every casual career, and in any full career that hands the portal to the staff, about 50-75 transfers a year never happen among the 95 rival programs. Buried and unhappy men stay on deep rosters, so talent stays concentrated, and the portal rumours mislead the player.

#### H2. Leaving the dugout with "Back to Today (the game waits)" voids the crash journal, so the game is silently lost if Android then kills the app

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes**; also reported by persistence, store-flow-A, store-flow-C, ui-home-live-game*

- **Issue:** Leaving the dugout with "Back to Today (the game waits)" voids the crash journal, so the game is silently lost if Android then kills the app
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx:698 (Back to Today button calls saveNow); src/state/store.ts saveNow (~9824) persists season.rng.state(); store.ts pendingFromJournal (~2498-2506) and resumeGame (~8290) compare it with journal.rngState via liveJournal.ts journalMatches
- **Problem:** The resume journal is anchored on the season generator's position at the first pitch, and it only counts as valid if the saved season's rng state still equals that anchor. A managed game draws from season.rng. So any save written mid-game stores the advanced rng position, and on the next load journalMatches fails and the journal is cleared. The dugout's own way out, "Back to Today (the game waits)", calls saveNow() every time. So do other mid-game actions that save: strategy changes, lineup swaps, recruiting moves.
- **How to reproduce:** Playwright (real UI, dev server): agents/game-sim/ui_backtotoday.cjs. Career seed 4242, team 3 (Thibodaux State). Start the next managed game, tap 4 calls, then Dugout -> "Back to Today (the game waits)". page.reload() emulates the OS killing and restoring the app; then tap Continue. Control run: the same steps but reload without leaving the dugout. Headless: agents/game-sim/resume.ts scenario B (setStrategy or swapStarter mid-game -> loadSlot).
- **Expected behavior:** After the kill, the Today screen offers "You left a game on the field / Pick it up", and the replay lands on the same inning (this is what happens when you reload without leaving the dugout).
- **Actual behavior:** Control run: pendingGame={home:3,away:87}, journal present, 'Pick it up' on screen (shots/control-after-reload.png). After Back to Today: pendingGame=null, the journal is deleted, nothing is offered, dayIndex 0, gp 0 (shots/backtotoday-after-reload.png shows only the Season plan sheet). The game is gone. The day will be replayed from the advanced generator, so it becomes a different game, which also lets a losing game be re-rolled. Headless B: setStrategy mid-game showed journal anchor 3953022083 vs saved rng 1526171156 -> pendingGame=false, journal=false.
- **Root cause:** saveNow serialises season.rng.state() whatever is happening. During a live game that state has moved past the anchor, and pendingFromJournal/resumeGame treat any mismatch as a stale journal and clear it. Manage.tsx:698 saves on purpose when the coach leaves the dugout, which is exactly the moment Android is most likely to kill the backgrounded app.
- **Recommended fix:** While get().live is set and not over, have saveNow write the journal's anchor rngState (readJournal()?.rngState) instead of season.rng.state(). The live game mutates nothing else in the season; TeamState copies its inputs. Remove the saveNow() from the Back to Today button, since the anchor save already exists. Block actions that consume season.rng during a live game (recruitMajor's sway calls swayRecruit with season.rng), or give them a derived generator, so a replay cannot diverge. Add a store test: start managed game -> calls -> setStrategy -> reload -> pendingGame must be offered. *(Verifier's note: Simplest safe fix: drop saveNow() from the Back to Today handler (the anchor save already exists). In saveNow, while get().live && !get().live.over, either skip the write or serialise readJournal()?.rngState in place of season.rng.state(). grep found no season mutations inside game.ts or liveGame.ts, so persisting the anchor should replay cleanly. Add a store test: startManagedGame -> calls -> saveNow -> loadSlot -> pendingGame !== null. Repro: verify-game-sim/v0.ts.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/state/liveJournal.ts`
- **Risk:** Players who step out of a game (the UI invites it with "the game waits") lose the game whenever Android kills the app. This is the scenario the journal was built for (its header calls a lost backgrounded game the most player-hostile behaviour in the app). It also enables save-scumming a game you are losing.

#### H3. A Leagues 'Membership' trade made after the regular season says 'Takes effect next spring' but lands at once: it rewrites this June's conference fields and standings and, after a reload, the schedule already played (works mid-June too)

*Area: god-mode · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes**; also reported by schedule-standings*

- **Issue:** A Leagues 'Membership' trade made after the regular season says 'Takes effect next spring' but lands at once: it rewrites this June's conference fields and standings and, after a reload, the schedule already played (works mid-June too)
- **Location:** src/engine/godMode.ts:184-206 conferenceWindow/swapConferences ('next-spring' branch); src/ui/god/LeaguesEditor.tsx:221-224 and 272-274; src/state/seasonCodec.ts fromPortable (schedule rebuilt from worldFromTeams)
- **Problem:** In the 'next-spring' window (season complete: the whole of June and the offseason) swapConferences calls applyRealignment right away and only skips the schedule rebuild. The traded programs change conference at once. The conference tournament fields and standings for the season just played regroup, a program keeps the conference record it earned in its old league, and because a save rebuilds the schedule from the teams' current conferences, every reload rewrites the fixtures already played. The trade is also accepted with the conference cups already in progress. This overlaps the schedule-standings agent's probes (their god-swap-nextspring.ts); the evidence here is reproduced independently, and mid-June is added.
- **How to reproduce:** 1) scratchpad/agents/god-mode/p10-swap-nextspring.ts (a copy of the schedule-standings probe): seed 4242, regular season simmed, godSwapConferences(PSC, TAM), then a save/load round trip. 2) scratchpad/agents/god-mode/p7-midpost.ts: seed 8080, team 12; playPostseason (bracket stage 'conference', my conference cup live), then godSwapConferences(my team, the top of another league).
- **Expected behavior:** As the editor says: the trade takes effect next spring. This June's fields, standings, records and the played schedule stay as they were.
- **Actual behavior:** p10 log: 'GULF tournament field AFTER swap : BAY DLT MOB THB LKC BIL GLP ATF' (PSC removed, ATF added); 'TAM now in GULF; its conference record 27-6 was earned against ATL'; 'after reload, 22 of 45 of the user's PLAYED fixtures show a different opponent'; 'Schedule screen after reload: 22 result rows labelled with the wrong opponent'; 'whole league after reload: 505 scheduled (already-played) fixtures have no matching result'. p7 log: 'June open: stage conference myBracket conference ... trade PIE (ATL) <-> BAY (GULF) mid-June -> true'.
- **Root cause:** conferenceWindow returns 'next-spring' for any complete season and swapConferences applies the realignment immediately (godMode.ts:201). The deferral exists only in the UI copy. fromPortable then rebuilds the finished season's schedule from the new membership.
- **Recommended fix:** In the 'next-spring' window, store a pending trade (e.g. season.pendingRealignment) and apply it in nextSeason/rollYear, the way the world's own realignment does. Or close the window between the first pitch and the year roll. Do not rebuild a complete season's schedule from current membership on load: persist the schedule, or the conference map it was built from.
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/godMode.ts`, `src/ui/god/LeaguesEditor.tsx`, `src/state/seasonCodec.ts`
- **Risk:** One tap corrupts the finished season's tables, fields and schedule history in a sandbox career, and the damage spreads on every reload.

#### H4. SIM WEEK, SIM GAME, the year roll and the June stage presses run the whole league's simulation on the UI thread. The sim worker is wired only to a God Mode button.

*Area: performance · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** SIM WEEK, SIM GAME, the year roll and the June stage presses run the whole league's simulation on the UI thread. The sim worker is wired only to a God Mode button.
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:8948-9006 simWeek, 5382-5407 advanceDay, nextPhase('signing')→rollYear, 7377 playPostseason, 7681 advanceBracket; src/ui/screens/Today.tsx:412-446 (buttons); only worker caller: src/ui/god/TimeEditor.tsx:52 and App.tsx:901 (simError retry)
- **Problem:** The two season buttons a normal player has on Today are 'Sim game'/'Next day' (advanceDay) and 'Sim week' (simWeek). Both call simNextDay synchronously on the main thread for every one of the 96 programs: about 48 games a day and roughly 190 games per SIM WEEK. The same is true of the offseason year roll, the June 'Play the tournaments' and 'POSTSEASON' presses, and the start of a new career. The comlink worker (simWorker.ts) is only reached through playSeason, and nothing calls that outside God Mode's 'Sim the season' and the sim-error retry bar. The docs say these sims take milliseconds (05 §103, Today.tsx:112, simWorker.ts:4). They do not.
- **How to reproduce:** Headless: node --import ./register.mjs --import tsx weekcpu.ts casual week (in the performance agent's headless/ dir). This plays a whole season with SIM WEEK and reads main-thread CPU from /proc for each press. Browser: serve the store-exposed production build (probuild/vite.config.mjs on :5199), then run NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node pw/simweek2.cjs http://127.0.0.1:5199/ 1,4 casual 5. It starts seed 4242 at team 7 and times store.simWeek(), the exact function the button's 800 ms timer calls, from call to painted frame, including long tasks.
- **Expected behavior:** A SIM WEEK or SIM GAME press keeps the UI responsive. A whole season is documented as 'a few hundred milliseconds on a desktop', and 05 §103 says 'The sim runs after the ring, in milliseconds'.
- **Actual behavior:** Main-thread CPU per SIM WEEK on this server core: 480–600 ms (mean 524 ms, 6.3 s per season). In a 3-season run the mean was 770 ms and the max 1,420 ms. SIM GAME is 80–200 ms per press (mean 123 ms). The year roll (nextPhase 'signing') averages 783 ms (max 930). Conference-stage advanceBracket peaks at 560 ms and playPostseason at 490 ms. In the production React build in Chromium, one SIM WEEK is a single long task of 1.6–3.0 s at CPU 1x and 1.9–4.1 s at 4x throttle. Over 10 in-browser seasons, winter long tasks reached 2.4–2.5 s (the roll) and June long tasks 1.1–1.7 s. The worker's own CPU for one season is 5.1–5.4 s, against the documented 'few hundred milliseconds'. On a mid-range Android phone (2–4x slower) each SIM WEEK freezes taps and animation for roughly 1.5–3 s.
- **Root cause:** simWeek loops simNextDay(season) up to 10 times synchronously (store.ts:8982-8993), then runs syncRecruitingCalendar, noteSeasonNews and saveNow in the same task. advanceDay and rollYear work the same way. The CPU profile (profweek.ts → cpuprof.cjs) puts 85% of simWeek in simNextDay→playGame→simGame. depthChart chartFor/coverFor take about 21% of the sim, saveDynasty 7% and recruiting AI 6%. simWorker.ts has only a whole-season API, so no per-week or per-day work can be sent off-thread.
- **Recommended fix:** 1. Add simDays(portable, untilWeek|days) and rollYear-sized entry points to simWorker.ts and route simWeek, advanceDay, rollYear and the June stage sims through simSeasonInWorker-style calls with busy=true. Keep the roster-alert and injury-stop logic by having the worker stop at the first day that changes the user's walking-wounded set and return that day. 2. Move the recruiting-week close (syncRecruitingCalendar/advanceRecruitingWeek) into the worker as well, so the landing does not replay 12 weeks on the main thread. 3. As a stopgap, chunk the week per day with a yield between days (await scheduler.yield() or setTimeout 0) and keep the buttons disabled until it finishes. 4. Fix the chartFor hot spot (separate finding) for about 20% less CPU. 5. Correct 05 §103 and the simWorker.ts header. *(Verifier's note: Worst case is the year roll. rollYear sets busy:true and then runs fully synchronously with no yield, so the busy state never paints. On a phone that is several seconds of frozen UI with no new feedback, once a year. For the stopgap (yield between days), simWeek and advanceDay must also set busy, or the buttons must be disabled for the whole run. They do not set busy today, so a yield would let a queued tap start a second sim mid-week.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Today.tsx`, `src/state/simClient.ts`, `src/state/simWorker.ts`, `src/engine/season.ts`, `docs/05-systems-reference.md`
- **Risk:** On target phones every SIM WEEK, year roll and June stage freezes the app for seconds, with no feedback beyond a spinner that stopped updating. Players read it as a hang, and queued taps fire afterwards (see the double-tap finding). This is the core loop of the game.
- **Lead auditor's note:** Kept HIGH (verifier suggested MEDIUM): multi-second UI freezes on every SIM WEEK / June press on mid-range phones are the first thing a player feels, and they cause the double-tap bugs below.

#### H5. June played through the store ignores the same-night calendar and stage breaks: the postseason runs into August and pitcher rest depends on simulation order

*Area: postseason · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes***

- **Issue:** June played through the store ignores the same-night calendar and stage breaks: the postseason runs into August and pitcher rest depends on simulation order
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts openStage (conference 7446-7473, esp. 7452-7454; regional 7475-7524, esp. 7485-7495), openNationalStep (7570-7612), simBracket both() 7912 + stepSideShow 7659-7678 + closeMyBracket 8206-8211; engine helpers src/engine/postseason.ts afterTheBreak/onTheSameNights 611-626 (module-private, unused by the store)
- **Problem:** The engine stage functions (allConferenceTournaments, stageRegionals, stageNational) open every tournament of a stage on the same night and put STAGE_BREAK=5 days between stages. That is the fix documented in docs/05 §69.1/§113. The store is the only path a real career uses, and it re-implements the stages without any of that whenever the user is in a stage. (1) openStage plays the other seven conference tournaments with a plain `.map(conferenceTournament)`, so each starts where the previous one finished, and the user's double elimination only starts after them. (2) The regional stage plays the other fifteen series one after another via singleElimination, with no afterTheBreak, and the user's series comes last. (3) openNationalStep never applies afterTheBreak, and a spectator gets the two halves back to back (runDoubleElim A, then B). (4) When the user is in a half, each night is two stepDoubleElim calls (his half, then the side show), and each call advances the shared clock, so the national calendar runs two days per night.
- **How to reproduce:** cd scratchpad/agents/postseason; SEED=4242 TEAM=strong npx tsx --import ./register.mjs storeflow.ts. The script drives start → simSeason → playPostseason → simBracket/advanceBracket the way the June buttons do, and calls openStage() after every action like Postseason.tsx's effect; read the 'calendar' block. For the visible symptom, run `NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node pw-june.cjs` (Pixel 7, Bayou State, seed 4242): Today ▸ Postseason, sim through June, then on the Bracket tab tap 'Game 1' of the national championship. For the rest effect: SEED=101 npx tsx --import ./register.mjs rest.ts.
- **Expected behavior:** The same calendar as the engine path and tests/audit-followups.test.ts. All eight cups open on firstPostseasonDay, all sixteen regionals open on one night at least 5 days after the last cup game, and the national halves share nights at least 5 days after the last regional. engine-soak.ts (30 postseasons, all three lengths) shows June spans of 27-30 days with 0 calendar violations.
- **Actual behavior:** Store path with the user in the conference field (19 of 36 batch1 runs): cups ATL:81-86, PAC:87-92 … GULF (user):123-128; regionals 129-130, 131-132 … 163-164 (user's last); national A 165-180, B 165-179; final 181-182. Both breaks (conference→regional, regional→national) are 1 day, and June spans 76-110 days, ending between Jul 8 and Aug 11. Spectator runs end May 23-25. On the June screen the national final's box score reads 'Tuesday, August 3' under the header '2027 postseason · In June'. Spectators also get a 1-day regional→national break, with the halves played back to back (A 96-103, B 104-110). Rest effect at SEED=101: 'GULF #2 v ATL #3 day 132: rest 1/47 starters slot 3/0'. The first regional opened the day after one team's conference final, so it started its #4 starter while its opponent had 47 days off. The user's own regional opened on day 169 with 38 days' rest. SEED=4243 shows the same (GULF #1: rest 1 vs 47, #4 starter).
- **Root cause:** store.ts:7452-7454 runs `conferenceIds(season).filter((id) => id !== me.conference).map((id) => conferenceTournament(season, id))`; each runDoubleElim advances season.postseasonDay from wherever the last one stopped, and startDoubleElim(season, mine.field) at 7459 inherits the end of that chain. store.ts:7485-7495 builds the other regionals with singleElimination per pairing, with no afterTheBreak and no shared opening night. openNationalStep (7586-7612) never calls afterTheBreak; for spectators it runs runDoubleElim(bracketA) and then runDoubleElim(bracketB) in sequence. In lockstep (both() at 7912, stepSideShow at 7662, the run-out at 8209) every stepDoubleElim calls advancePostseasonDay. audit-followups.test.ts only exercises the engine functions, so this regression has no test.
- **Recommended fix:** Export a scheduler from postseason.ts: onTheSameNights plus a `stageOpen(season, {afterBreak})` helper. In openStage: apply afterTheBreak for the regional and national stages and record `open = currentDay(season)`. Run the other tournaments with season.postseasonDay reset to `open` before each, keeping `othersLast = max(...)`. Then set season.postseasonDay = open before startDoubleElim/startSeriesBracket for the user, so his first game is on the stage's opening night. In closeMyBracket (and the no-user-bracket path), set season.postseasonDay = max(othersLast, currentDay(season)). National stage: the spectator path should use stageNational's logic (afterTheBreak, then both halves via onTheSameNights). For lockstep, capture the day before stepping the user's half, rewind to it before stepSideShow, and keep the max afterwards. Add a store-level test (user in the field, and a spectator) asserting equal opening nights, gaps ≥ STAGE_BREAK and a June span under 45 days. *(Verifier's note: Scope: the spectator conference and regional paths are fine, because stageConferenceTournaments and stageRegionals already apply onTheSameNights and the break. In my SEED=101 long run the user missed the regionals and all 16 opened on day 139 after a 6-day break. The defect is limited to (a) any stage where the user has his own tournament and (b) the national stage in every case: no break, and spectator halves back to back. The pitching bias is modest in aggregate: 31 of 32 regional openers were still started by a top-two arm, against 32 of 32 on the engine path. The heavier effects are July/August dates under the 'In June' header, an injury clock that runs about 100 ticks instead of about 30, and a 1-day regional→national break. That break lands on the user's own team, because his regional is always simulated last.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/postseason.ts`, `src/engine/doubleElim.ts`, `tests/audit-followups.test.ts`
- **Risk:** Most seasons where the coached team reaches a stage play a different and biased postseason. Teams simulated first play on short rest, while the coached team and late-order teams play fully rested, which moves results, titles and prestige across the whole world. Box scores and game logs show July/August dates, and the June injury clock runs about 100 ticks instead of about 30. The documented §69.1/§113 fix is effectively not shipped for players.

#### H6. Programs with a full class keep recruiting, and their points count as the lead everyone else must beat, so about 70 prospects a year go unsigned and the coach's Ask to commit is refused

*Area: recruiting · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes***

- **Issue:** Programs with a full class keep recruiting, and their points count as the lead everyone else must beat, so about 70 prospects a year go unsigned and the coach's Ask to commit is refused
- **Location:** src/engine/recruiting.ts:2255-2262 leadersAtWeekStart; :1736-1744 lostCause; :1752-1759 winScore; :2095-2111 askBlocked (best of all other teams); src/state/store.ts:4812-4849 advanceRecruitingWeek (no full-class check before aiTargets/planAiRecruitActions); src/ui/screens/recruitRace.ts:101 raceOf, :136 standing; src/engine/staffRecruiting.ts:249 givenUp, :328 staffReplacement, :464 suggestStaffList
- **Problem:** closeWeek correctly skips programs that already have 8 commits (`inTheRunning`, recruiting.ts:2190). Nothing else does. In advanceRecruitingWeek every AI program runs aiTargets and planAiRecruitActions every week, whether or not its class is full. Every 'who leads him' reading uses the max over ALL programs' points: leadersAtWeekStart, lostCause, winScore, askBlocked, raceOf/standing on the board, and the staff's givenUp/suggestion/replacement logic. A program that filled its class in week 5 keeps adding about 40 interest a week to men it can never sign. Every program that can still sign then treats those men as a 'lost cause' and stops working them. At the final week the best suitor with room has less than 60% of his price, so the man signs with nobody. The coach is told 'Somebody else is ahead of you. Take the lead first.' about a school with no scholarship to offer.
- **How to reproduce:** cd scratchpad/agents/recruiting && npx tsx r10.ts (store-driven season) ; npx tsx r11.ts (same store weekly loop run twice per seed: as shipped vs leader snapshot ignoring full programs) ; npx tsx r12.ts (coach ask vs full-program leader)
- **Expected behavior:** A program with no scholarship left stops spending and is ignored when deciding who leads a recruit. Open men flow to programs with room, and the coach can ask a man he leads among programs that can still sign him.
- **Actual behavior:** r10 (seed 4242): from week 4, 4-32 full programs a week still banked interest (8,848 total). All 74 unsigned prospects at the close were 'led' by a full program, 10 of them 4/5-star. r11 (seeds 4242/777/9001): as shipped, 638/648/643 signed, 82/72/77 unsigned, 52/52/45 programs short of 8. With the snapshot ignoring full programs: 714/713/705 signed, 6/7/15 unsigned, 20/21/26 short. r12 at week 8: 42 programs full, and 73 of the 95 open men in reach were led by a full program. A 3-star where the coach had 16.3 interest (price 10.8, nobody with room on him) was refused: askBlocked -> "Somebody else is ahead of you. Take the lead first.", recruitMajor(ask) -> false.
- **Root cause:** The 'has room' rule lives only in closeWeek. leadersAtWeekStart/lostCause/winScore/askBlocked/raceOf all read raw `prospect.points`, and the store's weekly loop never asks whether a program can still sign before it plans that program's week.
- **Recommended fix:** Compute the set of full programs once per week in advanceRecruitingWeek (signed >= SCHOLARSHIPS). Skip aiTargets/planAiRecruitActions for those programs. Give leadersAtWeekStart, lostCause, winScore and askBlocked a `canSign(team)` predicate (or a pre-filtered points view) that drops points of programs with no room, mirroring `inTheRunning`. Use the same filter in raceOf/standing and in the staff's givenUp/suggestStaffList/staffReplacement. After the fix, re-check class size: generateClass makes 7.5 per program (720) against 8 scholarships (768), so the class is no longer 'well above what the league will sign'. *(Verifier's note: Natural repro, without r12's hand-raised points: scratchpad/agents/verify-recruiting/v0.ts (lib.workBoard each week, then askBlocked checked against programs with room). Fix as proposed. The simplest single point is a points view, built once a week in advanceRecruitingWeek, that drops teams with signed >= SCHOLARSHIPS. Feed it to leadersAtWeekStart/atWeekStart, and skip aiTargets/planAiRecruitActions for those teams. askBlocked needs a set of full teams, or a filtered best, so it matches closeWeek's inTheRunning rule. The UI race bars and the staff's lostCause callers should use the same filter.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/recruiting.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/staffRecruiting.ts`, `src/ui/screens/recruitRace.ts`
- **Risk:** Every season, in every save, about 10% of each national class (including 10-16 four/five-star men) evaporates, and roughly 25-30 extra programs fill holes with walk-ons rated 13 points lower. This drifts league quality over a long dynasty. From mid-season the coach's Ask to commit, the race bars ('Far behind') and the staff list ('Keeping in touch', suggestions) all point at schools that cannot sign the man.

#### H7. The closed Transfer portal step stays on the rail and the back gesture: it shows a blank screen, and a save plus reload there reopens the portal with a fresh pool and a zeroed budget

*Area: store-flow-A · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes**; also reported by store-flow-B, ui-postseason-offseason*

- **Issue:** The closed Transfer portal step stays on the rail and the back gesture: it shows a blank screen, and a save plus reload there reopens the portal with a fresh pool and a zeroed budget
- **Location:** store.ts:6602-6613 goPhase and store.ts:4389-4401 stepBack (back peel at nav.ts:60) re-enter 'portal' after closePortal (store.ts:3510) has set portal=null; Portal.tsx:67 `if (!portal || !rec || !pts) return null;`; store.ts:10276-10288 loadSlot rebuilds a portal whenever `phase==='portal' && portal===null`; budget is read off portal.spent (OffseasonStep.tsx:93-103, store.ts:6665 takeFromPortal)
- **Problem:** Leaving the portal step closes the portal for the whole country and sets portal=null, but the step stays walkable. On Signing day, Android back (stepBack) or a tap on 'Transfer portal' in the rail lands on phase 'portal' with portal=null. Portal renders nothing: no list and no Continue button. If anything then saves (for example 'Mark all read' in the inbox) and the app is restored, loadSlot's legacy-repair branch treats the state as an old save, opens a brand-new pool from the current rosters with spent=0, and the next Continue runs closePortal a second time.
- **How to reproduce:** UI: pw-back-signing.cjs (fast-forward to Signing day, then page.goBack()) and pw-portal-blank.cjs (rail tap 'Transfer portal' -> screenshot; inbox 'Mark all read'; page.reload(); Start screen 'Resume'), both in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Playball/f986342b-e697-5fb0-a121-7921d265dffe/scratchpad/agents/store-flow-A/. Store: t-portal-reopen2.ts (spend the whole budget in the real portal, reach signing, goPhase('portal'), saveNow, loadSlot, takeFromPortal everything available, nextPhase('portal')).
- **Expected behavior:** A closed portal step is skipped by back and the rail, or shows a read-only 'The portal has closed' summary with a way on. A reload never reopens a portal that already closed this winter.
- **Actual behavior:** Back from Signing day gives {phase:'portal', portal:null} with an empty main frame (shots/portal-02-rail-back.png: rail 'Step 5 of 6' over a blank page, no Continue). After Mark all read + reload + Resume, the portal is open again: 'Available 67', 'Offseason points 79 of 79 left', 'Continue to signing day' (shots/portal-03-after-reload.png). This was a casual career whose staff had already spent 77 of the 79. Store run: the first portal spent 79/79 and signed 2. After the reopen, portal.spent was 0, 3 more men were signed, portalSpend[me] reached 138 against a budget of 79, and the roster went 19 -> 22. closePortal then ran a second time for the league.
- **Root cause:** There is no 'portal closed' state. goPhase checks only `at > furthestPhase`, and stepBack walks railSteps. loadSlot (10276) cannot tell 'saved on the portal step before the pool was persisted' (legacy) from 'walked back to a portal that already closed', although furthestPhase (5 > 4) records that it closed. The coach's spend is also stored twice: portal.spent, which resets with the rebuilt pool, and season.portalSpend.
- **Recommended fix:** In loadSlot, rebuild only when `furthestPhase <= PHASES.indexOf('portal')`. In Portal.tsx, render a closed-portal summary with its ContinueBar when portal===null, or make stepBack/goPhase skip a closed portal step. Compute 'left' and the takeFromPortal/keepFromPortal checks from season.portalSpend[userTeam] (one source) instead of portal.spent.
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Portal.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/OffseasonStep.tsx`, `src/state/nav.ts`, `src/ui/App.tsx`
- **Risk:** A blank, apparently dead step behind the system back gesture on the last winter step. After a routine save + Android restore, a second transfer window: a full fresh budget, extra signings beyond the shared offseason pool, and a second round of rival departures, all persisted in the save.

#### H8. Injury replacements with Lineups delegated freezes the calendar for good; switching Injury replacements off does nothing for a coach who sets his own lineup

*Area: store-flow-C · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes***

- **Issue:** Injury replacements with Lineups delegated freezes the calendar for good; switching Injury replacements off does nothing for a coach who sets his own lineup
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:480-507 unresolvedRosterDecision; src/ui/screens/Lineup.tsx:73, 462, 540, 581, 645, 688; src/ui/Needs.tsx:171-230; src/state/depth.ts:177-182; store.ts:6776 moveDepth (no UI caller)
- **Problem:** unresolvedRosterDecision holds the day (advanceDay, simWeek, playSeason, startManagedGame, manageBracketGame, simBracket) whenever `handles(lineups) || handles(depthChart)` and a starter or rotation arm is unavailable but a cover exists. Every control that can clear that hold is gated on `handles(depth,'lineups')` only: swap, position picker, rotation/pen taps, AUTO and KEEP THE COVER (Lineup.tsx `mine`). The depth-chart action `moveDepth` has no UI caller. This splits two ways. (1) A coach whose staff sets the lineup but who keeps Injury replacements on is sent to a read-only lineup with no way out. That is Casual with 'Injury replacements' on, or Full with 'Lineups' off. (2) A coach who sets his own lineup and turns Injury replacements off ('Your staff slots in a replacement when a starter is hurt') is still held on every injury, because `writesCard` alone triggers the hold. The switch never makes the staff cover.
- **How to reproduce:** Store: scratchpad/agents/store-flow-C/p1b.ts (Casual + setDepthSystem('depthChart',true)) and p1c-full-lineups-off.ts (Full + setDepthSystem('lineups',false)). Each advances days until a starter is hurt, then presses advanceDay x40 and simWeek x5. UI: pw-chartonly.cjs (seed 13, team 9, Casual + Injury replacements on): Home shows 'Fix the lineup', Play ball is locked ('Settle the list') and Sim week is disabled. Fix the lineup opens the Lineup screen with 'Your bench coach sets the lineup', no Auto lineup button, and tapping the hurt starter opens his player card. Dead switch: p9-depthchart-off.ts (Full + Injury replacements off).
- **Expected behavior:** A coach is only held on a decision he has a control for. With Lineups delegated, either the staff covers or the chart/lineup controls are offered. With Injury replacements off, the staff covers a hurt starter before the next game.
- **Actual behavior:** With Lineups delegated, 5 of 6 Casual careers and 3 of 3 Full+Lineups-off careers stopped permanently: dayIndex stuck at 20/7/41/29/3 and stayed there after 40 more advanceDay and 5 simWeek presses. The only escape is to find Settings and flip a switch. With Injury replacements off in Full, the day is still held on every hurt starter (seed 12 day 20, seed 13 day 7, seed 16 day 3).
- **Root cause:** The hold condition (`if (!writesCard && !handles(depth,'depthChart')) return null`) treats depthChart as able to resolve the hold. Nothing in the UI that resolves it reads depthChart: Lineup.tsx `const mine = useDynasty(s => handles(s.depth,'lineups'))` disables every edit route, and moveDepth is never called from src/ui. The off state of depthChart is never consulted when lineups is handled. The 2026-09 fix in docs/05 §62.6 ('The return hold asked a chart-only coach a question with no button') removed only the return branch, not the hurt-starter branch.
- **Recommended fix:** In unresolvedRosterDecision, hold only when the coach both handles lineups and handles depthChart. When lineups is delegated, staffSetsTheCard already covers the hurt man before the day; also run fitTheNine/bestNine for the hurt man when depthChart is off for a lineup-setting coach. If a lineup-delegated coach who keeps depthChart on should still choose, enable swapStarter/promoteArm on the Lineup screen for unavailable men when handles(depthChart), or ship a depth-chart UI on moveDepth. Add a guard so a hold is never returned when the current depth settings expose no action that can clear it. *(Verifier's note: Part (2) is better described as a dead switch than a freeze: a lineup-setting coach can clear the hold himself. Fix: hold only when there is a control that can clear it, i.e. writesCard && handles(depthChart). With depthChart off, run fitTheNine/staffSetsTheCard for the hurt man before simNextDay. For lineups-off + depthChart-on, enable swap/promote for unavailable men on Lineup.tsx.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Lineup.tsx`, `src/ui/Needs.tsx`, `src/state/depth.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Today.tsx`
- **Risk:** Any player who turns on 'Injury replacements' in Casual, or turns 'Lineups' off in Full, both offered on the creation 'How you play' step and in Settings, gets a career that cannot reach the next day at the first injury, typically within the first week. The game looks broken and there is no hint beyond 'Change it in Settings'.

#### H9. Guided tour cards and spotlights draw underneath every design-system sheet, so step 10 'Set a focus' can never be seen or tapped and the tour stalls with nothing on screen, which also hides every first-visit tip for the rest of the first season

*Area: ui-first-run · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; independent reproduction: **yes***

- **Issue:** Guided tour cards and spotlights draw underneath every design-system sheet, so step 10 'Set a focus' can never be seen or tapped and the tour stalls with nothing on screen, which also hides every first-visit tip for the rest of the first season
- **Location:** src/ui/design/screens.css:79 (.pb-sheet-host z-index 60) vs screens.css:101 (.pb-tip-host z-index 38, used by TourLesson) and src/ui/prototype-frame.css:3233 (.guide-mask z-index 46); GuidedStretch.tsx:363-373; guide.ts:291-304 (step 'task'); Tutorial.tsx:30-31

Then close it with back. Script: scratchpad/agents/ui-first-run/tour2.cjs (AFTER=1 SEED=4242 TEAM=5 MODE=full).
- **Expected behavior:** The 'Set a focus' card and its spotlight sit above the coach sheet. Skip step / End tour can always be reached. A step whose control lives in a closed sheet tells the player how to get back to it.

After back: 'nothing of the tour on screen' until 'STUCK at task'. After the stall, team/stats, home/wire, team/stand and program/records all show 'first-visit tip=null tour UI=false'. Playwright's own click on Show me failed with '<div class="pb-sheet-host" data-owner="office|staff#4"> subtree intercepts pointer events'. Caption lines for sim-rest, hire-options and hire-detail log 'is hidden under: ["Protect this inning"]' / '["Open seat","Fletcher Montes"]'.
- **Root cause:** The tour layers' z-indices (38/46) predate the design-system sheet host (60) and were never raised above it. guide.ts 'task' has no fallback target outside the sheet; its target is only ['directive'].

Add a CSS invariant test that keeps the tour layers above .pb-sheet-host. *(Verifier's note: The Settings tutorials preference is the only other way out (readPrefs().tutorials), and it is not discoverable from the stalled state. The fix as proposed: put the tour layers (.pb-tip-host--tour, .guide-mask, .guide-scrim, .guide-caption) above 60, or below .pb-fulloverlay.is-over-sheet/65 if that has to stay on top. Add a fallback target ('seat-hitting') to 'task', and loosen its `where` so it does not need the sheet open.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/design/screens.css`, `src/ui/prototype-frame.css`, `src/ui/GuidedStretch.tsx`, `src/ui/guide.ts`, `src/ui/Tutorial.tsx`
