#### H10. Box-score Replay of every managed game is wrong: stuck in 'Top of the 1st', outs climb past 3, all runs credited to the away team

*Area: ui-home-live-game · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Box-score Replay of every managed game is wrong: stuck in 'Top of the 1st', outs climb past 3, all runs credited to the away team
- **Location:** src/ui/replay.ts:37 (HEADER regex) vs src/engine/liveGame.ts:310 (openHalf header); rendered by BoxScoreSheet in src/ui/screens/Schedule.tsx:271-405
- **Problem:** buildFrames() recognises a half-inning only when the log line matches /--- (Top|Bottom) (\d+)\w+ --- \((\d+)-(\d+)\)/, which requires an ordinal suffix ('1st'). simGame writes '--- Top 1st ---' (game.ts:737), but the managed game writes '--- Top 1 ---' (liveGame.ts:310). So for every game the coach managed (the replay that is stored on its box score at season.ts:2544), no header ever matches: half stays 'top', inning stays 1, outs and bases never reset, and every run (home runs included) is added to awayRuns. The header lines are shown as 'note' frames ('Play 1 of 126 | --- Top 1 --- (0-0)'). Separately, simGame's ORD array stops at 15, so a 16+ inning simulated game logs 'Top undefined' and loses its headers too.
- **How to reproduce:** Playwright: new career, Play ball, Dugout > Sim the rest (tap twice), Record the game, tap the WEEK label > Results > the Final game > Replay > End. Script: agents/ui-home-live-game/r12b-replay-end.cjs. Headless: agents/ui-home-live-game/t01-replay-live.ts (npx tsx) builds frames from createLiveGame vs simGame for 3 seeds.
- **Expected behavior:** Replay steps through innings 1-9 with outs 0-3 and finishes on the real final score (10-4 for THB), as it does for simulated games.
- **Actual behavior:** UI end frame: 'Colliers 14 | Top of the 1st | Herons 0 | Bases loaded, 3 outs | Play 126 of 126' under a sheet titled 'Thibodaux State 10, Allegheny Ridge 4'. Headless: 'LIVE seed 11: header lines 17 e.g. "\n--- Top 1 --- (0-0)"; inning frames parsed 0; distinct innings in frames 1; max outs 51; final 11-0 vs result 5-6' (seed 404: max outs 54, final 17-0 vs 12-5). SIM games parse 17-18 inning frames, max outs 3.
- **Root cause:** Two engines write the same header in different formats and the parser only accepts the ordinal one; tests/replay.test.ts only feeds simGame output, so the managed path was never exercised.
- **Recommended fix:** Accept both formats: HEADER = /--- (Top|Bottom) (\d+)(?:st|nd|rd|th)? --- \((\d+)-(\d+)\)/ in replay.ts, and/or make liveGame.ts:310 use the same ordinal helper as game.ts. Replace game.ts ORD[inning-1] with an ordinal() function so inning 16+ cannot print 'undefined'. Add the managed-game invariants (inning frames > 0, outs <= 3, final score matches result) to tests/replay.test.ts using createLiveGame. *(Verifier's note: One more quirk: for innings 10+ the regex backtracks, so 'Top 10' matches as inning 1 (\d+='1', \w+='0'). That makes the ordinal-optional regex fix, or a shared ordinal() helper in both engines, even more important. game.ts:94 ORD stops at 15, so a 16+ inning simGame prints 'undefined'.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/replay.ts`, `src/engine/liveGame.ts`, `src/engine/game.ts`, `tests/replay.test.ts`
- **Risk:** Every game the player personally coaches shows a nonsensical replay with a final score that contradicts the box score directly above it; it undermines trust in the results of the core 'Play ball' loop. Display-only, no save corruption.

### MEDIUM (108)

#### M1. Status-bar and gesture-bar icons follow the phone's theme, not the in-app theme: clock/battery become invisible whenever Settings > Display > Theme differs from the system (Android 15/16)

*Area: android-release · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Status-bar and gesture-bar icons follow the phone's theme, not the in-app theme: clock/battery become invisible whenever Settings > Display > Theme differs from the system (Android 15/16)
- **Location:** src/state/devicePrefs.ts:211-232 applyPrefs (theme only sets data-theme); src/ui/App.tsx (no SystemBars call anywhere in src); node_modules/@capacitor/android/capacitor/src/main/java/com/getcapacitor/plugin/SystemBars.java:95-117, 282-300, 326-332
- **Problem:** On Android 15/16 (targetSdk 36 forces edge-to-edge; WebView >=140 with viewport-fit=cover draws the page under the bars) the status-bar and gesture-bar icon colour is chosen by Capacitor SystemBars style DEFAULT = the SYSTEM night mode. The in-app theme (Light/Dark override in Settings > Display, a feature added because 'this white is too bright') only flips CSS. When the two disagree, dark icons sit on the app's dark top bar (or white icons on its white top bar).
- **How to reproduce:** Device: phone in system LIGHT mode, Android 15/16, Settings > Display > Theme: Dark (or system DARK + app Light). Runtime emulation: agents/android-release/statusbar.cjs (dev server, CDP Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride top=24px, samples the pixels under the status bar on Start, Home, Settings and a live game for all four system/app theme combinations; icon colour modelled as #1f1f1f for a light-status-bar window and #fff otherwise).
- **Expected behavior:** Bar icons always contrast with the app's own top bar (>=3:1), whatever the in-app theme.
- **Actual behavior:** System light / app dark: contrast 1.12:1 (Start), 1.20:1 (Home), 1.03:1 (Settings), 1.03:1 (live game). System dark / app light: 1.07, 3.36 (Home under a scrim), 1.00, 1.00. The bottom gesture-handle strip measures the same (1.00-1.12:1). Matching themes: 15.4-19.8:1.
- **Root cause:** SystemBars.initSystemBars() applies style DEFAULT; setStyle() resolves DEFAULT via getStyleForTheme(), which reads Configuration.uiMode (system night mode), then calls setAppearanceLightStatusBars/NavigationBars. Nothing in src calls SystemBars.setStyle when DevicePrefs.theme overrides the system, and <meta name=theme-color> (index.html:15-16) has no effect inside a WebView. On Android 14 and below the app is not edge-to-edge and the bar is opaque, drawn from AppTheme.NoActionBar which sets no status-bar colour, so it does not match the app's paper either (code-reviewed only).
- **Recommended fix:** Where prefs are applied (applyPrefs or an App effect keyed on prefs.theme plus a matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') listener), when isNativeShell(): `import { SystemBars, SystemBarsStyle } from '@capacitor/core'` and call `SystemBars.setStyle({ style: resolvedDark ? SystemBarsStyle.Dark : SystemBarsStyle.Light })` (Default only when theme==='system'). SystemBars re-applies the current style on configuration changes, so one call per change is enough. *(Verifier's note: Small scoping note: with WebView<140 on Android 15+, SystemBars pads the WebView's parent and sets the decor background to windowBackground (DayNight, which follows the system theme), so icons and background still match there. The mismatch needs WebView>=140 plus viewport-fit=cover. The proposed fix is valid: @capacitor/core 8.5.1 exports SystemBars and SystemBarsStyle (core-plugins.d.ts:242, 336-342), and handleOnConfigurationChanged re-applies the current style. Call it from the same place applyPrefs runs, and also on a matchMedia change while theme==='system'.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/devicePrefs.ts`, `src/ui/App.tsx`, `index.html`, `node_modules/@capacitor/android/capacitor/src/main/java/com/getcapacitor/plugin/SystemBars.java`
- **Risk:** Players who choose the theme opposite to their phone lose the clock, battery and notification icons and the gesture handle on every screen of the game.

#### M2. App start is blocked for as long as fonts.googleapis.com hangs: the render-blocking font stylesheet holds first paint (12.4 s in a 12 s stall) - not even the boot splash shows

*Area: android-release · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** App start is blocked for as long as fonts.googleapis.com hangs: the render-blocking font stylesheet holds first paint (12.4 s in a 12 s stall) - not even the boot splash shows
- **Location:** index.html:28-33 (preconnect + <link rel=stylesheet> to fonts.googleapis.com in <head>), index.html:41-55 (boot splash and module script come after it)
- **Problem:** The baseline already notes the Google Fonts request contradicts the privacy policy. Separately, the stylesheet is render-blocking and also blocks execution of the following module script, so the game's first paint waits for that network request. On a connection that neither answers nor fails fast (Wi-Fi without internet, captive portal dropping HTTPS, weak mobile data) the WebView stays blank until the request gives up - for an app advertised as fully offline.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/android-release/fontstall2.cjs: production build on :5173, Playwright route makes fonts.googleapis.com/fonts.gstatic.com stall 12 s and then abort; compare with an immediate abort (airplane mode). Read performance paint entries.
- **Expected behavior:** An offline-first app paints its splash and start screen within a few hundred ms regardless of network state.
- **Actual behavior:** Stall: first-paint@12404ms, first-contentful-paint@12472ms, font CSS ended @12173ms, main JS had loaded @285ms. Fast failure: first-paint@276ms. During the stall #root stays empty and the boot splash (which lives in <body>) is never painted.
- **Root cause:** <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?..." rel="stylesheet"> in <head> is a render-blocking stylesheet; browsers also hold a later script until preceding stylesheets settle.
- **Recommended fix:** Self-host the three families (woff2 files in public/fonts + @font-face with font-display: swap in src/ui/tokens.css) and delete the preconnect/stylesheet links. This also removes the third-party request the privacy policy and Data safety answers say does not exist. Interim mitigation: load the stylesheet non-blocking (media="print" onload="this.media='all'"). *(Verifier's note: It shares its root cause and fix with the baseline Google Fonts/privacy item: self-host the woff2 files with font-display: swap and drop both links. Report the two together rather than as separate defects.)*
- **Files affected:** `index.html`, `src/ui/tokens.css`
- **Risk:** Users on flaky networks see a blank screen for many seconds (up to the OS connect timeout) every launch; reviews will read it as a broken app.

#### M3. On phones without WebGL2 the live game's 3D field is an empty green box: the designed fallback to the 2D diamond never fires

*Area: android-release · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** On phones without WebGL2 the live game's 3D field is an empty green box: the designed fallback to the 2D diamond never fires
- **Location:** src/ui/Diamond3D.tsx:1559-1568 (FieldBoundary), 1630-1661 (ok/setOk fallback); src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx:130,155 (3D chosen purely from prefs.field, default '3d'); node_modules/@react-three/fiber/dist/react-three-fiber.esm.js:62-115 (Canvas)
- **Problem:** three.js r185 needs WebGL2. On devices whose GPU/driver gives no WebGL2 context (GLES2-only or blocklisted GPUs, common among the old Android 7-9 phones minSdk 24 admits) the renderer fails, but the error never reaches FieldBoundary, so the 2D diamond the code comment promises ('A device that cannot give us WebGL gets the 2D diamond rather than a crash - or an empty box') is never shown. The field stays an empty green rectangle in every managed game until the player finds Settings > Display > field 2D.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/android-release/nowebgl.cjs: Chromium launched with --disable-webgl2 (WebGL1 still available) and, separately, with WebGL fully disabled; prefs.field '3d' (the default); start(777,5) then startManagedGame().
- **Expected behavior:** The 2D <Diamond> renders in place of the park (Diamond3D.tsx:1647-1655).
- **Actual behavior:** Empty green field box (shots/webgl2-off-live.png); pageerror 'THREE.WebGLRenderer: Error creating WebGL context.'; no .app-crash; prefs.field still '3d'; same in both runs.
- **Root cause:** R3F 9.7 Canvas creates the renderer inside `async function run(){ await root.current.configure({ gl, ... }) }`, invoked as a bare `run()` from a layout effect with no catch. The rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection; R3F's own ErrorBoundary (set: setError) only wraps children rendered after configure succeeds, and React error boundaries never see async errors, so FieldBoundary.componentDidCatch -> setOk(false) never runs. No code checks WebGL2 availability up front (park.ts/Manage.tsx/Diamond3D.tsx).
- **Recommended fix:** Before mounting <Canvas>, probe once: `const gl2 = (() => { try { return !!document.createElement('canvas').getContext('webgl2'); } catch { return false; } })()`; if false render the 2D Diamond (and optionally persist prefs.field='2d' once, so three.js is not fetched again). Belt and braces: pass a `gl` factory that wraps `new THREE.WebGLRenderer(...)` in try/catch and calls setOk(false) on failure. *(Verifier's note: Probe up front: if canvas.getContext('webgl2') fails, render the 2D Diamond, ideally in Manage.tsx/usePark so three.js is not even fetched. Also pass Canvas a gl factory that wraps new THREE.WebGLRenderer in try/catch and calls setOk(false), to cover renderer failures after the probe.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/Diamond3D.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx`, `src/ui/park.ts`, `src/state/devicePrefs.ts`
- **Risk:** Exactly the 'older phones' the store listing promises a 2D field for get an empty field instead of runners and fielders on every managed game.

#### M4. `npm run apk` / `npm run aab` cannot work from a clean checkout on any machine: the script writes into android/ before anything creates it, and outside Windows it calls gradlew.bat

*Area: android-release · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** `npm run apk` / `npm run aab` cannot work from a clean checkout on any machine: the script writes into android/ before anything creates it, and outside Windows it calls gradlew.bat
- **Location:** scripts/apk.cjs:61-64 (writes android/local.properties first), 70-72 (never runs `cap add`), 42-45 (Windows-only default JAVA_HOME/ANDROID_HOME), 162 (`gradlew.bat`)
- **Problem:** The android/ shell is gitignored and generated, and the .gitignore and README say the project 'can be rebuilt from scratch by anyone with the toolchain' with 'one command'. The script never runs `npx cap add android`; its first action is fs.writeFileSync('android/local.properties'), which throws ENOENT on a fresh clone. With a shell present, on macOS/Linux it does all the work and then fails at Gradle because it runs the Windows batch wrapper. (The tsc failure that also breaks `npm run build` is baseline and separate.)
- **How to reproduce:** 1) `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C agents/android-release/clean`; JAVA_HOME/ANDROID_HOME pointed at existing dirs; `node scripts/apk.cjs`. 2) Copy the lead's generated android/ project in, stub npm/npx with no-op shims on PATH, add a dummy android/keystore.properties, `node scripts/apk.cjs bundle`.
- **Expected behavior:** A fresh clone plus the toolchain produces the signed AAB, as documented.
- **Actual behavior:** Run 1: 'Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open .../clean/android/local.properties at .../scripts/apk.cjs:61:4' before any build step. Run 2: build, cap sync, capacitor-assets, native copy, 'version 1.0.0 (code 10000) written', signing patch all run, then `"…/android/gradlew.bat" bundleRelease` exits with status 126 on Linux.
- **Root cause:** The script assumes a pre-provisioned Windows machine with an already-generated shell: no `cap add` step, and the Gradle wrapper name is hard-coded to gradlew.bat.
- **Recommended fix:** Before line 61: `if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(ROOT, 'android'))) run('npx', ['cap', 'add', 'android'], ROOT);`. At line 162 use `process.platform === 'win32' ? 'gradlew.bat' : './gradlew'`. Document the toolchain prerequisites (JDK 21, SDK platform 36) in the README. *(Verifier's note: Downgrade to LOW. Fix as proposed: run `npx cap add android` when android/ is missing, choose the wrapper with process.platform, and document JDK 21 and SDK 36 in the README.)*
- **Files affected:** `scripts/apk.cjs`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`
- **Risk:** If the author's machine or android/ folder is lost, nobody can produce a store build from the repository without reverse-engineering the steps; CI builds are impossible.

*Area: android-release · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

#### M6. The seeded NCAA season records fall in year one (HR, SLG, K/9, usually RBI) or can essentially never fall (IP, Wins), not 'one season in fifteen to twenty'

*Area: balance-realism · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The seeded NCAA season records fall in year one (HR, SLG, K/9, usually RBI) or can essentially never fall (IP, Wins), not 'one season in fifteen to twenty'
- **Location:** src/engine/records.ts:325-386 (SEEDS) and the rationale table at :244-262; tests/records-probe.ts:63-75 (LEAGUE_BEST, last changed in 571391b, 2026-09-11); tests/records.test.ts:100-111; docs/05-systems-reference.md §13.3 (:2789-2880)
- **Problem:** Each seeded mark was placed where 'about one season in fifteen to twenty beats it', using a league-best distribution measured on the 2026-09-11 engine. In today's store-driven world, the country's best season clears Incaviglia's HR and SLG and Wagner's K/9 in almost every season, including the very first season of every career. Meanwhile Bannister's 158 IP and Loynd's 16 wins sit far above anything a normal season produces. The test cannot notice, because it reads the frozen LEAGUE_BEST constants instead of simulating.
- **How to reproduce:** cd $D && SEED=27999 STARS=1 USER_MODE=delegate YEARS=25 npx tsx bal2.ts, which logs each season's league best per category (qualified the way recordSeasonMarks qualifies) and the record book after the draft step. Then python3 recbest.py run-*.jsonl run2-*.jsonl.
- **Expected behavior:** Each seeded row is beaten about once in 15-20 seasons (records.ts:244-262, docs/05 §13.3). records.test.ts asserts a 10-30-year return period.
- **Actual behavior:** League best per season against the seed. HR, RBI, W and IP are pooled over 114 league-seasons and six seeds; the other rows over 66 league-seasons and three seeds:
- HR: 22.0±2.2 vs 18. Beaten in 96% of seasons; the probe said 14.5±2.4.
- SLG: .900±.051 vs .830. Beaten in 91%.
- K/9: 15.7±0.9 vs 13.5. Beaten in 100%.
- RBI: 101.5±9.9 vs 93. Beaten in 76%.
- Doubles: 30.0 vs 30. Beaten in 36%.
- AVG: .483 vs .500. Beaten in 23%.
- TB: 190 vs 198. Beaten in 24%.
- Triples: 7.7 vs 10. Beaten in 5%.
- Wins: 12.9±1.3 vs 16. Beaten in 3%.
- IP: 112.7±12.4 vs 158. Beaten in 2%, and only by the overworked-arm outliers in the next finding.
In all three 20+-season worlds, HR, SLG and K/9 changed hands in year 1. In seed 27999, K/9 changed hands 6 times in 25 seasons, and by year 12 every seeded row except IP and scoreless innings had been replaced.
- **Root cause:** SEEDS were fitted to LEAGUE_BEST, which records-probe measured on the 2026-09-11 engine with the headless dynasty loop. The 2026-09-15 passes changed the population: §83 aged rosters, §85 re-fitted BAT_NORM/PIT_NORM/JENSEN_K, and §86-88 changed the recruiting boards and raised the top star band to 68-80. That lengthened the hitting and strikeout tail and shortened innings per arm. records.test.ts re-reads the same constants, so it passes whatever the engine does.
- **Recommended fix:** Re-run records-probe on the current engine using the store's yearly order (or $D/bal2.ts), then re-seed. On these numbers that is roughly HR 26, SLG 1.000, K/9 17.5, RBI 125, doubles 35, AVG .530, TB 215, IP 130, W 15 and triples 10, each at or below the real mark. Replace the constant-reading assertion with a slow or nightly probe that checks each row's empirical beat rate stays between 3% and 12%. *(Verifier's note: Re-run records-probe (or a store-driven harness) on the current engine and re-seed every row at or below the real mark. Replace the constant-reading test with a periodic probe of empirical beat rates. The rare 155-168 IP seasons that beat the IP seed come partly from the rest misdating described in finding 6.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/records.ts`, `tests/records-probe.ts`, `tests/records.test.ts`, `docs/05-systems-reference.md`
- **Risk:** The NCAA-badged rows the screen presents as targets vanish in the first June of every career, while the IP and Wins rows become furniture. The book no longer means 'once in a generation'.

#### M7. Program prestige inflates for about 20 seasons: five-star programs go from 3 to 30, every four-star program becomes five-star, and the documented convergence figures are wrong

*Area: balance-realism · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Program prestige inflates for about 20 seasons: five-star programs go from 3 to 30, every four-star program becomes five-star, and the documented convergence figures are wrong
- **Location:** src/engine/program.ts:42-50 (initialPrestige, STAR_MARKS 38/48/60/72), :188-275 (seasonScore, climbLift, programTarget), :382-503 (prestigeChange); docs/05-systems-reference.md:3610-3619 (§16.9 table) and :174 (row 74b); README.md:33
- **Problem:** Wins are zero-sum, yet almost every program's prestige rises for the first two decades, and the fixed star thresholds then relabel the country. 66-73 of 96 programs gain prestige in each of the first three years and only 6-10 lose any; programs still net +0.1-0.5 a year in years 15-20. By year 16, all 44 programs that started at four stars are five-star, along with 71% of the three-star starters and 26% of the two-star starters. The 182 one-star starters average 27.6 → 38.8 and none reaches five stars. Prestige separates from strength at the top: top-5 prestige climbs 74.6 → 89, while top-10 roster strength stays about 72 through year 16 and is 69 by year 22 in seed 27999. The four-star board tier gets squeezed and signs 4.5-6.3 men a winter in years 10-16 (§86 says 6.6).
- **How to reproduce:** cd $D && three store-driven careers: SEED=27999 STARS=1 / SEED=5000 STARS=5 / SEED=20080 STARS=3, each with USER_MODE=delegate YEARS=25 npx tsx bal2.ts, plus SEED=4242/12161/20080 YEARS=25 npx tsx bal.ts (stopped at 16 seasons). Then python3 analyze.py, pooled.py and the summary() function. Counterfactual: SEEDS=4242,12161 npx tsx ratchet.ts.
- **Expected behavior:** docs/05 §16.9: mean 40.9 → 51.4, 'flat from year 18', SD 17.1, star distribution 25/23/22/12/14 (14 five-star programs) at year 35. Row 74b: 'Mean prestige drifts 41→51 … over thirty five seasons'.
- **Actual behavior:** Store-driven, mean of three seeds: mean prestige 40.9 → 49.2 (y5) → 54.0 (y10) → 56.0 (y15) → 57.2 (y20), and seed 27999 levels off at 58.2 from year 22. SD 15.4 → 20.6. Top-5 average 74.6 → 88.5. Star distribution 46/20/16/11/3 → 23.7/10/17/15.3/30.0 at year 20, i.e. 30% of the league is five-star.
- **Root cause:** Starting prestige comes from the school table and has a mean of 40.9 with 46 one-star programs. programTarget pulls toward winPct×100 plus postseason bonuses (about +3 on average), boosted by climbLift and climbBonus below 48, and that target sits about 15 points higher. So almost every program drifts upward until it meets it. The board floors are a minor part: ratchet.ts shows that with no verdict at all, 63-66 of 96 programs still rise in year one, net +2.6-2.8 a program against +2.8-3.0 shipped. STAR_MARKS are absolute, so the shifted distribution moves programs between tiers.
- **Recommended fix:** Put prestige on one scale. Options: map initialPrestige onto the target's equilibrium (league mean about 56) while keeping each school's rank; make programTarget league-relative by subtracting the league's mean target minus 50, the same correction leagueShape already applies to rival boards; or make the star tiers percentile-based (for example, top 4% is five-star). Then re-measure and correct §16.9, row 74b and README.md:33. The fix must keep the climbLift and climbBonus behaviour for small programs. *(Verifier's note: Re-measure §16.9, row 74b and README.md:33 with today's carousel-probe as well as the store harness. Decide whether to normalise prestige to the league or to make star tiers percentile-based. That is a design decision, so treat it as calibration work rather than a crash-class bug.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/program.ts`, `docs/05-systems-reference.md`, `README.md`
- **Risk:** Star labels drive job offers, the hiring ladder (HIRE_REQUIREMENT), recruiting reach (canPursue), budgets and boardsByTier, and they mean something different in year 15 than in year 1. A third of the country becomes 'five-star', the four-star tier is squeezed, and the docs promise a stationary ladder that does not exist.

#### M8. Firing an assistant refunds his whole year's wage, so staff can work a full season and their wages be spent again on buildings before the roll

*Area: career-program · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; also reported by store-flow-C*

- **Issue:** Firing an assistant refunds his whole year's wage, so staff can work a full season and their wages be spent again on buildings before the roll
- **Location:** src/engine/economy.ts:774-776 remaining(); src/state/store.ts:9155-9167 fireAssistant, 9125-9153 hireAssistant (replace), 9284-9326 build/upgradeFacility; rollYear store.ts:5951-5952 (spent: 0)
- **Problem:** Wages are never charged. `remaining = annualBudget - wageBill(current staff) - spent`, so a wage is only a reservation against whoever is on staff right now. A coach can keep three assistants all season (development, game edge, season work) and fire them in the offseason. That frees the full year's wages, which build/upgradeFacility then spend before the roll resets the ledger. The Budget room tells the player wages are 'paid every year'.
- **How to reproduce:** money.ts (seed 4242, Bayou State, assistants and facilities handled by the coach): hireAssistant slot 0 in all three seats. Play the season and June, then go to the Coach points step. Try every build/upgrade. Fire all three assistants and try again.
- **Expected behavior:** A season of service costs its wage. Firing after the work is done should not hand the money back, or wages should be booked into `spent` as they accrue.
- **Actual behavior:** 'money after hiring {budget:1764,wages:785,left:979}' → offseason 'builds possible while staff kept: {} -> {cage:1}' → 'fired all three in the offseason: money {wages:0,spent:620,left:1196}' → 'builds after firing: levels -> {cage:3} ... spent:1670'. Summary line: '=> this year: wages reserved for a full season of work 785, facilities bought 1670; total 2455 vs annual budget 1816'.
- **Root cause:** remaining() subtracts the live wage bill instead of wages actually owed or paid. fireAssistant and the replacement path in hireAssistant remove the man's whole annual wage from the ledger regardless of how much of the year he worked.
- **Recommended fix:** Charge wages into economy.spent: pro-rate by recruiting week or calendar week when a man leaves, or charge the full annual wage at hire or at the roll as 'committed'. Then firing frees only the unworked part. Alternatively make the Budget ledger keep a 'wages committed this year' figure that firing does not reduce.
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/economy.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** The economy's central trade-off (staff versus buildings) can be bypassed every year. A coach ends up with a full staff and maxed facilities on one budget.

*Area: career-program · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **How to reproduce:** money3.ts shows the real path: at Bayou State, star every 1-star job (TRACK JOB PATH); at the next roll 36 flagged 1-star offers ring. money4.ts / ui-budget.cjs (seed 132, whose 2027 market has $1.36M of slot-0 assistants): at Bayou State hire the three dearest men, then take the Passaic Falls (prestige 19) job through the Job offers screen's two-tap button. Open the Budget room.
- **Expected behavior:** Either the move warns about and settles the wage bill (contracts end or the board pays the difference), or remaining() can never go below zero.
- **Actual behavior:** money4: 'took Passaic Falls p19 (budget $997k): wages 1360 -> remaining -363 (NEGATIVE)'; 'can build? false'; scouting is refused too. Budget room on Pixel 7: 'Left this season $0k of $997k · Staff wages $1.36M · Buildings $0k · Left $0k', and Build the Clubhouse shows '$580k short'. market-scan.ts: in 602 of 1,800 seed-year markets the three best men cost more than a prestige-25 school's whole budget ($1,075k).
- **Root cause:** The carried Economy (`{...freshEconomy(), staff: {...oldEconomy.staff}}`) is never checked against annualBudget(new prestige). The UI clamps the deficit to 0 instead of showing it.
- **Recommended fix:** In acceptOffer, if wageBill(staff) > annualBudget(new prestige), show the overrun on the offer card ('Your staff's $1.36M wages exceed this program's $997k budget') and let the player choose who comes. Or have the new school absorb the contracts with a one-off grant. Show a real deficit in BudgetLedger instead of Math.max(0, left), and compute 'short' from the signed value. *(Verifier's note: Risk wording: the player is not locked out for three years, since firing restores spending power at once. The defect is the absent warning on the offer card plus the clamped display. Also fix BuyList (program.tsx:687) to use the signed value for 'short'.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/economy.ts`, `src/ui/screens/ProgramRooms.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/JobMarket.tsx`
- **Risk:** A coach moving down the ladder with a good staff is locked out of facilities and scouting for up to three years, and the money screens misreport by hundreds of thousands, which reads as a bug.

#### M10. Every school whose coach changes at the June carousel has last season credited in its yearbook to the incoming coach

*Area: career-program · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Every school whose coach changes at the June carousel has last season credited in its yearbook to the incoming coach
- **Location:** src/engine/postseason.ts:1700-1702 recordSchoolAnnals (coach: t.coach.name), called from rollYear src/state/store.ts:6008; the carousel runs earlier in settleSeason store.ts:5710 → src/engine/rivals.ts:574-616 runCarousel
- **Problem:** The school annals row for year N is written at the year roll and takes the head coach's name from `t.coach`. By then settleSeason has already run runRivalYear, which sacks, retires and poaches coaches and seats replacements. Any chair that changed hands therefore names the new hire as the man who coached season N. The History screen ('Head coach' in Season details) and the legacy sheets read these rows.
- **How to reproduce:** annals.ts (seed 2024, 4 seasons): record each team's coach at the end of June, walk the offseason, then compare annals[year].coach after the roll.
- **Expected behavior:** The yearbook names the coach who coached that season.
- **Actual behavior:** 'year 2028: chairs that changed hands at the June meeting 1; yearbooks naming the wrong head coach for 2028: 1 — Lake Charles: 2028 coached by Cooper Warrington, yearbook says "Cormac Warrington"'; '2029: ... 6; ... 6 — Port Arthur: 2029 coached by Justin Strickland, yearbook says "Kobe Avalos"'; '2030: ... 8; ... 8'. All of them are wrong, every year.
- **Root cause:** The annals are written after the carousel has mutated `t.coach` (ordering bug between settleSeason and rollYear).
- **Recommended fix:** Capture each chair's coach name before runRivalYear in settleSeason (e.g. `t.seasonCoach = t.coach?.name`) and have recordSchoolAnnals use it. Or call recordSchoolAnnals from settleSeason before the carousel (it is idempotent by year). Add a test that sacks a rival and checks the annals. *(Verifier's note: The simplest fix is to call recordSchoolAnnals from settleSeason before runRivalYear (it is idempotent by year), passing the coach the user had during the season. Alternatively snapshot coach names before the carousel.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/postseason.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/rivals.ts`
- **Risk:** Permanent wrong attribution in every program's history, growing by about 5-10 rows a year. The same timing makes a coach hired in the offseason (acceptOffer before the roll) the named coach of the season his predecessor coached.

#### M11. The year roll settles moods with an old copy of the rule, so every pitcher reads as benched in a no-portal world and after any winter the coach leaves

*Area: code-quality-tests · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The year roll settles moods with an old copy of the rule, so every pitcher reads as benched in a no-portal world and after any winter the coach leaves
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:6140-6181 and 6224-6237 (rollYear, the `!settled` fallback settle) vs src/state/store.ts:2240-2276 (settleTheMoods). Triggered via stepAfter (store.ts:943, the portal step is skipped when rules.portal is false) and winterWithoutHim (store.ts:3372-3377), which the review exit (store.ts:5092-5105), resign (6977) and endCareer (7007) call
- **Problem:** There are two copies of the rule that settles a season's mood. settleTheMoods runs when the portal opens. It measures pitchers with armShare: their outings against the busiest arm doing the same job. The copy inside rollYear runs whenever the portal step did not run first, and it still passes `starts: p.starts ?? 0, games: played`. For a pure pitcher that is 0 starts out of every team game, so settleMood (morale.ts:221-243) reads every pitcher in the country as buried and takes about 20 points off his mood. The comment at store.ts:6136-6139 says no such winter exists on the rail. Two do. A world created with Transfer portal: Off never reaches the portal step, every winter. A winter in which the coach is let go, not renewed, resigns or ends his career at the review goes through winterWithoutHim, which never calls settleTheMoods.
- **How to reproduce:** Scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Playball/f986342b-e697-5fb0-a121-7921d265dffe/scratchpad/agents/code-quality-tests: `npx tsx moodMine.ts` (seed 4242, team 0, same season with portal on vs off), `npx tsx moodFired.ts` (portal on: normal winter vs lastReview.fired=true at the review) and `npx tsx moodSettleProbe.ts noportal` (predicts both formulas for every rival pitcher before the roll and compares them with the real result). Each script calls start(), then simSeason + freezeRegularSeason, sets phase 'awards', and calls nextPhase until the year rolls.
- **Expected behavior:** Pitchers come out of the winter with about the same mood whatever the portal rule, and whether or not the coach left. With the portal on that is a mean of about 65, with 1-2 of about 1,015 pitchers unhappy (<42).
- **Actual behavior:** Portal off: pitchers' mean mood is 49.2 and 272/1015 are unhappy, against 64.9 and 2/1017 with the portal on. Coach let go at the review (portal on): 49.2 and 266/1016, against 65.0 and 1/1014. Hitters do not change (58.7-59.1). moodSettleProbe: 832 of 849 rival pitchers' post-roll moods equal the fallback (no-armShare) formula exactly and 0 equal the settleTheMoods formula. The mean gap is 18.9 points per pitcher. The user's own staff drops from about 71 to 44-58.
- **Root cause:** The armShare fix (store.ts:2248-2250: 'Nothing ever counted a pitcher playing...') went into settleTheMoods only. rollYear still has its own inline copy, at store.ts:6172-6181 for the user's men and 6231-6236 for the other 95, and that copy predates the fix. Whether the copy runs depends on two things, `season.moraleSettled` and a `furthestPhase` 'belt' (6140-6145). Both are false in the two skipped-portal winters.
- **Recommended fix:** Keep one implementation. Move settleTheMoods into the engine (for example morale.ts settleWinterMoods(season, userTeam, captainOf)). In rollYear, call it on the finished season whenever `season.moraleSettled !== true`, before `starts` is wiped, and delete the inline copies at 6172-6181 and 6231-6236. Also call it from winterWithoutHim, so a winter the coach leaves is judged like any other. Add the parity test described in testGaps. *(Verifier's note: Root cause and fix are as stated. One way to fix it with minimal churn: in rollYear, replace both inline `!settled` blocks with a call to `settleTheMoods(season, userTeam)` on the finished season before `starts` is deleted, and call it as well from winterWithoutHim before leagueWinter. settleTheMoods already sets `moraleSettled`, so the `furthestPhase` belt can go. Keep the promise-expiry and `starts` wipes in the roll.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/morale.ts`
- **Risk:** In no-portal careers about a quarter of the country's pitchers, and most of the user's own staff, read Unhappy every spring on the player card (mood and flight risk). After a winter the coach leaves, the depressed moods carry into the next winter's portal, because settleMood starts from the current mood. That raises pitcher flight risk and keep costs (portal.ts:143, 282; Portal.tsx:35) for every program. Pitching itself is unaffected, because moodMultiplier applies only to batters (game.ts:1229).

#### M12. In 56-game worlds June builds a five-man rotation, but Signing Day, the NEEDS tab, the staff's list and the Draft screen all still assume four

*Area: code-quality-tests · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** In 56-game worlds June builds a five-man rotation, but Signing Day, the NEEDS tab, the staff's list and the Draft screen all still assume four
- **Location:** src/engine/progression.ts:236 (walkOnClass calls walkOnShortfall with no rotation size), 266-268 (walkOnShortfall `rotationSize = ROTATION_SIZE`), 390-391 (holesFor default), 446 (depthShortfall `starters === ROTATION_SIZE`), 822-825 (regroup slices the rotation to ROTATION_SIZE). These differ from progression.ts:934, where fillRosters passes rotationSizeFor(season.config), and from roster.ts:274/218 (refill, with the walkOnArm(rng) fallback). Callers: SigningDay.tsx:112, Board.tsx:335/338/361, store.ts:309 (suggestedStaffList), recruitingPlan.ts:82-83, Draft.tsx:135/141/241
- **Problem:** The rotation size is a world rule: rotationSizeFor gives 5 for the 56-game schedule a player can pick at creation ('Four-game weekends and a five-man rotation'). Only createSeason and fillRosters pass that value. Every projection function defaults to ROTATION_SIZE (4), and three places hard-code it. So the Signing Day class review, which promises to show 'exactly the men who turn up in June', computes walk-ons for four starters. June then needs a fifth: it consumes an arm the projection had counted for the pen, and draws an extra walk-on from the shared season rng (roster.ts:218 fallback) that was never shown. regroup also demotes the fifth starter to the pen for the whole draft-to-signing stretch. The NEEDS tab, the staff's suggested list, the 'needs' recruiting focus and the Draft screen's loss check all ignore the fifth starter.
- **How to reproduce:** Engine: `npx tsx walkOnLong2.ts long` and `npx tsx walkOnLong2.ts standard,short` (createSeason with configForRules({length}), 24 teams x 3 seeds, varied classes, departAndDevelop; walkOnShortfall/walkOnClass projections for every team vs the walk-ons fillRosters actually adds). Store: `npx tsx walkOnStore.ts` (start(seed, team, ..., {length:'long'}), season, nextPhase to 'signing', SigningDay.tsx:112's exact walkOnClass call, leave signing, compare with lastOffseason.walkOns). Both in the scratch dir.
- **Expected behavior:** In every world the Signing Day review lists the walk-ons June brings. NEEDS and the staff list count a fifth starter as a hole when the world needs five.
- **Actual behavior:** Engine, long world: in 49 of 72 team-winters June manufactures a walk-on never shown (49 men). Standard and short worlds: 0 of 72 each. Store: 4 of 4 sampled long-world careers get one extra walk-on, e.g. 'seed 4242 team 0 long: Signing Day showed 5 walk-ons [1B,1B,SS,2B,3B]; June brought 6 [1B,SS,1B,2B,3B,RP]; never shown: 1; rotation now 5'. The same seeds in a standard world show 'never shown: 0'.
- **Root cause:** The rule is encoded as a default parameter (`rotationSize = ROTATION_SIZE`) in walkOnShortfall, holesFor, refill and makeTeam, and as a literal ROTATION_SIZE in depthShortfall, regroup and Draft.tsx. The defaults let every caller compile without stating the world's rotation size.
- **Recommended fix:** Remove the defaults and pass rotationSizeFor(season.config) (or the season) through walkOnClass -> walkOnShortfall, holesFor, depthShortfall, regroup, suggestedStaffList, programRecruitingPlan and Draft.tsx's loss check. Then extend tests/progression.test.ts:581 ('projects on signing day exactly the men who turn up in June') to iterate SEASON_SPANS and several team indices instead of team 0 in a standard world. *(Verifier's note: The smallest fix is to thread `rotationSizeFor(season.config)` into walkOnClass, which then passes it to walkOnShortfall, and from SigningDay.tsx:112, Board.tsx:335/338/361, store.ts:309 and Draft.tsx:241. depthShortfall and regroup need a rotationSize parameter in place of the literal. Removing the default parameters lets the compiler find every caller.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/progression.ts`, `src/engine/roster.ts`, `src/ui/screens/SigningDay.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Board.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Draft.tsx`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/recruitingPlan.ts`
- **Risk:** Long-season careers are told which walk-ons are coming and then receive another arm they were never shown, a non-deterministic draw instead of the previewed one. Recruiting NEEDS understates pitching need by a starter, the staff's list and the +10% 'needs' focus ignore it, and the Draft screen reports 'covered' when the rotation will be short.

#### M13. News front page re-sorts the wire by weight, undoing the engine's interleave, so 8 identical 'upset' stories run back to back

*Area: copy-generated · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** News front page re-sorts the wire by weight, undoing the engine's interleave, so 8 identical 'upset' stories run back to back
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Wire.tsx:67-80 (items useMemo) vs src/engine/wire.ts:370 + interleave() 384-407
- **Problem:** wire() trims each kind to a cap and then interleaves kinds round-robin, because, in its own comments, a straight weight sort 'reads terribly: upsets carry the biggest numbers, so the first eight items were all upsets'. The Wire screen then sorts the interleaved list again by weight plus boosts (`[...wire(season)].sort((a,b) => score(b) - score(a))`), which brings back the clustering. Every upset carries the same detail sentence, so the first screen of News is one template eight times.

- **Root cause:** Wire.tsx:79 applies a full weight sort after wire() has already interleaved.
- **Recommended fix:** Keep wire()'s order and lift only the boosted stories with a stable partition (e.g. mine first, then followed, then conference, otherwise wire order), or pass the boosts into wire() before interleave(). *(Verifier's note: Keep wire()'s order and apply the boosts as a stable partition (mine, then followed, then conference, then the rest, each in wire order). Alternatively, pass the boosts into wire() before interleave().)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Wire.tsx`, `src/engine/wire.ts`
- **Risk:** The main news page reads as robotic and repetitive every day of every season.

#### M18. Screen under every overlay, sheet and dialog stays focusable and readable by screen readers; covered controls can be activated (table overlays also take no focus and ignore Escape)

*Area: design-system-a11y · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Screen under every overlay, sheet and dialog stays focusable and readable by screen readers; covered controls can be activated (table overlays also take no focus and ignore Escape)
- **Location:** src/ui/App.tsx:1020-1062 (TableOverlay renders <div className="pb-tableoverlay"> with no role/aria-modal/focus handling); in-season frame src/ui/App.tsx:789-870 (SchoolHeader, SectionTabs, main.app-content, AreaNav never get inert); same pattern in every frame that renders <Overlays /> (App.tsx:469/508/532/678/759/778/866); Sheet src/ui/components/ui/layout.tsx:400, Modal src/ui/Modal.tsx:112, Overlay src/ui/Overlay.tsx:99 rely on aria-modal only
- **Problem:** When Settings, Saves, Inbox, Schedule, Rankings, Standings, Captain, Jobs, Book or any room (coach, network, watchlist, staff...) is opened, the full-screen 'table overlay' is a plain div: it is not a dialog, focus is not moved into it, Escape does nothing, and the home/tab screen it covers is neither inert nor aria-hidden. Keyboard focus therefore walks into invisible controls behind it and can activate them. For sheets and dialogs (role=dialog aria-modal=true) the Tab trap works, but Chromium still exposes the whole page behind them in the accessibility tree, so TalkBack swipe navigation reads (and double-tap activates) the hidden header, Play ball / Sim week buttons and bottom nav. The overlay is rendered after the page in DOM order, so a TalkBack user swiping through Settings hears the entire hidden Home screen first.
- **How to reproduce:** NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node scratchpad/agents/design-system-a11y/a11y3.cjs (and a11y2.cjs). Start a career, close the season plan, tap the inbox ball (Inbox overlay covers the frame), press Tab three times: focus goes Coach menu -> Today -> News, all covered by the overlay (elementFromPoint does not hit them). Press Enter.
- **Expected behavior:** While a layer is up, everything beneath it is inert (not focusable, not in the accessibility tree); the overlay takes focus on open, traps Tab, closes on Escape, and returns focus to the opener.
- **Actual behavior:** a11y3.cjs output: 'Tab path from bell: [BUTTON "Coach menu", BUTTON "Today", BUTTON "News"]' then 'before {tab:home, screen:today, overlay:inbox} after Enter on covered control {tab:home, screen:wire, overlay:inbox}' - the hidden screen changed under the Inbox. AX tree while Settings is open: 'Sim week 4 games left' ignored=false focusable=true; with the Season plan Sheet (aria-modal) open the AX tree still exposes 'Home','Team','Play ball Coach it live','Sim week 4 games left'. a11y2.cjs: for settings/inbox/schedule/coach overlays focus stays on BODY after open, overlayRole=null, overlayModal=null, mainInert=false, and 'after Escape overlay= settings' (Escape ignored).
- **Root cause:** Only the overlay slots BELOW the top one are made inert (App.tsx:1062 inert={!top}); nothing inerts the frame chrome and <main> beneath the top layer. TableOverlay does not use useDialogFocus (Overlay.tsx and Sheet do), and aria-modal alone is not honoured by Chromium's accessibility tree.
- **Recommended fix:** 1) In each app-frame branch of App.tsx, compute layerUp = overlay !== null || a sheet/dialog/fulloverlay is mounted (e.g. a small store flag set by useDialogFocus register/release, or a MutationObserver on .app-frame for .pb-sheet-host/.pb-dialog-host/.pb-tableoverlay/.pb-fulloverlay) and render SchoolHeader, SaveAlert, SectionTabs, main.app-content and AreaNav inside a wrapper with inert={layerUp || undefined}. 2) Give .pb-tableoverlay role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label={overlay title} and call useDialogFocus(ref, back, { layer: false }) in TableOverlay so focus moves to its Back button, Tab is trapped and Escape closes. 3) Add a Playwright/RTL regression asserting the frame is inert while overlay !== null. *(Verifier's note: Only the aria-modal part (Sheet, Modal, Overlay leaking the page to screen readers) was measured in desktop headless Chromium through CDP. Android WebView/TalkBack handling of aria-modal is not verified. The table-overlay part holds either way, because .pb-tableoverlay has no role or aria-modal and nothing under it is inert, so TalkBack reaches the covered Sim week / Play ball nodes regardless. The fix as proposed is right. The cheapest version: wrap the frame chrome and main in an element with inert={overlay !== null || undefined}, and add role=dialog, aria-modal and useDialogFocus(ref, back, {layer:false}) to TableSlot when it is top.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/App.tsx`, `src/ui/components/ui/layout.tsx`, `src/ui/Modal.tsx`, `src/ui/Overlay.tsx`, `src/ui/dialogFocus.ts`
- **Risk:** Screen-reader and hardware-keyboard/Chromebook users can trigger Sim week / Play ball / tab changes they cannot see (unintended season progression), and TalkBack navigation of every overlay starts by reading the hidden page; Play Store accessibility pre-launch reports will flag it.

#### M19. 'Larger' text size breaks the Home action row on 360-dp phones (labels hard-clipped, no ellipsis); fixed px line-heights and unpinned Android font scale make it worse

*Area: design-system-a11y · Evidence: both · verifier: **plausible***

- **Issue:** 'Larger' text size breaks the Home action row on 360-dp phones (labels hard-clipped, no ellipsis); fixed px line-heights and unpinned Android font scale make it worse
- **Location:** src/ui/design/screens.css:843 (.pb-home__actlabel is display:flex with text-overflow:ellipsis), screens.css:835-841 (.pb-home__actions 1fr/1.35fr/1fr grid), screens.css:790 (.pb-gcard__name b overflow-wrap:anywhere); design/*.css 374 font rules with fixed px line-heights; index.html:12 (maximum-scale=1); native/android/com/playball/dynasty/MainActivity.java (no WebSettings.setTextZoom)
- **Problem:** Settings > Display > Text size 'Larger' (textScale 1.3, the documented maximum) on a 360x640 phone - the most common Android width - clips the two side buttons of Home's three-button bar to 'Sim gam' and 'Sim weel' with no ellipsis, breaks team names mid-word on the game wheel ('Thiboda ux...', 'Alleghe ny') and squeezes to-do titles to one word per line. The ellipsis never appears because text-overflow does not apply to a flex container's text. Pinch zoom is disabled (maximum-scale=1) and the APK does not pin WebView textZoom, so Android's system font size multiplies on top of the in-app size; emulating that combined scale (1.69 = Larger x Android 130%, 2.0 = Android 200%) makes all three Home buttons clip and lines overlap across the header, wheel cards and to-dos, because 374 design-system font declarations use fixed px line-heights (59 of them already exceed their line-height at Larger, e.g. .pb-profile__name 28px/32px -> 36.4px font on a 32px line).
- **How to reproduce:** NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node scratchpad/agents/design-system-a11y/scale.cjs (sets prefs textScale, phone 'small' = 360x640; forced scales set --pb-ts/--ts after load). Or manually: Settings > Display > Text size Larger on a 360-dp phone, open Home.
- **Expected behavior:** At every offered text size on a 360-dp phone, button labels either fit (wrap to two lines / smaller meta) or end in an ellipsis; words never break mid-word; line boxes grow with the font.
- **Actual behavior:** scale.cjs: 'small-1.3 today acts [{label:"Sim game",clipped:true},{label:"Play ball",clipped:false},{label:"Sim week",clipped:true}] hardClipped 6 [... {text:"Sim game",cls:"pb-home__actlabel",ellipsis:false,display:"flex",over:11}]'; 'pixel7-x2 today acts [all three clipped:true] ... {text:"Sim game",display:"flex",over:47}'. Normal size and pixel7 Larger are clean (hardClipped 0).
- **Root cause:** .pb-home__actlabel { display:flex; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis } - ellipsis is ignored on flex containers, and the 1fr/1.35fr/1fr grid gives each side button ~105px at 360dp. .pb-gcard__name b uses overflow-wrap:anywhere inside a 2-line clamp. Line-heights are written as fixed px next to calc(Npx * var(--pb-ts)) font sizes, so they do not scale. Android WebView applies the system font scale via textZoom unless the app sets it, which MainActivity does not.
- **Recommended fix:** Wrap the label text in its own span: <span class="pb-home__actlabel"><Icon/><span class="pb-ellipsis">Sim game</span></span> with .pb-ellipsis{min-width:0;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;white-space:nowrap}, or let the label wrap to two lines (white-space:normal; text-align:center) and drop the meta line at --pb-ts>1.15. Replace overflow-wrap:anywhere with overflow-wrap:normal; hyphens:auto in .pb-gcard__name b. Convert fixed line-heights to unitless (e.g. calc(15px*var(--pb-ts))/1.45) or calc(Npx*var(--pb-ts)). Decide the Android policy explicitly: either call bridge.getWebView().getSettings().setTextZoom(100) in MainActivity and add an 'Extra large' in-app size, or keep system scaling and test layouts at 1.69-2.0. *(Verifier's note: Restate it as: (a) the game-card names break mid-word at Larger on 360dp with DM Sans (screens.css:790 overflow-wrap:anywhere; use overflow-wrap:normal or break-word with hyphens:auto). (b) The Home buttons have no ellipsis fallback (screens.css:843, flex container) and about 3px of slack at Larger. They clip as soon as Android's system font scale stacks on top, if WebView applies it. Set an explicit textZoom policy in MainActivity and put the label text in its own ellipsis span. Repro with real fonts: scratchpad/agents/verify-design-system-a11y/font2-v.cjs and font3-v.cjs.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/design/screens.css`, `src/ui/design/components.css`, `src/ui/screens/Today.tsx`, `index.html`, `native/android/com/playball/dynasty/MainActivity.java`
- **Risk:** Low-vision players who pick the largest size (the only accessibility size control, since pinch zoom is off) get truncated core commands on the most common Android screen width; with Android font scaling the Home screen becomes hard to read.

#### M20. Win/loss goes to the wrong pitchers when a lead is tied and the same team retakes it (no reset on a tie)

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Win/loss goes to the wrong pitchers when a lead is tied and the same team retakes it (no reset on a tie)
- **Location:** src/engine/game.ts:718-726 (simGame onScore) and src/engine/liveGame.ts:283-289 (managed-game onScore)
- **Problem:** onScore only records a lead change when the batting team goes ahead and `leadHolder !== bat`. It never clears leadHolder when the trailing team ties the game. If team A leads, B ties, and A goes ahead again, `leadHolder === bat` is still true. The win then stays with A's pitcher of record from the first lead, and the loss with the B pitcher who gave up that first lead. The rule (and the GameResult docstring: 'the lead it never gave back') says a tie starts a new contest: the win goes to the pitcher of record when the final lead was taken, and the loss to the pitcher charged with the go-ahead run.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/game-sim/boxsweep.ts (6 seeds x 400 games, real season teams with playGame-equivalent options). It replays every game through a copy of simGame's loop with a rulebook pitcher-of-record tracker; same RNG, identical scores verified. Concrete case: seed 1001 game 29 (rng 100029), SDL@GAL, `npx tsx one.ts 1 29`.
- **Expected behavior:** In seed1001/game29, SDL led 4-0, the game was tied 4-4 after the 7th, and SDL went back ahead 6-4 in the 8th on Landon Saunders' HR off Joaquin Medina. Correct decisions: W Agustin Kavanagh (SDL pitcher of record in the 8th), L Joaquin Medina.
- **Actual behavior:** Shipped: W Takeshi Weber (the SDL starter who gave up the tying runs), L Stuart Kramer (the GAL starter, whose runs had been erased by the tie). Over 2,400 games, 712 had a lead tied and retaken by the same team. W differed from the rulebook in 155 games (6.5%) and L in 200 (8.3%).
- **Root cause:** `if (bat.runs <= fld.runs) return;` treats a tying run like any non-lead run, and `if (leadHolder === bat) return;` then treats the retaken lead as 'already ahead'. Both copies (game.ts and liveGame.ts) share the defect, so simulated and managed games are both affected.
- **Recommended fix:** In both onScore closures, after scoring: if bat.runs === fld.runs set leadHolder = null (also creditTo/blameTo = null). Only then apply the existing lead-change branch. Better still, extract one shared decision tracker into game.ts so the two copies cannot drift again. Add a scripted-engine test: A scores, B ties, A retakes after a pitching change, then assert W/L. *(Verifier's note: In both onScore closures, add before the existing checks: `if (bat.runs === fld.runs) { leadHolder = null; creditTo = null; blameTo = null; return; }`. Better: extract one shared decision tracker so the copies in game.ts and liveGame.ts cannot drift. This changes recorded decisions in the goldens, so expect to re-bless them.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/game.ts`, `src/engine/liveGame.ts`
- **Risk:** Season and career W/L, win records in the record book, Pitcher of the Year voting and player cards are wrong in about 1 game in 14, permanently, for every program in every season.

#### M21. Simulated games judge pitcher rest 1-3 days in the future, so tired starters and relievers pitch early with no short-rest penalty

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Simulated games judge pitcher rest 1-3 days in the future, so tired starters and relievers pitch early with no short-rest penalty
- **Location:** src/engine/season.ts:2739 (simNextDay increments season.dayIndex before playing the day), playGame season.ts:2238-2256 (restedFirst, startableSlot, shortRest called with currentDay(season)), restedFirst season.ts:2117
- **Problem:** simNextDay does `season.dayIndex += 1` before it calls playGame for the day's games. Inside playGame, currentDay(season) therefore returns the next scheduled date, or firstPostseasonDay (last day + 3) on the final regular-season day. Every readiness check uses that date: pitcherReady in restedFirst, startableSlot, and shortRest. Workloads are recorded on the game's real date (opts.day), so arms are cleared 1-3 days before their recovery gap ends. The managed path (startManagedGame) computes `today` before the increment, so managed and simulated games apply different rest rules. The Today screen's probable-starter card, which also uses the true date, can name a different starter from the one the simulation then uses.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/game-sim/restclock.ts (seed 11) replays a full season day by day. For each side it compares startableSlot/restedFirst/shortRest at the date playGame reads against the game's own date. agents/game-sim/rotcase2.ts shows the RWL day-27 case.
- **Expected behavior:** Rest is judged on the date the game is played. Rossi (56 pitches on day 26, recoveryGap 3) is not available on day 27, so the slot walks to Callum Santiago. Any short-rest start gets the 70% budget.
- **Actual behavior:** Read-ahead: 1 day for 1,056 games, 2 days for 528, 3 days for 576 (all 2,160 games). On day 27, currentDay=29, so Rossi starts on 1 day of rest. In one season: 28 starts by an arm the game's own date would have skipped (e.g. 'day 29 CHS: starts Jose Pritchard (124p on day 27, needs 5 days)'), none flagged shortRest, and in 2,129 of 4,320 team-games (49%) the available bullpen included arms not yet recovered.
- **Root cause:** currentDay() reads season.schedule[season.dayIndex], and simNextDay advances dayIndex before playing the games. playGame passes opts.day only to recordResult, never to the readiness helpers.
- **Recommended fix:** Thread the game date through: in playGame use `const today = opts.day ?? currentDay(season)` for startableSlot and shortRest. Give restedFirst (and closerFrom's input) a `day` parameter defaulting to currentDay(season), and pass today. Alternatively compute everything before the increment in simNextDay. Add a regression test that simulates two days and asserts a 100-pitch starter does not start again before recoveryGap(100) days on the real calendar. *(Verifier's note: Thread the game date through instead of reading currentDay after the increment. In playGame, use `const today = opts.day ?? currentDay(season)` for startableSlot and shortRest. Add a `day` parameter to restedFirst (default currentDay(season)) and pass today. Alternatively compute starters and pens before the increment in simNextDay.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/season.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Today.tsx`
- **Risk:** Most games are simulated, so the workload and rest system the Lineup and Today screens explain is systematically 1-3 days more lenient than stated. Managed and simulated games disagree. The probable-starter card can be wrong for the coached team.

#### M22. Out-of-position fielders are judged by their roster label, not the spot they stand at (no throwing errors, ball drawn at the wrong station)

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Out-of-position fielders are judged by their roster label, not the spot they stand at (no throwing errors, ball drawn at the wrong station)
- **Location:** src/engine/game.ts:2131-2141 throwRisk (reads fielder.pos), game.ts:1924 landingFor (POSITION_SPOT[fielder.pos]), game.ts:460 recalculateDefense (FIELDING_SHARE[p.pos]), game.ts:1374 HR text (fielder?.pos); byPosition filled via positions.ts:222 fieldingAt, which keeps `pos` unchanged
- **Problem:** TeamState fits the nine to positions by cost and stores fieldingAt(man, spot) in byPosition. fieldingAt returns the man, or a ratings-reduced copy, with his roster `pos` unchanged. Several consumers then read that label instead of the spot. throwRisk returns 0 for any LF/CF/RF/DH label, so an outfielder or DH-labelled man standing on the infield never throws a ball away. landingFor draws the ball at the label's station, so a grounder to second fielded by a 3B-labelled man is drawn at third, and one fielded by an RF-labelled man is drawn in right field. Fielding shares and the HR direction text also use the label. Only the out text was fixed, via standingAt (game.ts:1849).
- **How to reproduce:** agents/game-sim/oop.ts: 96 teams x 20 games, each card with a bench OF written into the 2B batting slot. This is what a manual swapStarter produces, because it deliberately does not relabel. agents/game-sim/restcheck.ts counts the label/spot mismatches that occur naturally in AI seasons.
- **Expected behavior:** An outfielder standing at 3B carries at least the infield throw risk (more, since he is out of position), and a ground out to second is drawn at second.
- **Actual behavior:** OF/DH-labelled men on the infield: 0 throwing errors in 3,239 chances, against 300 in 16,809 (1.8%) for natives. 4,371 of 7,979 ground outs (55%) were drawn more than 0.25 field units from the station the play-by-play names (e.g. 'MOB: Ira Ruiz (label RF) stands at 3B; throwRisk 0.0000'). In ordinary simulated seasons (seed 11, 2,160 games): 547 OF-labelled infielders and 1,463 DH-labelled men fielding (mostly at 1B, throwRisk 0, ball drawn at the DH station (0, 0.30)).
- **Root cause:** byPosition values are Player objects whose `pos` is the roster label, and four consumers read `.pos` as if it were the fielded spot.
- **Recommended fix:** When filling byPosition (constructor, pinchHit, coverPitcher), store `{ ...fieldingAt(man, spot), pos: spot }`, or pass the spot explicitly to throwRisk/landingFor/recalculateDefense and the HR text. standingAt then becomes unnecessary. Keep identity comparisons on id, which they already use. *(Verifier's note: When filling byPosition (constructor, pinchHit, coverPitcher, and the moundBound cover), store `{ ...fieldingAt(man, spot), pos: spot }`. Identity checks already use id, and standingAt becomes redundant. throwRisk short-circuits its rng() draw when risk is 0, so the fix shifts the random stream and the goldens.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/game.ts`, `src/engine/positions.ts`
- **Risk:** Covers, injury replacements and manual card edits make the defence better at throwing rather than worse, contrary to the positions design. In managed games with a mismatched card, the field animation contradicts the play-by-play on a large share of ground balls.

#### M23. Home/Today cannot scroll, so in split-screen, pop-up windows and phone landscape the Sim game / Play ball / Sim week buttons are clipped or hidden and the to-do list shrinks to 10 px

*Area: gap-android-display-matrix · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Home/Today cannot scroll, so in split-screen, pop-up windows and phone landscape the Sim game / Play ball / Sim week buttons are clipped or hidden and the to-do list shrinks to 10 px
- **Location:** src/ui/design/screens.css:744-747 (.pb-page.pb-home {height:100%; overflow:hidden}, with the comment 'the page never scrolls'), :755 (.pb-wheel {flex:none; height:clamp(190px,30vh,290px)}), :810/:816 (.pb-home__todo / __todolist flex:1; min-height:0), :835 (.pb-home__actions flex:none); src/ui/screens/Today.tsx:453 (<main className="pb-page pb-home">) and :508 (actions row); src/ui/tokens.css:345-360 (.app-frame overflow:hidden). Same squeeze in the live game: screens.css:199-201 (.pb-live__scene height:34vh; min-height:150px) and :210 (.pb-live__panel)
- **Problem:** Home is a fixed column with no scroller other than the to-do list: app bar (53 px), top tabs (~45 px), the game wheel (at least 190 px, flex:none), the to-do header, the three action buttons (71 px, flex:none) and the bottom tab bar (69 px). When the window is shorter than about 480 px, the fixed rows are taller than the page box. The to-do list shrinks to nothing first, then the action row is pushed past the bottom of .pb-page.pb-home and clipped by its overflow:hidden. Nothing on the screen can scroll the buttons back into view. Height limits like this occur in Android split-screen and pop-up windows on any phone (the generated manifest has no resizeableActivity=false, so multi-window is on by default), and in phone landscape, which is reachable because orientation is not locked.
- **How to reproduce:** Dev server, start a career (seed 4242, team 3), sim one week and close the covers. Resize the viewport while keeping the same state (agents/gap-android-display-matrix/probe-home-short.cjs, run with the DejaVu fallback and again with FONT=dm, the real DM Sans). For each size, measure how many px of each 54 px action button sit inside the page box, and the height of the to-do list.
- **Expected behavior:** Every Home control stays reachable at any window height, either by scrolling the page or by keeping the action row pinned while the wheel and to-do list scroll.
- **Actual behavior:** 412x915: buttons 54/54 px visible, to-do list 337 px. 412x560: 54/54, list 66 px. 412x480 (split-screen): 54/54, list 10 px (the 'Let them finish' / 'Name a captain' musts cannot be reached). 412x420 (split-screen): buttons 23/54 px, only their top half shows above the tab bar, list 10 px. 915x412 landscape: 15/54. 867x388 (landscape minus the status and navigation bars): 0/54, so Sim game, Play ball and Sim week are completely hidden and the season cannot be advanced from Home until the phone is rotated back. Live game at 412x420: the call panel is 136 px and 0 of 5 calls are fully visible (2 of 5 at 412x480). This extends the known landscape 79 px finding to split-screen.
- **Root cause:** The Home stylesheet makes the page non-scrolling by design ('Three parts, and the page never scrolls', screens.css:744) and sizes the wheel and the action row as flex:none fixed boxes. The design assumes a viewport of at least about 560 px. No max-height media query or scroll fallback exists for shorter windows, and .app-frame is overflow:hidden, so the overflow is clipped instead of scrolled.
- **Recommended fix:** Add a short-window fallback, for example: @media (max-height: 560px) { .pb-page.pb-home { overflow-y: auto; } .pb-wheel { height: 168px; } .pb-home__todo, .pb-home__todolist { flex: none; overflow: visible; } .pb-home__actions { position: sticky; bottom: 0; z-index: 3; } }. Do the same for the live game: in the same query, let .pb-live__scene drop to height: 28vh; min-height: 96px, so the call grid keeps at least two rows. Separately, add android:screenOrientation="portrait" in scripts/apk.cjs (the android-release finding). Do not rely on the lock alone: it does not stop multi-window on phones, and Android 16 ignores orientation locks on screens of 600 dp or wider for apps targeting API 36. *(Verifier's note: Overlaps the known landscape/orientation finding (brief line 93-94). What this finding adds is split-screen/pop-up windows of 420 px or less and the to-do list collapsing below about 480 px. The fix should not lean on the orientation lock alone. The proposed max-height:560px fallback, with a sticky action row and a scrollable page, is reasonable.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/design/screens.css`, `src/ui/screens/Today.tsx`, `src/ui/tokens.css`, `src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx`
- **Risk:** A player who rotates the phone with auto-rotate on, or uses split-screen or a pop-up window, sees a Home screen with no working primary actions and an empty to-do list. This reads as a broken game. Pending-game and lineup 'musts' sit in the collapsed list.

#### M24. Haptics are dead in the APK: no VIBRATE permission, so every navigator.vibrate call is silently dropped by WebView

*Area: gap-android-lifecycle-media · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Haptics are dead in the APK: no VIBRATE permission, so every navigator.vibrate call is silently dropped by WebView
- **Location:** src/ui/sound.ts:216-222 buzz(); scripts/apk.cjs (no manifest patch); generated android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
- **Problem:** All haptics go through buzz() → navigator.vibrate(). The APK does not declare android.permission.VIBRATE. Chromium's Android vibration service checks that permission once at construction and, without it, only logs a warning and never calls Vibrator.vibrate(). It also skips vibration whenever the ringer is in RINGER_MODE_SILENT. So in the shipped APK the Settings 'Haptics' switch (Settings.tsx:257-261, 'Taps on contact and outs'), every per-play buzz in Manage.tsx:285-321, BigMoment, Awards, Portal, Legacy and the long-press tick in useLongPress.ts:66 do nothing, on every device. The store listing still advertises 'Sound, haptics' (16-store-listing.md:44).
- **How to reproduce:** 1) aapt2 dump permissions scratchpad/apkbuild/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk → INTERNET, BILLING, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION; no VIBRATE. 2) Read Chromium services/device/vibration/android/.../VibrationManagerAndroid.java (fetched to agents/gap-android-lifecycle-media/VibrationManagerAndroid.java). 3) In Playwright with navigator.vibrate instrumented (media.cjs), the JS does call vibrate once per play, e.g. [25,40,60] on a homer, so the calls are made and the platform drops them.
- **Expected behavior:** With Haptics on, the phone buzzes on contact, outs and big moments as Settings and the listing promise.
- **Actual behavior:** No vibration ever happens in the APK. The switch toggles a preference that has no effect.
- **Root cause:** The Capacitor template manifest has no VIBRATE, and scripts/apk.cjs never patches AndroidManifest.xml (grep finds no 'manifest' or 'permission' in it). VibrationManagerAndroid.java:37-41 sets mHasVibratePermission = checkCallingOrSelfPermission(VIBRATE)==GRANTED and logs 'Failed to use vibrate API, requires VIBRATE permission.'. Lines 59-61 then vibrate only if getRingerMode()!=RINGER_MODE_SILENT && mHasVibratePermission.
- **Recommended fix:** In scripts/apk.cjs, after `cap add/sync`, insert `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.VIBRATE" />` into android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml. VIBRATE is a normal install-time permission with no prompt. Another option is to add @capacitor/haptics, which declares VIBRATE and is not subject to the ringer check. Update docs/privacy.md's 'requests no runtime permissions' line only if needed (VIBRATE is not a runtime permission). Optionally note in the Haptics row that a silent ringer suppresses haptics. *(Verifier's note: Separately, even with VIBRATE added, the WebView path still skips vibration when the ringer is set to silent. @capacitor/haptics avoids that check, so it is the more robust fix.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/sound.ts`, `scripts/apk.cjs`, `src/ui/screens/Settings.tsx`, `docs/16-store-listing.md`
- **Risk:** An advertised feature and a Settings switch are non-functional on every Android install. Users and reviewers will see a dead toggle.

#### M25. An app update (or any engine change) between a crash-journal write and its resume silently replays a different game and presents it as the one the player left

*Area: gap-android-lifecycle-media · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** An app update (or any engine change) between a crash-journal write and its resume silently replays a different game and presents it as the one the player left
- **Location:** src/state/liveJournal.ts LiveJournal interface + journalMatches() (~line 200); src/state/store.ts resumeGame (8285-8345), pendingFromJournal (2498-2515)
- **Problem:** The live-game journal anchors only slot, year and rngState, plus the teams, starters and flags. It records no build or engine version. Play's auto-update kills the process. If it does so while a managed game is interrupted, the next launch replays the recorded calls through the new engine. Any change to a constant, a draw order or a tactic table gives a different game. The resume card ('Pick it up') and the reopened dugout present that game as the one the player left, with no warning. Calls that no longer apply are skipped by design.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/gap-android-lifecycle-media/update-midgame.mts: copy src to srcmod and change ratings.ts LEAGUE_K_RATE 0.19→0.23. With the shipped store: start(4242,10), startManagedGame, submit 25 tactics, record the live state. Then load the same slot with the srcmod store (shared fake IDB and localStorage), loadSlot → pendingGame → resumeGame(true). Run: `npx tsx --import ./register.mjs update-midgame.mts` with MOD=0 (same engine, control) and MOD=1 (updated engine).
- **Expected behavior:** The resumed game is identical to the one interrupted. If the engine changed, the journal is either refused with a notice ('this game could not be picked up after the update') or the game is replayed from its anchor with the player told.
- **Actual behavior:** MOD=0: identical (inning 3, 5-3, 40 log lines, same log). MOD=1: the player left a 5-3 game in the top of the 3rd. The pick-up offered the same matchup ('Chicopee Mills at Hattiesburg') and reopened the dugout at 0-2 in the bottom of the 3rd with 33 log lines. The log diverges at line 2, and nothing tells the player.
- **Root cause:** liveJournal.ts journalMatches(j, slot, year, rngState) returns j.slot===slot && j.year===year && j.rngState===rngState. No engine or build identity is written in writeJournal (store.ts ~8500 writes slot/year/rngState/home/away/day/starters/managing/flags/actions only). resumeGame then deliberately tolerates divergence: 'A call that no longer applies is skipped rather than forced'.
- **Recommended fix:** Add `build: string` (the app version from package.json via a Vite define, or an ENGINE_VERSION constant bumped with any sim change) to LiveJournal. In journalMatches/pendingFromJournal, a mismatch should refuse the replay. Either finish the day without the player (as resumeGame(false) does) or show 'The app updated while this game was paused; it was played out without you' rather than handing over a different game. Optionally store a short hash of the expected log length/score at each action so a replay can detect divergence and stop. *(Verifier's note: Stamp an ENGINE_VERSION in writeJournal and check it in journalMatches. On a mismatch, finish the game without the player and tell them, instead of replaying the old calls.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/liveJournal.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** After a Play update the first managed game a player returns to can show a different score and situation, presented as the game in progress. It quietly breaks the 'same game' guarantee the journal exists for, and the result counts in the standings.

*Area: gap-player-attributes · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Location:** src/engine/badges.ts:474 growthBonus; src/engine/progression.ts:540-627 growthFor/develop call
- **Problem:** growthBonus(p) = 1 + badgeSize(p,'gymRat')*2.2 is exported but nothing calls it. departAndDevelop passes growthFor(p) + growthFromCulture(p) into develop(), and neither includes the badge. So the badge changes nothing. It is also the most common innate badge (141 holders at the start of seed 777, 163 after 10 winters), and the card says 'Develops faster between seasons'.

Do the same in ageIntoClass if generated upperclassmen should benefit. Add a test asserting that develop's mean gain is higher with gymRat on the same rng stream. *(Verifier's note: Wire growthBonus(p) into the growthMult that progression.ts departAndDevelop passes to develop() (and into ageIntoClass if wanted). Add a test that pins the rng stream and asserts a higher mean gain with gymRat held.)*
