#### M29. CROWDS THE PLATE is several times stronger than any other regular-season badge, and the most common earned one

*Area: gap-player-attributes · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** CROWDS THE PLATE is several times stronger than any other regular-season badge, and the most common earned one
- **Location:** src/engine/badges.ts:420-422 (badgeMods), 324-330 (crowdsThePlate spec)
- **Problem:** Badges are sized so a gold STEADY badge moves its channel by about 7%. CROWDS THE PLATE multiplies HBP by 1+size*4 and walks by 1+size*3. The comment justifies only the HBP multiplier, which it calls 'a third of the size of a walk's effect'. The extra x3 on walks (an event ten times as common as an HBP) makes it the biggest lever in the catalogue. It is also earned at hbp>=6, which an ordinary regular reaches, so it grew from 63 holders to 234 in 10 winters.
- **How to reproduce:** cd scratchpad/agents/gap-player-attributes && N=8000 npx tsx ab.ts (same 13 hitters with vs without the gold badge, paired seeds).
- **Expected behavior:** About +1-2% team runs, similar to LIGHT TOWER (+2.5% RS) or WHEELS (+2.2% RS).
- **Actual behavior:** crowdsThePlate: BB/PA +21.6%, HBP/PA +33.9%, runs +16.6%, +6.7 win points. For comparison: getsHimIn +10.1% RS / +3.5 pts, lightTower +2.5% / +0.9 pts, toughOut +0.2% / -0.8 pts.
- **Root cause:** The walk multiplier `m.walk *= 1 + badgeSize(batter,'crowdsThePlate') * 3.0` triples the badge's nominal size on a common event. That, plus an easy earn rule (hbp>=6) and no rarity check.
- **Recommended fix:** Drop the walk term to the nominal size (`1 + size`), or remove it, keeping only the HBP lift. Raise the earn bar (e.g. hbp >= 9 and hbp/PA >= 5%). Re-run the traits.test 'what badges are worth' trial with this badge alone. *(Verifier's note: The more useful lever is the earn rule (hbp>=6 in a season, with no rate floor), which drives the proliferation. Tune walk*3 only after re-running the league walk-rate check in docs/05 §18.5, since the term exists to offset PAINTER.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/badges.ts`
- **Risk:** Badge-driven drift in walk and run environments over a long dynasty: holders accumulate, and the strongest offensive badge is the easiest to earn.

#### M30. Freshmen the coach redshirts go into the transfer portal saying 'He was told he would play' (6 of 18, against 1 of 30 other freshmen)

*Area: gap-player-lifecycle-trace · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Freshmen the coach redshirts go into the transfer portal saying 'He was told he would play' (6 of 18, against 1 of 30 other freshmen)
- **Location:** src/engine/portal.ts:135 entersPortal, :204 reasonFor; src/engine/morale.ts:74 expectationOf; called from src/state/store.ts nextPhase (portal opening, openPortal)
- **Problem:** A redshirt is a planned year out: the player sits on purpose, 0.85x development, and the coach gets a fifth year back. entersPortal and reasonFor check his starts against expectationOf(squadRank) the same way they check a man who was simply benched. A redshirted man has 0 starts by rule, so the 'buried' penalty (expected minus actual) is at its largest, and he walks out of the program at the end of the very season the coach redshirted him. The only redshirt check in portal.ts is for the noRedshirt promise (line 198).
- **How to reproduce:** agents/gap-player-lifecycle-trace/probe-redshirt-portal.ts: for each of 6 seeds, start a Full career at team 0, setRedshirt(true) at day 0 on up to 3 freshmen, finish the season and June through the store's bracket actions, nextPhase to 'portal', then read portal.leaving. Run: npx tsx --import ./register.mjs probe-redshirt-portal.ts
- **Expected behavior:** A man the coach chose to redshirt is not judged as buried for that season (or is judged much more gently), so redshirting does not push him into the portal.
- **Actual behavior:** 6 of 18 redshirted freshmen entered the portal, every one with the reason 'He was told he would play.' Only 1 of 30 freshmen who were not redshirted entered. The 5-season trace saw it happen naturally too: the tracked 'FR redshirt' (Manny Bainbridge, seed 4242) was in the portal the winter after his redshirt year, reason 'He was told he would play', and keepFromPortal(…, 6) did not hold him.
- **Root cause:** expectationOf and the buried and reason channels in entersPortal and reasonFor never read the redshirt flag. The flag is still set when openPortal runs: departAndDevelop banks it only for survivors, and openPortal reads the rosters after that, but starts/games is still 0/N for the sat season.
- **Recommended fix:** In entersPortal (and reasonFor), treat a man who sat out this year as meeting his playing-time expectation. For example, skip the buried channel when (p.redshirt === true || redshirtsUsed was incremented this winter), or have bankRedshirt stamp the year (redshirtYear) and exempt that year. Keep the noRedshirt promise check as it is. Add a test: a redshirted freshman with squadRank <= 8 must not enter the portal through the buried channel. *(Verifier's note: The finding's root-cause detail is wrong. The redshirt flag is NOT still set when openPortal runs: departAndDevelop calls bankRedshirt for every survivor who sat, and bankRedshirt deletes p.redshirt and increments redshirtsUsed. So the suggested 'p.redshirt === true' exemption would do nothing. The fix has to key off a stamped redshirt year (e.g. bankRedshirt records redshirtYear = board.year) or off redshirtsUsed being incremented this winter. Side effect of the same ordering: reasonFor's noRedshirt check (portal.ts:198) reads redshirt === true at portal time, which looks unreachable for a man who just sat.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/portal.ts`, `src/engine/morale.ts`
- **Risk:** Redshirting is a core roster lever in the systems reference. As it stands, using it costs a third of the men it is used on, and the player sees a 'broken promise' reason the coach never made. Casual staff redshirts (staffSitsTheFreshmen) feed the same channel for the coached program and for the 95 rivals.

#### M31. Pushing back on the board's terms nearly always takes the maximum ~20% off the win target, at no cost

*Area: gap-program-levers · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Pushing back on the board's terms nearly always takes the maximum ~20% off the win target, at no cost
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:9055-9095 argueTerms; src/state/store.ts:2654-2658 winterLosses; src/state/store.ts:3947-3954 boardAskFor
- **Problem:** argueTerms grants a cut when winterLosses >= 6 (HEAVY). Its own comment says this counts 'men who would have played' and is set where 'most of our good players left stops being a figure of speech'. winterLosses actually counts every graduated row (all seniors plus every walk-on, who always leave after one season) plus drafted men, so a normal winter clears the bar. The ask it reduces was already computed from the post-winter roster (boardAskFor uses rosterStrength(me.team) on the rolled roster), so the losses get counted twice. Push-back costs nothing: no security or board-confidence change.
- **How to reproduce:** cd scratchpad/agents/gap-program-levers && npx tsx full.ts 4242 5 3 (calls S().argueTerms() at each new season's opener, the same action as the SeasonTerms 'push back' button). For the population: npx tsx losses.ts (counts each program's winter the way winterLosses does).
- **Expected behavior:** The push-back succeeds only after an unusually damaging winter (lost starters), and the board ask is not discounted twice for the same departures.
- **Actual behavior:** full.ts: 2028 ask 24 -> 19 (gave 5, the cap); 10 losses counted, 1 a walk-on. 2029 ask 23 -> 18 (gave 5, the cap); 17 losses counted, 9 of them walk-ons. losses.ts, 288 program-winters: 88.9% have >= 6 losses (median 7-8, max 15), so almost every coach gets the full cut every year.
- **Root cause:** winterLosses filters only by team. It ignores whether the man played (starts, PA, IP) and ignores walk-ons. HEAVY=6 was set without measuring a real winter, and the tests in tests/mandate.test.ts use synthetic reports of 7 and 2 departures, never a real one.
- **Recommended fix:** Count only departures who were regulars: d.reason !== 'walk-on', and season batting PA or pitching IP above a threshold, or men in the top 9 hitters / top 4 arms by overall. Or measure the real roster drop: compare the opener roster strength with last season's and argue only when the drop is beyond a percentile. Add a real-winter test, e.g. start, settleSeason, rollYear, then expect argueTerms() to be 0 for a typical program. *(Verifier's note: Retitle: 'Push back wins a cut in ~89% of winters (median 2-3 wins, the 20% cap in ~26%) because walk-ons and non-playing departures count toward HEAVY.' Fix as proposed: exclude d.reason === 'walk-on' and weight by PA/IP or starter status.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `tests/mandate.test.ts`
- **Risk:** Every board target is effectively 20% softer than designed for any coach who taps the button. That weakens the firing/job-security loop the career is built on, and the 'once a season' decision turns into a reflex.

#### M32. 'Roster needs' focus boosts a different, smaller set of positions than the board's NEEDS list

*Area: gap-program-levers · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** 'Roster needs' focus boosts a different, smaller set of positions than the board's NEEDS list
- **Location:** src/engine/recruitingPlan.ts:82-84 recruitingPlan (need); src/state/store.ts:4858-4863 (week close); src/ui/screens/Board.tsx:329-340 (NEEDS); src/ui/StaffWorkPanel.tsx:67 FOCUS_HINT.needs
- **Problem:** The coordinator focus 'Roster needs' promises 'Points go 10% further at positions you need', and docs/05 §63.5 says '+10% on a projected hole'. recruitingPlan computes need from holesFor(full current roster) and depthShortfall(full current roster, []). Recruiting runs in-season, so the current roster is always full (holesFor is empty) and the seniors and likely draftees who are about to leave are still on it. The board's NEEDS list uses classSurvivors (roster minus seniors and likely draftees) plus the signed class. The multiplier misses most real needs, and it keeps boosting a position after the class has filled it.
- **How to reproduce:** npx tsx needs.ts (4 careers; for each, compares the positions recruitingPlan's multiplier fires on with the board's NEEDS (walkOnShortfall + depthShortfall over classSurvivors), and counts prospects).
- **Expected behavior:** With 'Roster needs' on, every prospect at a position the NEEDS list shows gets x1.10.
- **Actual behavior:** seed 4242 PSC: multiplier fires on [SP,C,SS]; board NEEDS shows [C,LF,1B,2B,3B,SP,SS]; 192 of 480 prospects at board needs not boosted. seed 99 VER: [SS] vs [2B,CF,3B,C,SS]; 192 of 240 not boosted. seed 7 ERI: [RP,C,SS] vs [3B,SP,RP,C,SS]; 237 of 477 not boosted. seed 123 PIE: [C,SS] vs [C,LF,RF,3B,RP,SS]; 288 of 384 not boosted.
- **Root cause:** recruitingPlan was written for the old offseason recruiting step, when the roster passed in had already lost its departures. Since recruiting moved in-season (05 §63.6), the roster passed by the store, Board.tsx and RecruitSheet.tsx is the full current roster.
- **Recommended fix:** Pass the board's own need list into recruitingPlan: compute need from classSurvivors(season, team, phase).survivors plus the signed class, through walkOnShortfall and depthShortfall exactly as Board.tsx does. Use one shared helper so the preview, the week close and the NEEDS tab cannot diverge.
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/recruitingPlan.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Board.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/RecruitSheet.tsx`
- **Risk:** A coach who picks the focus to fill his holes gets the bonus on a fraction of them. The preview and settlement agree with each other, so nothing on screen reveals that the focus is half-dead.

#### M33. Athletic director spends 58-89% of the budget on staff first, so delegated or casual careers cannot build, and season work stays locked

*Area: gap-program-levers · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Athletic director spends 58-89% of the budget on staff first, so delegated or casual careers cannot build, and season work stays locked
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:332-343 adFillsSeats; src/state/store.ts:5958-5987 (AD build, '+300' reserve at 5972); src/state/store.ts:5989-6000 (AD hire); src/state/store.ts:9213 startStaffProject (level < 1 refuses); src/engine/staffProjects.ts:282 staffPickFor
- **Problem:** When assistants are delegated (casual default), the AD hires the best man he can afford into every seat in turn, with no reserve. Season work for every seat needs that seat's building at L1, and the AD's own build rule (when facilities are delegated too) needs remaining >= cost + 300 after wages. The AD-hired staff usually leaves too little for either: the casual coach cannot afford even the cheapest building, and the AD never builds while the seats are full. Assistants are paid every year but their season work never starts, and 40-60% of the budget goes unspent each year (spent resets at the roll).
- **How to reproduce:** npx tsx casual.ts 4242 5 4 casual (casual default) and npx tsx casual.ts 99 70 3 casual '{"facilities":false}' (AD runs facilities too). Each prints the economy at season end and after each roll.
- **Expected behavior:** An AD who 'spends the budget' balances staff against buildings: something gets built, the staff he hired can do their season work, and the budget is not left idle year after year.
- **Actual behavior:** PSC (prestige 47, casual): AD hires $785k of $1,361k on day one, leaving $576k; the cheapest building (clubhouse) costs $580k, so the coach cannot build in year one. With facilities also delegated, PSC builds nothing for 3 full years ($576k/$675k/$764k unspent) and builds only when a seat happens to be vacant at the roll. SDY (1-star, prestige 23): AD hires an 84 pitching coach ($445k) and a 77 hitting coach ($365k), $930k of $1,049k; nothing built in 3 years; every seat shows 'Season work locked'; projectHistory stays empty.
- **Root cause:** adFillsSeats and the roll's AD hire pick the highest-rated affordable candidate per seat, without considering facilities or keeping a reserve. The roll builds before hiring, but with the staff retained its +300 reserve can never be met. Season work hard-requires facilityLevel >= 1.
- **Recommended fix:** Budget the AD as one plan: reserve the cheapest building cost (about $580k) before hiring, or hire the slot-1/slot-2 candidate when slot-0 would leave no room for the seat's building, and build the clubhouse or cage first. Drop the +300 reserve to something reachable. Alternatively, let season work run at reduced strength (L0) instead of locking it. *(Verifier's note: Note that the casual default (facilities handled by the coach) is stuck only in year one for mid-tier programs. It is stuck indefinitely for low-budget programs, and for any career that also delegates facilities.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/staffProjects.ts`, `src/state/depth.ts`
- **Risk:** Players who delegate (the casual audience) pay for assistants whose season work can never start, and never see the facilities or season-work systems working. A 1-star casual program can stay locked indefinitely.

#### M34. Turning 'Rotation and bullpen' off while a managed game waits removes the Bullpen button, but the engine still asks the coach about every pitch and nobody makes pitching changes (the starter threw 171 pitches)

*Area: gap-world-rules-switches · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Turning 'Rotation and bullpen' off while a managed game waits removes the Bullpen button, but the engine still asks the coach about every pitch and nobody makes pitching changes (the starter threw 171 pitches)
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx:80-81 and 641-659 (myPen/myVisits read from the live depth) vs src/state/store.ts:7826-7831 and 8466-8471 (autoPitching/autoVisits fixed when the game starts) and src/engine/liveGame.ts:319-320, 344, 362
- **Problem:** Manage decides whether to show 'Go to the bullpen' and 'Visit the mound' from the current depth setting (handles(depth,'bullpen'/'moundVisits')). The engine fixed autoPitching/autoVisits when the game was created, and the crash journal stores them too. After a flip in the middle of a game the two disagree. With bullpen turned off, the engine still treats the defensive half as manual (createHalfInning manualDefense=true, so maybeChangePitcher never runs) and stops at every batter for a call. The UI has hidden the only control for changing pitchers. Settings now says 'Your pitching coach runs the pen. (changed)', yet no pitching coach acts. The same applies to moundVisits off (visits hidden, nobody visits) and, the other way round, to turning bullpen on in a casual game (the controls appear only for defensive decisions, which never come). Resuming from the journal rebuilds the start-time value (store.ts:8303-8311), so the mismatch survives a kill and 'Pick it up'.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/gap-world-rules-switches/midgame-pen.cjs (Playwright, dev server 5174): start a full career (seed 4242, team 5) -> startManagedGame -> play to the first defensive decision -> Dugout shows 'Go to the bullpen' -> tap 'Back to Today (the game waits)' -> coach menu -> Settings and saves -> How you play -> turn 'Rotation and bullpen' off -> return to the game -> open Dugout -> play out the game answering 'Pitch'/'Swing'.
- **Expected behavior:** Either the flip takes effect in this game (the pitching coach makes changes: switch the live game to auto pitching or turn on the bench-coach delegate for pitching), or the game keeps the controls it was started with and Settings says the change applies from the next game.
- **Actual behavior:** Output: 'before flip: bullpen row visible = true' ... 'settings row: Rotation and bullpen / Your pitching coach runs the pen. (changed)' ... 'after flip, engine decision: {side: defense ...}' ... 'after flip: bullpen row visible = false' ... 'after rest of game: {over:true, pitchers:["Rafael Pemberton"], maxPitches:171}'. Nobody changed pitchers and the starter threw 171 pitches in a complete game. Screenshot shots-pen/3-dugout-after-flip.png shows the defensive call buttons and Dugout with only 'Visit the mound', no bullpen.
- **Root cause:** Two sources of truth: Manage.tsx reads useDynasty(s=>s.depth) on every render, while the LiveGame options (autoPitching/autoVisits) are captured once in startManagedGame/manageBracketGame and in the journal. setDepthSystem (store.ts:9804) has no live-game handling.
- **Recommended fix:** In Manage.tsx, gate the pen and visit rows on the game's own options (expose live.opts.autoPitching/autoVisits, or keep them in liveMeta) rather than on the depth setting. Optionally, when setDepthSystem('bullpen'|'moundVisits') runs while live!==null, call live.setBenchCoach(true) (and journal it) so the delegated pitching coach takes over at once. The minimum fix: have Settings note that the change applies from the next game while one is in progress. *(Verifier's note: Simplest fix: gate the Manage rows on the game's own options (expose live.opts.autoPitching/autoVisits through liveMeta), so the controls always match what the engine expects. Optionally, in setDepthSystem, when live!==null and key is bullpen/moundVisits, switch on the bench-coach pitching delegate and journal it.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/liveGame.ts`, `src/engine/game.ts`
- **Risk:** A coach who changes his mind mid-game cannot get his starter out (except through 'Let the bench coach call it', which nothing points him to). Arms rack up very high pitch counts and workloads, with injury-strain and rest effects later in the season.

#### M35. The 'Captains' switch does nothing when off: 'The room picks its own leaders' is never implemented, so every Casual career goes without a captain for good

*Area: gap-world-rules-switches · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The 'Captains' switch does nothing when off: 'The room picks its own leaders' is never implemented, so every Casual career goes without a captain for good
- **Location:** src/state/depth.ts:165-170 (captains, casual:false, whenOff 'The room picks its own leaders.'); src/engine/captains.ts:70 roomsChoice (called only by src/ui/screens/Captain.tsx:55 for display); src/ui/screens/Roster.tsx:91/254 and src/ui/Needs.tsx:304 (UI hidden when delegated); src/state/store.ts:6164 (mood settle damped only when captainOf != null)
- **Problem:** With captains delegated (the Casual preset default, or the switch turned off in Full), the coach's only routes to naming a captain are hidden: the Roster captain door and the Needs to-do. No store or engine code ever appoints the room's choice. roomsChoice() is only shown inside the Captain overlay, which a delegated coach cannot reach. The team never has a captain, so the June mood settle runs with damped:false every year. That is the one effect a captain has ('he damps mood swings across the whole roster').
- **How to reproduce:** agents/gap-world-rules-switches/flips.ts part A: start(4242, 5, ..., 'casual'), close the season plan, simWeek x4. Output: 'A casual captains handled? false candidates 1' then 'A after 4 weeks captain = null'. grep shows no caller of roomsChoice( or appoint( outside Captain.tsx and the nameCaptain action.
- **Expected behavior:** When the coach does not handle captains, the room names its own (for example appoint(team, roomsChoice(team)) at season start or the year roll, and again when the captain leaves), as the Settings row promises.
- **Actual behavior:** captainOf(team) stays null for the whole career; Settings says 'The room picks its own leaders.'
- **Root cause:** The catalogue row was added without a consumer: handles(depth,'captains') is only ever read to hide UI, never to trigger an automatic appointment (the depth.ts header itself warns about this: 'grep for handles( and make sure your key is in the list').
- **Recommended fix:** In rollYear (after rosters settle) and in start/acceptOffer, if !handles(depth,'captains') && !captainOf(team), call appoint(team, roomsChoice(team)) when there is one. Also re-run it after June departures. Add a store test that a casual career has a captain after the first roll when candidates exist. *(Verifier's note: Auto-appoint appoint(team, roomsChoice(team)) in rollYear, start and acceptOffer, and after departures, whenever !handles(depth,'captains') && !captainOf(team).)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/depth.ts`, `src/engine/captains.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Roster.tsx`, `src/ui/Needs.tsx`
- **Risk:** Casual players, who make up the default audience for the casual preset, silently lose a whole system (mood damping). The Settings copy misstates what their staff does.

#### M36. Text fields in every god editor commit only on Enter or blur: typing a value and pressing Back (Android back gesture) discards it

*Area: god-mode · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Text fields in every god editor commit only on Enter or blur: typing a value and pressing Back (Android back gesture) discards it
- **Location:** src/ui/god/controls.tsx:68-92 Field (commit on onBlur / Enter only); used by PlayerEditor name, ProgramEditor school/nickname, CoachEditor name and record counts, MoneyEditor staff names, LeaguesEditor new name
- **Problem:** Field keeps the typed text in local `draft` state and calls onCommit only from onBlur or Enter. Back from a god sheet (overlay Back, Android back gesture -> closeGod) unmounts the sheet with the input still focused. No blur reaches React's handler, so the draft is dropped silently. On Android the first back press usually just hides the keyboard and keeps focus, so the next back closes the sheet and loses the edit.
- **How to reproduce:** scratchpad/agents/god-mode/ui2-player.cjs (Playwright, pixel7 and small): header bolt > Team > Players and roster > tap a player > Profile > Name field: type 'Typed Then Back' > page.goBack() (the app's back handler) without tapping anything else.
- **Expected behavior:** The typed name is saved (or the user is asked whether to discard it).
- **Actual behavior:** ui2 output: 'name typed then back-gesture: stored name = "Diego Kaminski" (godStack ["tab","roster"])'. Typing then Enter commits: 'after Enter: Typed Then Enter'.
- **Root cause:** Commit is bound to blur/Enter, and nothing flushes a pending draft when the component unmounts.
- **Recommended fix:** In Field, keep the latest draft in a ref and commit it in a useEffect cleanup on unmount (when it differs from value), or commit on change with a short debounce. Optionally blur document.activeElement inside closeGod/closeGodAll before popping the stack. *(Verifier's note: The overlay's own Back button is safe. Only the system back path loses the draft. Fix: flush the draft on unmount (ref plus effect cleanup), or blur document.activeElement in closeGod/closeGodAll before popping.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/god/controls.tsx`
- **Risk:** Renames of players, programs, coach and staff are lost with no feedback on the main way Android users leave a sheet.

#### M37. 'Fork into a sandbox copy' leaves three saves with the same name: a redundant copy of the original, and the sandbox loses its '· sandbox' label on its first autosave

*Area: god-mode · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** 'Fork into a sandbox copy' leaves three saves with the same name: a redundant copy of the original, and the sandbox loses its '· sandbox' label on its first autosave
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:9764-9791 godForkToSandbox (protective copy at 9773); store.ts:9839 saveNow default name `name ?? team.def.school`; src/state/persistence.ts:219-241 SaveSummary has no sandbox flag
- **Problem:** The fork saves the original into a new slot named after the school, although the original's own slot is never touched by the fork. That makes an identical duplicate. It then writes the sandbox as '<school> · sandbox' and loads it. Every later autosave calls saveNow() with no name, which writes `team.def.school`, so the first day played renames the sandbox to the plain school name. The Saves list carries no sandbox marker (SaveSummary has no godMode), so the honest career and the sandbox cannot be told apart.
- **How to reproduce:** Headless: scratchpad/agents/god-mode/p5-fork.ts. UI: scratchpad/agents/god-mode/ui6-fork.cjs: device owns god mode, honest career, play a day, Settings > God mode > 'Fork into a sandbox copy', play a day, open Saved careers.
- **Expected behavior:** One original and one clearly labelled sandbox that keeps its label.
- **Actual behavior:** p5-fork.log right after the fork: 'Port Arthur · sandbox', 'Port Arthur', 'Port Arthur'. After one day, on disk: 'dyn-…6af2n89b: name="Port Arthur" god=true'. Screenshot shots/fork/01-saves-after-fork-and-a-day.png: 'Saved careers': three rows all titled 'Port Arthur', 2027 season, distinguishable only by 0-2 vs 0-1 and 'Playing now'.
- **Root cause:** The protective `saveNow(newSlotId(), school)` copy is redundant, and saveNow's name fallback ignores the slot's existing name.
- **Recommended fix:** Drop the protective copy (the original slot already holds it), or keep it but name it '<school> (before sandbox)'. In saveNow, when no name is passed, keep the slot's current name (or append ' · sandbox' when godMode is true). Add `godMode` to SaveSummary and show a 'Sandbox' badge in Saves.tsx. *(Verifier's note: The naming bug is wider than the fork. Any user-named copy from Saves > 'Save a copy' loses its custom name the first time it is loaded and autosaved, because saveNow writes `name ?? team.def.school`. saveNow should keep the slot's existing name when none is passed.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/state/persistence.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Saves.tsx`
- **Risk:** Players load or delete the wrong career, or carry on in the 'honest' one believing it is the sandbox (or the reverse). That undermines the 'This career stays as it is' promise on the fork card.

#### M39. Backgrounding the app mid-game does not pause anything: the bench coach keeps playing the game unseen and the crowd loop keeps sounding

*Area: lead-findings · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Backgrounding the app mid-game does not pause anything: the bench coach keeps playing the game unseen and the crowd loop keeps sounding
- **Location:** src/ui/sound.ts crowdStart/crowdStop (lines ~160-185); src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx:327-354 (crowd effect, bench-coach timer)
- **Problem:** Nothing in src reacts to visibilitychange, pagehide, or Cordova's document 'pause' event to stop audio or the bench coach. The only visibility listeners are in historySync.ts and predictiveBack.ts (navigation) and store.ts:806 (view transitions). The crowd bed is a looping AudioBufferSourceNode that stops only when the game ends or Manage unmounts. sound.ts's own doc comment on crowdStop says 'The game is over or backgrounded', but no backgrounding path ever calls it. While auto is 'watch', the bench coach submits one tactic per 900 ms setTimeout regardless of visibility.
- **How to reproduce:** Run agents/lead-findings/m1-background.cjs on the dev server (NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node m1-background.cjs). It starts a full career, presses Play ball, then Bench coach, then hides the page by setting visibilityState=hidden and dispatching visibilitychange. On a device: start a managed game, tap Bench coach, press Home or take a call.
- **Expected behavior:** When the app is hidden the crowd fades out (or the AudioContext suspends) and the bench coach stops calling pitches. Both resume, or the player resumes them, on return.
- **Actual behavior:** After 30 s hidden the game had moved from play seq 3 (top 1, 0-0) to seq 18 (bottom 2, 0-3). The AudioContext stayed 'running', the loop stayed active (loopsActive 1), and output RMS stayed nonzero (0.0087-0.0196). Capacitor does not pause the WebView: Bridge.onPause calls cordovaWebView.handlePause(keepRunning), and keepRunning = preferences.getBoolean("KeepRunning", true) (Bridge.java:463-464, 1364-1372). MockCordovaWebViewImpl.handlePause only calls webView.onPause()/pauseTimers() when !keepRunning. The app sets no KeepRunning (capacitor.config.ts, the generated config.xml), and MainActivity does not override onPause. JS timers (throttled to about 1 s when hidden) and WebAudio therefore keep running in the background.
- **Root cause:** The app has no lifecycle handling for audio or for the bench coach's auto-advance, and the Capacitor default KeepRunning=true leaves the WebView fully live after Activity.onPause.
- **Recommended fix:** In Manage.tsx, add a visibilitychange listener (document.hidden) that calls crowdStop() (or ctx.suspend() in sound.ts) and coachOff()/setAuto(null) when hidden, and calls crowdStart() again when visible while the game is live. Alternatively, export suspendAudio()/resumeAudio() from sound.ts and wire them in App.tsx to visibilitychange and to Cordova's 'pause'/'resume' document events. sfx() should also skip when document.hidden. *(Verifier's note: The handlePause path also fires a 'pause' document event (triggerDocumentEvent("pause")), so the JS can hook document 'pause'/'resume' as well as visibilitychange. The lead's emulation was a desktop Chromium visibility override; behaviour on a real Android WebView is inferred from the Capacitor source, not observed on a device.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/sound.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx`, `src/ui/App.tsx`
- **Risk:** After a phone call or the Home button, crowd noise keeps playing from a backgrounded app, which users report as a bug and which hurts Play store reviews. An auto-managed game can finish, with results and autosave, while the player is away, so they come back to a decided game they meant to watch.

#### M40. With SCOUTING switched off, full-mode careers show permanently locked rival tendencies, and every career gets a dead-end 'Scout a program' instruction on Strategy

*Area: lead-findings · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; also reported by ui-team*

- **Issue:** With SCOUTING switched off, full-mode careers show permanently locked rival tendencies, and every career gets a dead-end 'Scout a program' instruction on Strategy
- **Location:** src/state/features.ts:10 (SCOUTING=false); src/ui/screens/Player.tsx:849-893 (Tendencies); src/ui/screens/StrategyScreen.tsx:180-183 and :251; src/state/depth.ts:154-158 (scouting casual:false); src/ui/screens/Settings.tsx:381
- **Problem:** features.ts promises 'Off means the screens hide every way in and nothing else changes'. In practice, a full career handles scouting itself (handles(depth,'scouting') is true), so Tendencies treats a rival as scouted only when economy.scouted[owner] >= dayIndex. Only scoutTeam sets that, and its only caller is TeamCard's Scouting view, which is hidden when SCOUTING is false. Every rival player's Tendencies card therefore reads '0 of 5 read so far' with five lock rows, and with no note, because the note is also gated on SCOUTING. Rival tendencies cannot be read by watching either (isKnown returns opponentScouted for !isOurs). Settings hides the Scouting reports system toggle when SCOUTING is false, so a full-mode player cannot hand scouting to the staff, even though in casual mode the staff 'brings the report' and every rival tendency is readable. Separately, season.playbooks can only be minted by scoutTeam, so on Strategy, in every mode, the Callout 'Plans against one team — Scout a program to unlock one.' asks for an action that does not exist. The lead's extra claim that casual careers auto-mint playbooks from TeamCard.tsx:452 does NOT hold: that line is in openPlan inside the Scouting component, which is never rendered when SCOUTING is false.
- **How to reproduce:** NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node agents/lead-findings/m2-scouting.cjs. For full and casual: start a career (seed 4242, team 3), sim 2 weeks, open a Bayou State hitter's card, then Ratings, then the Tendencies card. Then go to Team > Strategy.
- **Expected behavior:** With scouting held back, a full career either reads rival tendencies the way the delegated (casual) path does, or does not show a locked report it can never unlock. Strategy does not instruct the player to do something the build removed.
- **Actual behavior:** Full: 'TENDENCIES: 0 of 5 read so far' with At the plate / First pitch / On the bases / Where he hits it / With men on all 'No report' and a lock (shots/m2-full-tendencies.png). Casual: 'What he does without being told' with all 5 readable. Both modes: 'STRATEGY: ... Plans against one team | Scout a program to unlock one.' (shots/m2-full-strategy.png, m2-casual-strategy.png), with playbooks [] and scouted {}.
- **Root cause:** The flag hides only the entry points (TeamCard tab, Player note, Settings row). The consumers that depend on what those entry points produce (economy.scouted, season.playbooks) still gate on handles(depth,'scouting'), which is true for full careers, and the Strategy Callout and EmptyState are not gated on SCOUTING at all.
- **Recommended fix:** When SCOUTING is false, treat scouting as delegated everywhere: e.g. const scoutsHimself = SCOUTING && handles(depth,'scouting') in Player.tsx and TeamCard.tsx, or have handles() return false for 'scouting' when !SCOUTING. Also gate the StrategyScreen Callout and the 'No plans yet' EmptyState on SCOUTING, or hide the 'Against one team' concept entirely.
- **Files affected:** `src/state/features.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Player.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/StrategyScreen.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Settings.tsx`, `src/state/depth.ts`, `src/engine/tendencies.ts`
- **Risk:** Full-mode players, the default preset, see a permanently locked panel on every opponent card and an instruction they cannot follow, which reads as a broken feature. Casual and full also play different games: casual players read every rival's tendencies, full players never can.

#### M41. Each career has exactly one save record, overwritten in place on every action; a named copy becomes the live slot as soon as it is loaded, so there is no backup generation to fall back to

*Area: lead-findings · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Each career has exactly one save record, overwritten in place on every action; a named copy becomes the live slot as soon as it is loaded, so there is no backup generation to fall back to
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:9824-9897 saveNow (target = slot ?? loadedSlot ?? AUTOSAVE_SLOT); src/state/persistence.ts saveDynasty (put to the same key); store.ts:9903-9940 loadSlot (refusal path)
- **Problem:** Every autosave put()s the whole world over the same IndexedDB key. Nothing keeps a previous generation. When a save becomes unloadable (loadDynasty throws, or assertSeason refuses it, e.g. the god-mode 'team with no starting pitcher' state already confirmed by the god-mode agent), loadSlot sets loadError/needsTeam and the only way out is a new dynasty. A manual 'Save a copy' protects the player only while it is never opened: after loadSlot(copy), loadedSlot is the copy and every later autosave overwrites, and renames, that copy.
- **How to reproduce:** NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node agents/lead-findings/m5-slots.cjs: start a career, sim 2 weeks, saveNow('dyn-copy1','My copy'), loadSlot('dyn-copy1'), sim 2 more weeks, then dump the IndexedDB records.
- **Expected behavior:** At least one earlier good state of the career (e.g. the previous autosave generation) survives, so a save that fails to load or validate can be rolled back.
- **Actual behavior:** After 2 weeks the career has one record (day 8). After Save a copy there are two (both day 8). After loading the copy and playing 2 weeks, the copy is now day 16 and renamed 'Thibodaux State' (it was 'My copy'), and loadedSlot is dyn-copy1. A single previous generation is never kept automatically, so a refused save means starting over.
- **Root cause:** saveDynasty writes one record per slot with no rotation, saveNow always targets the currently loaded slot, and loadSlot has no fallback slot to try.
- **Recommended fix:** In saveDynasty, before overwriting, copy the existing record to `${slot}~prev` (one generation, or only when the existing record passed assertSeason at its last load). In loadSlot, when loadDynasty throws or assertSeason fails, offer 'Open the previous autosave' from `${slot}~prev`. Hide ~prev records from listSaves. Optionally make loading a named copy fork it into a new live slot so the copy stays a true snapshot. *(Verifier's note: The risk should be scoped to 'a validation-refused save (assertSeason) has no rollback'. Remove the claim that an interrupted write can corrupt the save, because IDB put is atomic. The fix proposal (a ~prev generation) still stands.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/state/persistence.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Saves.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Start.tsx`
- **Risk:** Any engine or god-mode bug that leaves an unloadable state, or a write interrupted at the wrong moment, permanently destroys a long dynasty. Most players never make manual copies, and those who do lose them the first time they open one.

#### M42. Reloading a save changes the dynasty's future: the player-name pool is hidden module state that steers the season RNG

*Area: longterm-integrity · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Reloading a save changes the dynasty's future: the player-name pool is hidden module state that steers the season RNG
- **Location:** src/engine/players.ts:283 (usedNames), :368-376 uniqueName(); src/engine/season.ts:590 rebuildNameIndex(), :1671 nextSeason() -> generateClass(prev.rng); src/state/seasonCodec.ts:171; src/state/store.ts:5822 rollYear()
- **Problem:** Two copies of the same autosave produce two different worlds, depending only on whether the app process was restarted. At the signing step, rolling the year in a process that has been running produces a different recruiting class and a different season RNG position than rolling it right after a kill and reload. From then on every game, signing and record differs. The save stores rngState so that 'a resumed season does not diverge', but this hidden state defeats that.
- **How to reproduce:** cd <scratch>/agents/longterm-integrity && npx tsx --import ./register.mjs names-probe.ts 4242 5 2. It plays 2 seasons in one process to the signing step and takes the autosave. A = nextPhase('signing') in memory. B = kill, then refreshSaves + loadSlot of that autosave, then nextPhase('signing'). C = the same reload again. The probe compares rng state and a hash of the new recruiting class.
- **Expected behavior:** A, B and C produce the same 2029 class and the same season.rng.state(). The world should depend only on the save.
- **Actual behavior:** seed 4242: A rng 1667214721 class 5ca31f80fccf, top recruits 'Hiroshi Fairbanks, Percy Macalister…'. B and C rng 2610357642 class 969c33860391, top recruits 'Zane Clements, Luca Baez…'. A==B false; B==C true. Second world (seed 7331, team 40, 3 seasons): A rng 1180871099 vs B rng 2822299936, with different classes ('Oscar Underhill (5*)' exists only in A).
- **Root cause:** uniqueName(rng) rejection-samples FIRST/LAST pairs with the season generator against the module-level Set usedNames. So the number of season draws a new player costs depends on what is in that Set. No save stores it. fromPortable -> rebuildNameIndex() rebuilds it on load from only the names still in the save (rosters, the user's careers, current prospects). An uninterrupted process also still holds every name that has since left the world (graduates, unsigned prospects, released walk-ons). generateClass (720 prospects a year, called from nextSeason with prev.rng) therefore rejects different names in the two paths and ends on a different RNG position. Root cause confirmed: calling rebuildNameIndex(S().season) in memory just before the roll makes A identical to B (names-probe-rootcause.ts: A==B class true rng true).
- **Recommended fix:** Make name generation a function of the save, not of process history. Minimal fix: call rebuildNameIndex(season) at the top of rollYear, before fillRosters (store.ts:6493) and nextSeason/generateClass, and before any other path that generates players. Both paths then draw from the pool a load would build. More robust fix: draw names from a generator derived from the new player's id (e.g. makeRng(mix32(id))), so collision retries never consume season-RNG draws. Add a regression test: play to the signing step without a reload, then compare roll-in-memory against reload-then-roll on season.rng.state() and the class ids. *(Verifier's note: The probe contradicts the risk claim that the walk-ons shown on Signing Day can differ. Walk-ons and the user's own roster were identical across paths (walkOns true, roster true). walkOnClass uses its own makeRng(seed) and calls releaseNames, so the divergence is limited to the 720-man generateClass and the season-RNG position from then on. The proposed minimal fix (rebuildNameIndex at the top of rollYear) needs care. The signing-day class review draws walk-on names against the in-memory pool before the roll, so rebuilding only at rollYear could make fillRosters' walk-ons differ from the reviewed men when a name collision falls differently. Either rebuild the pool before the class review / at the start of the offseason as well, or (more robust) draw names from a per-player generator seeded from the new id so collision retries never consume season-RNG draws.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/players.ts`, `src/engine/season.ts`, `src/engine/recruiting.ts`, `src/state/seasonCodec.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** Dynasties are not reproducible from their saves: bug reports from a save cannot be replayed, and goldens/replay tests (which call resetNames to hide this) do not reflect real play. A 'Save as' branch taken before a decision does not replay the same world even when the same choices are made. It also gives a one-time re-roll of the next class: save a copy at the signing step, roll, then reload the copy and roll again. The walk-ons shown on Signing Day are drawn against the same pool, so they can differ from the ones who arrive after a restart.

#### M43. Every save structured-clones the whole 2-3 MB dynasty on the main thread, on every recruiting tap, and the cost doubles over a long career

*Area: longterm-integrity · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; also reported by performance, persistence*

- **Issue:** Every save structured-clones the whole 2-3 MB dynasty on the main thread, on every recruiting tap, and the cost doubles over a long career
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:9824 saveNow -> persistence.ts:596 saveDynasty put(buildSaveFile(...)). 124 'void get().saveNow()' call sites, including recruit() store.ts:4534 reached from RecruitSheet.tsx:478 Stepper onChange (one save per +/- tap), recruitPitch :4561 and recruitMajor :4649
- **Problem:** Saves are not coalesced. Each saveNow writes the complete dynasty: about 2.1 MB in structured-clone wire format in season 1 and about 3.0 MB by season 25 (3.97 MB as JSON). IndexedDB clones that synchronously on the main thread. The store calls saveNow after almost every action, including each step of the recruiting effort stepper. The harness counted 39-147 full saves per season.
- **How to reproduce:** 1) node: npx tsx bench-save.ts run-4242 4 (median structuredClone CPU of each dumped save). 2) Chromium: NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node browser-save.cjs run-4242/disk-25.bin 4. This starts a fresh career, measures saveNow() long tasks with CPU throttled 4x, then loads the 25-season save through the app's own loadSlot and measures again. 3) Per-season save counts are in run-4242/result.json rows[].puts.
- **Expected behavior:** One tap produces at most a cheap, coalesced write, and save cost stays roughly flat as a dynasty ages.
- **Actual behavior:** node structuredClone (median CPU): 29.8 ms (2028) -> 51.5 (2032) -> 54.1 (2040) -> 66.4 (2044) -> 62.4 ms (2052), about 2x. Chromium at 4x CPU, pixel7 profile, on a contended box: each saveNow is one long task of 65-181 ms on a fresh career, 176-341 ms at 14 seasons and 200-288 ms at 25 seasons. Saves per season: 76-147 in the run career (it recruits weekly) and 39-90 in the staff career, which is 4-10 s of main-thread clone CPU per season on this x86 box.
- **Root cause:** saveNow has no debounce or dirty-tracking and always serializes the entire season (~2,800 players across 96 rosters, 720 prospects, careerTotals, records, annals). The store fires it from about 124 sites, including per-tap controls.
- **Recommended fix:** Coalesce writes: debounce saveNow (e.g. one write per 300-500 ms, flushed on visibilitychange/pagehide/before a managed game anchors). Do not save on every Stepper change; save when the recruit sheet closes or the week closes. Longer term, split the record into a rarely-changing part (annals, careers, records, legends) and a per-day part, or clone in a worker, so a tap does not clone the whole history. *(Verifier's note: Minor count correction: there are 114 'void get().saveNow()' call sites in store.ts, not about 124. The fix stands: debounce/coalesce saveNow and flush on visibilitychange/pagehide and before a managed-game anchor. The recruiting stepper in particular should not trigger a full save on each tap.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/state/persistence.ts`, `src/ui/screens/RecruitSheet.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Board.tsx`
- **Risk:** Visible jank on Android that worsens the longer a dynasty runs. A row of +/- taps in the recruiting sheet queues one 200-300 ms freeze per tap on a mid-range phone, plus a 2-3 MB IndexedDB write each time.

APK: `Back.arm` is false, so Android's default back runs and the app goes to the launcher with the tour up. Browser/PWA: the page is left. (b) Follow the tour to step 7, 'Your budget', on Office, then press back. The route pops to Home and the tour silently disappears until Office is opened again. (c) Any first visit to Team/Roster shows the Quick tip 'Meet your team'. Back navigates to Home under the tip instead of closing it, and the tip reappears on the next visit.
- **Expected behavior:** While a tip is up, back closes it (the same as 'Got it' or the close icon). While the tour is up, back either steps or ends it, or is refused with a nudge. It never exits the app and never changes the screen under the modal.
- **Actual behavior:** t10-native: 'plan closed ... armed=false ["Tour · step 1 of 18 Welcome to Playball ..."]' (APK disarmed with the tour modal up). Browser: 'back with tour up LEFT data:text/html…'. t10b: 'team/roster ["Quick tip Meet your team…"]' then 'back with tip up home/today []' then 'team again … ["Quick tip Meet your team…"]'. t22: 'tapped Office … Tour · step 7 of 18 Your budget' then 'back home/today []'.
- **Root cause:** The CL rewrite (nav.ts as the single list of levels) dropped the tutorial/guide from the level list while both components still pass `layer: false` on the assumption that the store spends their entry. App arms the native callback from `nav.depth() > 0` and the history ledger sizes entries from the same list, so neither path knows a modal is up.
- **Recommended fix:** Tutorial.tsx: register the tip as a back layer, e.g. `useDialogFocus(dialog, close, { initial: primary, active: show && frame !== null })`, so back means close (markSeen). For the tour, add a level in nav.ts `levels()` when `activeGuideStep(...)` has a lesson or spotlight on screen: either a guard (`peel: refuse`, which nudges and keeps the APK armed) or a local layer whose peel is `onSkipStep`/'End tour'. Add both to the nav-levels tests. *(Verifier's note: Root cause is a documented contract (05 §91.2 'the tutorial and the guide opt out' because the store spends their entry) that nav.ts never implements. The fix belongs in nav.ts levels(), or Tutorial should simply register as a layer with dismiss = close.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/GuidedStretch.tsx`, `src/ui/Tutorial.tsx`, `src/state/nav.ts`, `src/ui/dialogFocus.ts`, `src/ui/App.tsx`
- **Risk:** Every new player meets the tour first. Android users habitually press back to dismiss dialogs, and doing so sends the app to the launcher or changes the screen under a modal that is still showing, which reads as broken onboarding.

#### M45. The route trail grows without limit and repeats screens, so back from Home cycles through every tab visited this season before the app can exit

*Area: navigation · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The route trail grows without limit and repeats screens, so back from Home cycles through every tab visited this season before the app can exit
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:3034-3047 `trailStep` (appends every route left, with no dedupe or cap); src/state/store.ts:3015-3018 `eraStops`; src/state/nav.ts:46-58 `base()`
- **Problem:** Every `go()`/`setScreen()` appends the route being left to `navTrail`. The trail is only reset at an era change (new frame or year), so within a season it holds every tab and sub-tab visit, including repeats. Back from Home/Today, the app's root, walks that whole list (Home, Team, Home, Team...) and the APK stays armed until it is empty.
- **How to reproduce:** In a season, tap the Team and Home bottom tabs alternately 30 times, ending on Home/Today. Press back repeatedly. It takes 30 presses, alternating Team/Roster and Home/Today, before the Back plugin disarms and Android may leave the app. Smaller case: Home -> Team -> Home, then back gives Team, then Home again, then exit (Home stacked twice).
- **Expected behavior:** Android bottom-navigation convention: back from a top-level destination returns to the start destination (Home/Today), and back from there exits. At minimum the trail is bounded and does not re-show the same screen in loops.
- **Actual behavior:** logs/t20.log: 'after 30 taps alternating Team/Home: home/today levels 30 armed true trail sample home|today,team|roster,home|today,team|roster,...' and 'back presses until disarmed (exit possible): 30'. logs/t2.log: 8 forward taps need 8 backs. logs/t5-native.log: Home->Team->Home then back gives team/roster, then home/today, then disarmed.
- **Root cause:** `trailStep` is a pure push: `navTrail: box ? s.navTrail : [...s.navTrail, { tab, screen, visit, era }]`. Nothing collapses a return to a route already in the trail or caps its length.
- **Recommended fix:** Give the trail popUpTo semantics. When the destination route is already in this era's trail, truncate the trail to before that stop instead of appending. Treat bottom-tab taps (`go(tab)` without a screen) as top-level switches that collapse the trail to [home|today], and cap the trail (for example 20 stops). The nav-levels and history-sync tests then need updated expectations. *(Verifier's note: Treat this as a design improvement: collapse to an existing stop (popUpTo) or cap the trail, as suggested. Downgraded from MEDIUM because the history model is documented intent.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/state/nav.ts`
- **Risk:** After an ordinary session players cannot leave the app with back without dozens of presses, and back appears to loop between the same screens.

#### M46. A second tap on SIM WEEK during the freeze is queued and plays an extra week, because the 800 ms 'think' guard is released just before the blocking sim

*Area: performance · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** A second tap on SIM WEEK during the freeze is queued and plays an extra week, because the 800 ms 'think' guard is released just before the blocking sim
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Today.tsx:118-126 think(); same pattern in src/ui/screens/Postseason.tsx:110-114 withBeat()
- **Problem:** think() sets thinking='week' and, 800 ms later, calls setThinking(null) and then run() (simWeek) in the same timer task. 05 §103 says the pause 'doubles as those buttons' rapid-fire guard'. Because simWeek then blocks the thread for 1–4 s, React commits thinking=null before the browser handles any tap queued during the freeze. The tap passes the `if (thinking !== null) return` guard and starts another week. Postseason's withBeat does the same (setBeat(null); run()).
- **How to reproduce:** Run NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node pw/doubletap.cjs http://127.0.0.1:5199/ 4. This is the production build, seed 4242 team 7, tour ended and must-dos cleared. It taps the real 'Sim week' button with CDP pointer input, then taps it again 1.2 s later, while the first week is still being simulated. For the control run, add the argument 'single'.
- **Expected behavior:** One week is simulated. The impatient second tap is ignored while the first week is being played.
- **Actual behavior:** Two taps give 8 days simulated, at both 4x and 1x throttle. A single tap gives 4 days. Dispatch of the second tap waited 1,858 ms (4x) and 767 ms (1x) behind the blocked main thread, then ran a second SIM WEEK. A player who taps again because nothing seemed to happen skips a week, including any game they meant to coach live.
- **Root cause:** The guard state is cleared synchronously before the long synchronous sim (Today.tsx:123-124), so the guard does not cover the period when the UI is unresponsive.
- **Recommended fix:** Release the guard only after the sim has finished and a frame has painted. For example, use a ref lock set in think() and cleared in a requestAnimationFrame→setTimeout after run(), or call setThinking(null) after run() and keep the button disabled while store.busy. With the sim moved to the worker (previous finding), set busy=true for the whole run and disable both sim buttons. Apply the same change to Postseason withBeat. *(Verifier's note: Of the two suggested fixes, 'setThinking(null) after run() and disable while store.busy' does not work as written. simWeek and advanceDay never set busy, and a state cleared inside the same task still commits before the queued click is dispatched. Use a ref lock that is released only after the next frame (requestAnimationFrame then setTimeout 0). Alternatively, have the sim set busy and clear it after a yielded frame.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Today.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Postseason.tsx`
- **Risk:** Weeks are simulated that the player did not ask for, and this cannot be undone in a save that autosaves every step. It is most likely on slow phones, where the freeze is longest.

#### M47. simClient retains every season the worker returns: Promise.race against the never-settling workerFailed leaks about 7 MB of heap per 'Sim the season'

*Area: performance · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** simClient retains every season the worker returns: Promise.race against the never-settling workerFailed leaks about 7 MB of heap per 'Sim the season'
- **Location:** src/state/simClient.ts:35-48 (workerFailed) and :64-67 simSeasonInWorker `Promise.race([call, workerFailed])`
- **Problem:** workerFailed is one promise per worker lifetime and only settles if the worker crashes. Each simSeasonInWorker call does Promise.race([call, workerFailed]), which attaches a new reaction to workerFailed. That reaction holds the race promise's resolve function, the race promise holds its resolved value, and the resolved value is the full Portable (a whole season world) the worker sent back. None of this is ever released until disposeWorker, which only runs on a new dynasty or a crash. The Comlink.proxy(onProgress) port and its listener are also kept per call, as the comment at :57-61 acknowledges.
- **How to reproduce:** Open a 10-season save in the production build (persistent profile pw/profile-long-backup). Run NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node pw/leak.cjs http://127.0.0.1:5199/ <profile-copy> 3 worker, which plays each year with playSeason (the God Mode 'Sim the season' action) plus June and the winter, and forces 3 GCs before each heap reading. Compare with the same script using 'week' (SIM WEEK path). Run pw/leak-snap.cjs for the heap snapshot retainer paths.
- **Expected behavior:** After each season the old world is collectable. The heap stays flat, as it does on the SIM WEEK path.
- **Actual behavior:** Heap after GC on the worker path: 9.0 → 17.4 → 24.5 → 31.6 MB over 3 seasons (+7.1 MB per season). On the SIM WEEK path: 9.0 → 14.4 → 14.9 → 15.5 MB. After 2 worker seasons the heap snapshot holds 3 world-shaped objects (teams+recruiting): the live store season plus two retained Portables. Each is retained via the module-scope variable fh (the minified workerFailed) → Promise reactions_or_result → PromiseReaction → resolve closure → Context → race Promise → result Object → .season.
- **Root cause:** Racing each call against a long-lived promise that never settles accumulates reactions. This is the standard Promise.race leak.
- **Recommended fix:** Use a per-call rejection hook that is removed when the call settles. For example, keep a Set of pending reject functions that the worker 'error'/'messageerror' listener iterates, then `return new Promise((res, rej) => { pending.add(rej); call.then(res, rej).finally(() => pending.delete(rej)); })`. Release the progress proxy when the season finishes: have the worker call onProgress[Comlink.releaseProxy]() at the end of simSeason, or pass a MessagePort the client closes.
- **Files affected:** `src/state/simClient.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** God Mode users who sim many seasons in one sitting grow the WebView heap by about 7 MB per season (70 MB per 10 seasons) until the app is killed. That adds OOM risk on low-memory Android devices. Once the main sim moves to the worker (first finding), every SIM WEEK would leak a world unless this is fixed first.

#### M48. Today recomputes the national RPI table for all 96 programs on every render, including every step of the schedule wheel

*Area: performance · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Today recomputes the national RPI table for all 96 programs on every render, including every step of the schedule wheel
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Today.tsx:176 `const rank = nationalRank(season, team.index)` (unmemoized); src/ui/GameWheel.tsx:133 onFocus on every front change; same pattern at Standings.tsx:65, Rankings.tsx:40-50, TeamCard.tsx:70
- **Problem:** nationalRank → nationalOrder → rpiOrder computes rpi() for every team. Each rpi() walks opponents and opponents' opponents (O(teams·games²)), then seedTeams sorts with tiebreaks. Today calls it directly in render, with no useMemo. Today re-renders on every store version bump, on its own thinking/jump/bump state, and on every card the schedule wheel passes, because GameWheel calls onFocus→setFocus each time `front` changes during a glide.
- **How to reproduce:** 1) Run node --import ./register.mjs --import tsx headless/render-costs.ts to time nationalRank at weeks 6 and 12. 2) Build the unminified store-exposed production build (probuild/vite.nomin.config.mjs, served on :5198). Run NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node pw/wheel.cjs http://127.0.0.1:5198/ 1. It sims 6 weeks, presses ArrowUp 12 times on the wheel and records rAF frame gaps plus a CPU profile.
- **Expected behavior:** The rank is computed once per simulated day (memoized on season/version), and scrolling the wheel costs only the wheel.
- **Actual behavior:** nationalRank costs 11.6 ms per call at week 6 and 18.7 ms at week 12 (node, loaded box). During a 12-card wheel glide, Today's renders took 85 ms of CPU, 72 ms of it in nationalRank (rpiOrder 71, rpi 36). Seven frames exceeded 34 ms and the worst gap was 167 ms.
- **Root cause:** An expensive whole-league derivation sits in the render body of the home screen. The wheel drives per-card state updates into that component.
- **Recommended fix:** Wrap it in useMemo(() => nationalRank(season, team.index), [season, version, team.index]). Better, compute the national order once per simulated day in the store or engine (cache keyed on season.results.length) and share it with Standings, Rankings and TeamCard. Optionally call onFocus only when the glide settles. *(Verifier's note: The main cost of the glide is elsewhere: GameWheel calls setF, a React state update, on every animation frame, and each one is followed by layout and paint. That deserves its own investigation. The memo fix is still worth doing, ideally as one national order cached per day and shared with Standings, Rankings and TeamCard.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Today.tsx`, `src/ui/GameWheel.tsx`, `src/engine/season.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Standings.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Rankings.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/TeamCard.tsx`
- **Risk:** The most-used screen janks whenever the schedule wheel moves. On phones each extra render costs about 40–60 ms in this call alone.

#### M49. The recruiting board re-sorts the class with fit() inside the sort comparator, and the memo depends on version, so every tap and every simulated day redoes it

*Area: performance · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The recruiting board re-sorts the class with fit() inside the sort comparator, and the memo depends on version, so every tap and every simulated day redoes it
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Board.tsx:326 `[...reachable].sort((a, b) => (b.stars * fit(b, pitch)) - (a.stars * fit(a, pitch)))` inside the useMemo whose deps (Board.tsx:364) include version
- **Problem:** fit() is expensive: factorScore → playingTime → playingTimeAt over the program's depth. The comparator calls it twice per comparison, so a sort of n prospects costs about 2·n·log2(n) fit calls instead of n. The memo is keyed on `version`, which every recruit tap, inbox read and simulated day bumps, so the whole computation reruns each time the board renders.
- **How to reproduce:** 1) Run headless/render-costs.ts, which compares the board's sort as written against one with keys computed once. 2) Run NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node pw/board-prof.cjs http://127.0.0.1:5198/ (unminified production build), which applies 5 version bumps with the board visible and attributes CPU under Board. 3) Run pw/taps.cjs to time a version bump on recruiting against other screens.
- **Expected behavior:** Opening the board, or tapping +1 on a recruit, costs a few milliseconds of sort.
- **Actual behavior:** Sorting 181 open prospects calls fit() about 1,970 times: 75.6 ms with fit in the comparator against 2.6 ms keyed (29x). At season start the profile shows Board at 278 ms over 5 bumps, with fit at 261 ms (94%). A pure version bump re-renders recruiting in 139 ms, against 6 ms on Today and 11–46 ms elsewhere. A recruit tap costs 318–387 ms to the next frame, including the save.
- **Root cause:** Sort keys are computed in the comparator rather than once, and a heavy memo is keyed on a global version counter instead of on recruiting state.
- **Recommended fix:** Decorate-sort-undecorate: `const key = new Map(reachable.map(p => [p, p.stars * fit(p, pitch)]))`, then sort by key. Key the memo on recruiting inputs (season.recruiting.week, a recruiting revision counter or the prospects' spent/points) rather than version. Also memoize classSurvivors/walkOnShortfall, which run in the same block.
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Board.tsx`, `src/engine/recruiting.ts`
- **Risk:** The board, a screen players tap repeatedly every week, lags 100–400 ms per tap on phones and adds about 30–60 ms to every simulated day while it is kept alive behind other screens (next finding).

#### M50. Screens kept alive behind the visible one re-render on every store version bump, because AppBody subscribes to version and Screen is not memoized

*Area: performance · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Screens kept alive behind the visible one re-render on every store version bump, because AppBody subscribes to version and Screen is not memoized
- **Location:** src/ui/App.tsx:175 `const version = useDynasty((s) => s.version)` in AppBody; App.tsx:842-851 `alive.map(... <Activity mode=hidden> <ScreenSurface><Screen id/>)`; App.tsx:1343 Screen (not memo); src/ui/keptAlive.ts:10 KEEP_ALIVE = 4
- **Problem:** AppBody re-renders on every version bump: every simulated day, tap and save-affecting action, since the engine mutates in place and 38 components subscribe to version. Each AppBody render creates new elements for all kept-alive screens (up to 3 hidden plus the visible one). React then re-renders the hidden subtrees too, because ScreenSurface and Screen are not memoized. Each hidden screen's version-keyed useMemos recompute even though nothing is shown.
- **How to reproduce:** Run NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node pw/hidden-prof.cjs http://127.0.0.1:5198/ (unminified production build). It starts a career, optionally visits Recruiting, Stats and Lineup, returns to Today, then CPU-profiles 3 version bumps and attributes samples to component functions.
- **Expected behavior:** Hidden (kept-alive) screens do no work until they are shown again.
- **Actual behavior:** With no kept screens, the profile shows Today 2 ms, GameWheel 3 ms and AppBody 1 ms. With Board, Stats and Lineup kept behind Today it shows Board 91 ms, Today 18 ms, Stats 12 ms and Lineup 1 ms for the same 3 bumps. The hidden board costs about 5x the visible screen on every mutation.
- **Root cause:** The whole frame component subscribes to a global change counter, and the Activity children are rebuilt each render with no memo boundary, so React re-renders hidden subtrees.
- **Recommended fix:** Make `Screen` (and ScreenSurface) React.memo so a parent render does not reach hidden screens. Hidden Activity already disconnects their store subscriptions, and they re-sync when shown. Better still, remove the version subscription from AppBody and move it into the small header/record components that need live numbers. *(Verifier's note: React.memo on Screen alone is enough, because its only prop is the primitive id. Memoizing ScreenSurface does nothing, since it receives new children elements on every render.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/App.tsx`, `src/ui/keptAlive.ts`
- **Risk:** Every simulated day and tap pays for up to three invisible screens. With the board in the kept set, the cost compounds the fit() sort finding above.

#### M51. The front door and the Saves screen fully deserialize every save on the device, twice at boot, just to list names and records

*Area: performance · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The front door and the Saves screen fully deserialize every save on the device, twice at boot, just to list names and records
- **Location:** src/state/persistence.ts:747-748 listSaves `getAll(STORE)`; boot callers src/ui/App.tsx:456 and src/ui/screens/Start.tsx:49 (both refreshSaves); also Saves.tsx:100, store.ts:10356 saveAs, 10377 deleteSlot
- **Problem:** listSaves reads every SaveFile whole. Each is a complete world of 2–3.3 MB serialized, materialized as JS objects on the main thread, but only slot, name, savedAt, year, the user team's record and school are used. At launch, App's effect and Start's own effect each call refreshSaves, so the read happens twice. Opening Saves, 'Save as' and Delete each re-read everything again.
- **How to reproduce:** Run NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node pw/manysaves.cjs http://127.0.0.1:5199/ <copy of pw/profile-long-backup> 4. It opens the 10-season career, makes 4 'Save as' copies (5 saves in total), then cold-starts at CPU 1x and 4x and records when .pb-start appears, the getAll requests and long tasks.
- **Expected behavior:** Listing saves reads small summary records. Start-up time does not grow with the number or size of careers.
- **Actual behavior:** With one save the Start screen appears at 699 ms (1x) and 1,051 ms (4x), with getAll taking 8–28 ms. With five saves it appears at 1,003 ms (1x) and 2,623 ms (4x). Each of the two boot getAll calls is followed by a long task: 347 and 215 ms at 1x, 1,066 and 796 ms at 4x. Opening Saves adds another 63–360 ms. Each 'Save as' re-reads all saves, so 'Save as' grew from 211 ms to 516–624 ms.
- **Root cause:** The summary is derived from the full record at read time, and there is no lightweight index. The boot path calls refreshSaves from two components.
- **Recommended fix:** Write a small summary record (slot, name, savedAt, year, school, record, retired) to a separate object store in the same transaction as each save, and have listSaves read only that store. Alternatively store the summary as an indexed field and use an index or key cursor. Drop the duplicate boot refresh, since Start can rely on the App-level read.
- **Files affected:** `src/state/persistence.ts`, `src/ui/App.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Start.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Saves.tsx`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** Launch on a phone takes seconds longer for players with several careers. It grows with every 'Save as' and spikes memory, since all worlds are inflated at once.

#### M52. 'Save and leave' (Settings) and 'End here' (Legacy) close the career even when the save failed, discarding unsaved progress without a word

*Area: persistence · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; also reported by ui-first-run*

- **Issue:** 'Save and leave' (Settings) and 'End here' (Legacy) close the career even when the save failed, discarding unsaved progress without a word
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Settings.tsx:155-167 (void st.saveNow().then(() => useDynasty.getState().backToStart())); src/ui/screens/Legacy.tsx:253 (void saveNow().then(() => backToStart())); store.ts:9889-9899 saveNow returns false on failure; store.ts:10298-10333 backToStart
- **Problem:** Both exits promise to save first ('Saves first.') but ignore saveNow's boolean result and call backToStart regardless, which drops the in-memory season. Everything since the last successful write is gone, and the Start screen shows no save state, so the player is never told.
- **How to reproduce:** scratchpad/agents/persistence/pw-quota.cjs: career saved at 4-0; make IDBObjectStore.prototype.put throw QuotaExceededError (a full phone); Sim week -> 8-0 with the 'Not saved. Tap to try again.' bar; Settings > Save and leave -> Start screen 'Piedmont State - 2027 season - record 4-0 - saved just now', no warning; restore storage, reload, Resume -> day 4, 4-0.
- **Expected behavior:** If the save fails, stay in the career and say so, or ask 'Leave anyway and lose the changes since your last save?'.
- **Actual behavior:** Career closed; the week played while saving failed is silently lost.
- **Root cause:** The .then() callback ignores the resolved boolean; backToStart clears the season unconditionally; Start does not render saveState.
- **Recommended fix:** const ok = await st.saveNow(); if (!ok) { show a confirm / keep the career; return; } st.backToStart(); in Settings.tsx and Legacy.tsx. Optionally surface saveState === 'error' on Start. *(Verifier's note: Also misleading: Start's card reads 'saved just now' from the last successful savedAt, which reassures the player that the save worked.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Settings.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Legacy.tsx`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Start.tsx`
- **Risk:** Data loss exactly when storage is failing, at the moment the UI says the career is being saved.

#### M53. When IndexedDB will not open, the Start screen is a dead end: New career is disabled and the 'Play without saving' escape can never appear

*Area: persistence · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed**; also reported by ui-first-run*

- **Issue:** When IndexedDB will not open, the Start screen is a dead end: New career is disabled and the 'Play without saving' escape can never appear
- **Location:** src/state/persistence.ts:312 OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS = 4000 (db() 395-404); store.ts:10336-10349 refreshSaves -> savesState 'error'; src/ui/App.tsx:225-231 (8 s 'stalled' timer, cancelled once checked), 454-457 (refreshSaves().catch(() => {}).finally(() => setChecked(true))), 559-572 ('Play without saving'); src/ui/screens/Start.tsx:63 (const blocked = busy || savesState === 'error'), 121 and 132-133
- **Problem:** A blocked or failing open makes listSaves reject at ~4 s; that marks the boot as checked, which cancels the 8 s watchdog that is the only route to the 'Play without saving' frame. Start then renders 'Your careers could not be read' with 'Start a new career' disabled, and Try again repeats the same failure. There is no way to play.
- **How to reproduce:** scratchpad/agents/persistence/pw-noidb2.cjs: indexedDB.open('playball') replaced by an upgrade request held blocked by another connection; after 9.5 s the page shows 'Your careers could not be read the browser did not open local storage within four seconds Nothing is lost. Try again Start a new career Settings'; 'Start a new career' disabled=true; 'Play without saving' count 0; Try again -> same. pw-noidb.cjs (open errors immediately) -> same dead end.
- **Expected behavior:** The designed escape ('You can play anyway, but nothing will be saved.') is offered whenever storage is unavailable.
- **Actual behavior:** Dead end; the only enabled controls are Try again and Settings.
- **Root cause:** The 4 s persistence timeout turns a hang into a rejection before App's 8 s watchdog fires, and Start treats savesState 'error' as 'block new careers'.
- **Recommended fix:** On Start, when savesState === 'error', offer 'Play without saving' (enable new career with a warning) instead of disabling it; or set the stalled state when refreshSaves rejects with StorageUnavailable.
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/App.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Start.tsx`, `src/state/persistence.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** A device whose WebView IndexedDB backing store fails to open (low storage, corrupted LevelDB; blocked storage on the web build) cannot play at all, while the screen says 'Nothing is lost'.

#### M54. An interrupted game is not scoped to its career: its card follows the player into a brand-new career (Sim disabled), and touching it - or opening another career - deletes the original career's journal

*Area: persistence · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** An interrupted game is not scoped to its career: its card follows the player into a brand-new career (Sim disabled), and touching it - or opening another career - deletes the original career's journal
- **Location:** store.ts:4157-4311 start() (never resets pendingGame, liveMeta, unseenTrophies, unseenRecords, newBadges, rosterAlert, weekStoppedBy, bigMoment, loadError); store.ts:10298-10333 backToStart (no pendingGame reset); src/ui/App.tsx:465 Start's New career = useDynasty.setState({ needsTeam: true }) (newDynasty(), which does reset pendingGame, is not used); src/ui/screens/Today.tsx:317-322, 397-399, 423; store.ts:8288-8293 resumeGame and 2501-2505 pendingFromJournal call clearJournal() when the journal's slot differs
- **Problem:** pendingGame belongs to one career but survives backToStart and start(). A new career's Today shows the previous career's interrupted game and disables Sim game and Sim week until the card is tapped; tapping it runs resumeGame, which finds a journal for another slot and deletes it, destroying the first career's interrupted game. Opening any other career from 'Load a career' deletes it the same way via pendingFromJournal.
- **How to reproduce:** scratchpad/agents/persistence/pw-ghost.cjs: career A (Piedmont State) killed mid-game, Resume (card shown), Settings > Save and leave, New career, start(99, 40) Kearney State -> Today shows 'You left a game on the field - Teton State at Piedmont State' and 'Pick it up - Game in progress'; Sim game and Sim week disabled. twocareers.probe.ts: A killed mid-game, loadSlot(B) -> journal CLEARED, loadSlot(A) -> pendingGame null.
- **Expected behavior:** A new career starts clean, and another career's journal is ignored rather than deleted.
- **Actual behavior:** Ghost card naming another career's schools, blocked Sim buttons, and silent loss of career A's interrupted game.
- **Root cause:** Per-career transient fields are not reset on the start()/backToStart() path the UI actually uses; the journal check deletes on any slot mismatch instead of only on staleness for the same slot.
- **Recommended fix:** Reset pendingGame and liveMeta (and unseenTrophies, unseenRecords, newBadges, rosterAlert, weekStoppedBy, bigMoment, loadError) in start() and backToStart(), or route Start's New career through newDynasty(); in pendingFromJournal/resumeGame return null without clearJournal() when j.slot !== slot.
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/App.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Today.tsx`, `src/state/liveJournal.ts`
- **Risk:** Confusing ghost state that blocks play in a fresh career, and silent loss of the other career's game.
