#### M92. Interest is quoted in units the board never shows: "Worth ~13 interest", "Bank 8 more interest first", "1 point of interest back"

*Area: ui-office · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Interest is quoted in units the board never shows: "Worth ~13 interest", "Bank 8 more interest first", "1 point of interest back"
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/RecruitSheet.tsx:343-346 worthLine, 196 raceSay; src/engine/recruiting.ts:2117 askBlocked ('Bank N more interest first'); src/ui/screens/recruitRace.ts raceOf/raceText (shares only); src/ui/screens/SigningDay.tsx:333-339
- **Problem:** The race card, the row bar and the 'Other programs' tab show only percentage shares of interest. The move tiles, the ask gate and the race sentence speak in raw banked interest ('Worth ~28 interest', 'Bank 1 more interest first.', 'Close behind, 1 point of interest back'). The coach's own banked total, and the price the ask needs, appear nowhere, so these numbers cannot be compared with anything. 'Points' also means two things: the weekly budget ('15 /15 left', '3 pts') and banked interest ('point of interest'; Signing day's 'Recruiting points spent on him · Points' is actually banked interest). The '0% → 81%' forecast assumes every rival stands still, and nothing says so.
- **How to reproduce:** r02-week1.cjs and r03-moves.cjs: open any target in week 2 and read the Ask tile ('Bank 1 more interest first.' while the race shows 'You 39%'). Signing day recruit sheet: r08-signing.cjs.
- **Expected behavior:** One unit, shown consistently. Either show his interest in you as a number with the price ('Interest 9 of 10 needed'), or express moves and the gate as share/progress ('Adds ≈ +12% of his interest', 'A little more interest needed'). Keep 'points' for the weekly budget only, and caption the forecast 'if the others stand still'.
- **Actual behavior:** RACE 'You 39% · Bayou State 34% · 4 others 27%' next to 'Ask to commit 6 · Bank 1 more interest first.' and 'Program visit 8 · Worth ~27 interest'. Signing day shows 'Recruiting points spent on him … School · Points · Lake Charles 21 · Pascagoula Tech 10' (banked interest, not points spent).
- **Root cause:** The engine's raw `points[team]` (interest) is rendered as shares in raceOf, but as absolute numbers in worthLine/askBlocked/raceSay, and as 'Recruiting points' in SigningDay. No component ever renders the raw total.
- **Recommended fix:** Add 'Your interest: 9 · needs 10 to ask' to the race card (or the Ask tile), or convert the move and ask copy to shares/progress. Rename SigningDay's card to 'His interest, by school' with column 'Interest'. Add 'if the others stand still' to the projected-share label. *(Verifier's note: Rename the SigningDay column to 'Interest', and show 'Your interest N of price' near the Ask tile.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/RecruitSheet.tsx`, `src/engine/recruiting.ts`, `src/ui/screens/recruitRace.ts`, `src/ui/screens/SigningDay.tsx`
- **Risk:** The board's main explanatory numbers cannot be acted on. A new player cannot tell how close an ask is or what a visit buys relative to the race, which is exactly what the recruiting screen is meant to teach.

#### M93. Revisiting Awards or Season review after the draft step shows different winners: Player, Pitcher and Freshman of the Year disappear and team leaders change

*Area: ui-postseason-offseason · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Revisiting Awards or Season review after the draft step shows different winners: Player, Pitcher and Freshman of the Year disappear and team leaders change
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Awards.tsx:131-133 (seasonAwards/allConference/coachOfTheYear on the live season); src/engine/postseason.ts:1101-1116 rosterIndex, 1469-1472 make() drops a winner who is on no roster, 1537-1538 freshman filter by current classYear; src/ui/screens/SeasonReview.tsx:85-130 MVP/leaders from team.team.* ; src/state/store.ts:3190 leagueWinter
- **Problem:** Both screens recompute their content on every render from the live rosters. Entering the draft step runs leagueWinter/departAndDevelop: drafted players and seniors are taken off every roster and class years advance. Walking back on the rail (or with Android back) to Awards or Season review then recomputes everything. Winners who left are silently dropped, because make() returns when the player is not on a roster. The freshman award no longer finds freshmen, and All-Conference picks and team leaders are replaced by whoever is left.
- **How to reproduce:** Run agents/ui-postseason-offseason/awards-revisit.cjs: best team (seed 4242), sim to Awards, tap 'Turn them all' and record the list. Continue to the draft step, tap 'Awards' on the rail and 'Turn them all' again. Then tap 'Season review'.
- **Expected behavior:** The awards and the season's leaders are fixed facts. A revisit shows the same list as the ceremony, as the history record already does.
- **Actual behavior:** On the night there were 17 rows: Player of the Year Leo Guerrero, Pitcher of the Year Rene Wilburn, Reliever, Freshman of the Year Kaden Ledesma, 9 position picks, 3 pitchers and Coach of the Year. On the revisit there were 12 rows: only Reliever of the Year remains among the national awards, the All-Conference 1B/2B/SS/RF are different players, and only 1 pitcher is left. The marquee changes from 'Handed out 5' to 'Handed out 2'. Season review leaders change from 'Best average Leo Guerrero .559' and 'Best ERA Rene Wilburn 1.81' to 'Best average Callum Woodbury .454' and 'Best ERA Evan Duran 3.08'.
- **Root cause:** The ceremony data is derived, not stored. seasonAwards() looks each winner up through rosterIndex(season), which only contains players currently on a roster, and departAndDevelop has already rewritten the rosters at the draft step. The awards stored on SeasonRecord.awards (written in settleSeason) cover only the user's own players and are not what this screen renders.
- **Recommended fix:** Snapshot the full award list (seasonAwards, allConference, coachOfTheYear) and the review leaders when the season is settled (settleSeason, or when entering the review step). Persist the snapshot with the save, for example on lastOutcome or a new lastAwards field, and render both screens from it whenever furthestPhase >= PHASES.indexOf('draft'), or always. *(Verifier's note: My run lost all four national awards, not only three as in the specialist's run. Snapshot the full award list (seasonAwards, allConference and coachOfTheYear) and the review leaders when the season settles, persist them, and render both steps from the snapshot. PlayerHub.tsx also calls seasonAwards on live rosters and may show the same drift.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Awards.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/SeasonReview.tsx`, `src/engine/postseason.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** The player sees their own Player of the Year vanish and the record contradict itself. This undermines trust in the awards night, which is the reward screen for the season. There is no save corruption.

#### M95. A June game interrupted by an app restart can be re-rolled: the resume card sits beside live Sim/Play buttons for the same game, and stays after the game is decided

*Area: ui-postseason-offseason · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** A June game interrupted by an app restart can be re-rolled: the resume card sits beside live Sim/Play buttons for the same game, and stays after the game is decided
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Postseason.tsx:496-533 (action ignores pendingGame), 731-744 (resume card rendered alongside); src/state/store.ts:7897 simBracket and 7746 manageBracketGame (no pendingGame guard), 8288 (pendingGame only cleared by resumeGame)
- **Problem:** In the regular season, Today disables Sim/Play while pendingGame is set (Today.tsx `blocked = busyNow || !!live || held || pendingGame !== null`), so an interrupted managed game must be resumed or finished by the bench coach. That is the journal's whole guarantee: a game resolves the same way whether or not it was interrupted. June has no such gate. After a reload mid-game, the June screen shows 'Game in progress · You left this one on the field' (Let them finish / Pick it up) and also the next-game card with working 'Sim this game' and 'Play this game' for the same matchup. Tapping Sim discards the half-played game, for example one the coach was losing, and simulates it fresh. The resume card then stays on screen. Tapping 'Pick it up' afterwards silently does nothing, because the journal no longer matches.
- **How to reproduce:** Run june-pending.cjs: in the conference tournament tap 'Play this game', make three calls, then reload and Resume. The June screen shows both cards. Tap 'Sim this game', then 'Pick it up'.
- **Expected behavior:** While a June game is pending, the only actions are 'Pick it up' and 'Let them finish', as on Today. Sim/Play are hidden or disabled, and the store refuses simBracket/manageBracketGame.
- **Actual behavior:** Log: 'after reload: {"pending":"Altamaha State at Piedmont State",..."w":45}', buttons [... 'Let them finish','Pick it up','Lineup','Sim this game','Play this game' ...]. After Sim: '{"pending":"Altamaha State at Piedmont State",..."games":4,"w":46}' with the resume card still shown. After 'Pick it up': '{"pending":null,"live":false,...}', with no game and no message.
- **Root cause:** Postseason computes `due -> Play this game / Sim this game` from myBracket alone, and simBracket and manageBracketGame have no pendingGame check. pendingGame is only cleared inside resumeGame and rollYear.
- **Recommended fix:** In Postseason, when pendingGame !== null, replace `buttons` with the resume pair, or disable Sim/Play with a note 'Finish the game you left first'. In the store, return early from simBracket, manageBracketGame and advanceBracket while pendingGame is set. Also clear pendingGame whenever its journal no longer matches the season (for example after any bracket step). *(Verifier's note: Also return early from manageBracketGame, simBracket and advanceBracket while pendingGame !== null, and hide or disable the June Sim/Play pair while the resume card is shown.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Postseason.tsx`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** Players can save-scum June games, the very thing the journal design forbids, and they see contradictory controls and a dead button after an ordinary Android process kill.

#### M96. 'Find my team' in the Regionals bracket says your school 'did not reach this one' while your own regional series is being played

*Area: ui-postseason-offseason · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** 'Find my team' in the Regionals bracket says your school 'did not reach this one' while your own regional series is being played
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Postseason.tsx:262-266 (inShownStage), 572-580 (findMine), 716-718 (message)
- **Problem:** inShownStage for the regional stage checks only bracket.regionals. While the user's series is live it is held in myBracket, and closeMyBracket appends it to bracket.regionals only when it ends. So during the user's own regional, tapping Find my team sets notHere and prints '<School> did not reach this one.', directly above the card showing their live series with the You tag.
- **How to reproduce:** june-nav.cjs step 7: best team, win the conference tournament, enter the regionals, open the Bracket tab and tap 'Find my team'.
- **Expected behavior:** No 'did not reach' message; the page scrolls to the live series.
- **Actual behavior:** 'Piedmont State did not reach this one.', with store state {regionals:15, mineInList:false, my:'regional'}.
- **Root cause:** `shown === 1 ? (bracket?.regionals ?? []).some((r) => r.seeds.includes(userTeam))` ignores myBracket.kind === 'regional'.
- **Recommended fix:** `shown === 1 ? (myBracket?.kind === 'regional' || (bracket?.regionals ?? []).some((r) => r.seeds.includes(userTeam)))`. *(Verifier's note: The specialist's fix is right: `shown === 1 ? (myBracket?.kind === 'regional' || (bracket?.regionals ?? []).some(...))`.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Postseason.tsx`
- **Risk:** The screen contradicts itself at a high-stakes moment and the player may think the bracket is broken.

#### M97. A coach who is out of June sees an empty bracket, an empty 'Games to watch' and a false 'still filling' note before each press that plays a whole tier

*Area: ui-postseason-offseason · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** A coach who is out of June sees an empty bracket, an empty 'Games to watch' and a false 'still filling' note before each press that plays a whole tier
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Postseason.tsx:940-945 (regional placeholder text), 946-995 (national ImportantGames yields no card), 1357-1360 (RegionalStage returns null for unplayed regions), 1483-1494 and 1525 (NationalStage 'This bracket is being drawn.')
- **Problem:** After the 2026-09-12 change, a stage the coach is not in waits for a press ('Play the regionals', 'Play the brackets') rather than resolving on arrival. The point was to let the player watch June. But before that press the screen shows nothing to watch. At the regionals, the Bracket tab is blank under 'Find my team', and 'Games to watch' shows a TBD card saying 'The conference tournaments are filling the regional field now.', although every conference tournament has finished and regionalPairing() already knows the 16 pairings. At the national stage, 'Games to watch' is a bare heading with no cards, and both bracket halves say 'This bracket is being drawn.', although selectNationalField has seeded the 20. (The store comment in openNationalStep says 'the twenty are on screen, waiting'.) One press then plays the whole tier, so the matchups are never seen before they are decided.
- **How to reproduce:** june-deep.cjs with WORST=1 BOOST=-20 DARK=1 (Passaic Falls, misses the field). After 'Play the tournaments' and 'See the regionals', look at both tabs; repeat after 'See the national tournament'.
- **Expected behavior:** The set pairings and the 20-team field are drawn as 'Set' matches, as the conference stage does once played, and empty sections have an empty state.
- **Actual behavior:** Screenshots show the blank Bracket tab (regional), the misleading 'filling the regional field now' card, and the national 'Games to watch' heading with nothing under it plus 'This bracket is being drawn.'
- **Root cause:** The views only draw played results (bracket.regionals, bracketA/B), the user's live bracket or sideShow. The selected but unplayed field is never rendered, and ImportantGames has no fallback for the national case.
- **Recommended fix:** Draw regionalPairing(season, bracket.cups) as 'Set' cards in RegionalStage and ImportantGames when bracket.regionals is empty. Draw splitShowdown(nat.field.seeds) for halves with no live or finished state. Give ImportantGames an EmptyState and correct the regional placeholder copy.
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Postseason.tsx`
- **Risk:** A coach who missed the postseason, the most common case early in a career, gets several presses of empty screens. This undercuts the stated design goal of following June.

#### M98. 'Trips to Omaha' and 'Bids' are counted with a different rule than the lists they open

*Area: ui-program-career · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; also reported by gap-title-run-trace*

- **Issue:** 'Trips to Omaha' and 'Bids' are counted with a different rule than the lists they open
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Program.tsx:820 (Trophies tab), src/ui/screens/Legacy.tsx:188-205 (Omaha and Bids plaques), src/engine/retirement.ts:337-342 endingOf ('Omaha once'), src/ui/screens/LegacySheets.tsx:47-53 KEEPS
- **Problem:** The national field is 20 teams: the 16 regional champions plus protected and at-large bids (selectNationalField, postseason.ts:848-866), and summarize() gives every field team the finish 'omaha' (postseason.ts:1045). A coach can therefore reach Omaha without winning his regional. Despite that, the coach's Trophies row 'Trips to Omaha', the legacy 'OMAHA' plaque and the verdict line all use coach.regionalTitles, while the lists behind them filter by finish. The 'BIDS' plaque uses coach.tournaments (national field), but its sheet keeps every finish except 'missed' and 'conference', so it also lists regional exits.
- **How to reproduce:** Run legacy.cjs (save5: Omaha in 2027 and 2028, one regional title, a regional exit in 2029), retire, and tap each plaque on the legacy screen. Or open the coach profile's Trophies tab in multi.cjs.
- **Expected behavior:** Each plaque number equals the length of the list it opens, and the verdict line agrees with both.
- **Actual behavior:** The OMAHA plaque reads 1 but its sheet lists 2028 and 2027. The verdict reads 'The nearly man — Omaha once.' The BIDS plaque reads 2 but its sheet lists 2029 Regional, 2028 and 2027. The coach Trophies tab shows 'Trips to Omaha · 2027, 2028' with the value 1.
- **Root cause:** regionalTitles is used as a proxy for Omaha trips, which stopped being true when the national field gained at-large and protected bids. The YearsSheet 'bids' predicate is broader than the tournaments counter.
- **Recommended fix:** Count Omaha trips from history or legend.years with the same predicate as KEEPS.omaha, and use that count for the plaque, the Trophies row and endingOf (or keep regionalTitles but label it 'Regional titles' and filter its sheet on wonRegional). Make KEEPS.bids match madeTournament (finish in omaha, runner-up, champion or national). Use the national-field trophy art for Omaha rather than 'REGIONAL CHAMPIONS'. *(Verifier's note: The profile Overview (Program.tsx:755) also labels regionalTitles with the note 'Each one is a trip to Omaha', which is false for the same reason. Fix it too.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Program.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Legacy.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/LegacySheets.tsx`, `src/engine/retirement.ts`, `src/engine/postseason.ts`
- **Risk:** The legacy screen, which the game frames as the summary of a whole career, contradicts itself the first time a player taps a number.

#### M99. Board goals list one event twice, and for a championship board both copies are guaranteed by a required goal

*Area: ui-program-career · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed**; also reported by copy-generated*

- **Issue:** Board goals list one event twice, and for a championship board both copies are guaranteed by a required goal
- **Location:** src/engine/program.ts:686-776 baseObjectives (bid() and omaha() for contend and championship); objectiveMet 801-803; shown in src/ui/screens/Program.tsx:387-398 BoardRoom and SeasonTerms/SeasonReview
- **Problem:** 'Reach the national tournament' (madeTournament = in nationalField) and 'Reach the national showdown' (reachedOmaha = finish omaha, runner-up or champion) are the same fact, because every national-field team gets the finish 'omaha'. Both appear as separate bonus goals for the contend and championship mandates. For championship boards both are also implied by the required 'Win your regional', since every regional champion is seated in the field. A board that shows 9 goals really asks for fewer, and judge() needs 3 bonuses for 'exceeded' (program.ts:1208), so one regional title hands over 2 of the 3 automatically.
- **How to reproduce:** cd agents/ui-program-career && npx tsx goals.ts. Then open Office › Board in year one at Piedmont State (y1.cjs, p7-board).
- **Expected behavior:** Each goal describes a distinct achievement, and no bonus is guaranteed by a required goal.
- **Actual behavior:** Across 480 team-seasons (5 seeds), madeTournament never differed from reachedOmaha, and 80 of 80 regional champions were in the national field. The year-one board lists 'Win your regional · Required', 'Reach the national tournament · Bonus' and 'Reach the national showdown · Bonus'.
- **Root cause:** The 'national' finish (lost in an opening round) was retired (postseason.ts:985-990), and with it the only gap between the tournament and the showdown, but the objective list kept both. The championship tier's required regionalTitle box sits above two bonuses it already implies.
- **Recommended fix:** Drop one of 'tournament' and 'omaha' from the contend and championship lists, or redefine 'omaha' as a later stage (for example 'reach the national final' or 'win your showdown bracket'). In baseObjectives, never offer a bonus that a required goal implies. Re-run mandate calibration (tests/mandate.test.ts) afterwards.
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/program.ts`, `src/engine/postseason.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Program.tsx`
- **Risk:** Players misread what the board wants, and 'exceeded' verdicts (+20 security, contract extensions) are easier than the list suggests.

#### M100. Job-security display does not reflect the board's real firing rules, and the final contract year is never flagged

*Area: ui-program-career · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Job-security display does not reflect the board's real firing rules, and the final contract year is never flagged
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Program.tsx:66-75 (SECURITY_REVIEW 35 / SECURITY_SECURE 55, securityWord), 376-385 Board confidence meter; src/ui/screens/SeasonTerms.tsx:286-306, 380-383 contractLine; engine bars in src/engine/program.ts:1087-1135, 2202-2239
- **Problem:** The board meter and the season terms use UI-only thresholds: 35 'Review' and 55 'Secure', with the text 'Fall below 35 and your job is under review at season's end.' The engine decides on different numbers, applied to the security after the June review. A coach is sacked if security drops below sackBarFor(patience), which is 13–27, plus 14 if he was caught looking. In the last year of a contract he is not renewed if security after the review is below PLAYER_RENEW_BAR (38). The deltas are +20, +9, −14 and −28. contractLine(years<1) 'This is the last year of your contract' can never show during a season, because contractYears is at least 1 then. The final season therefore reads '1 year remains on your contract' and the board shows 'Contract 1 yr'. The halfway board letter (store.ts:3863-3915) never mentions the seat either.
- **How to reproduce:** Run fired.cjs: restore save5, set the coach to the last year of his deal (contractYears 1, security 60 as saved), open Office › Board, then tank the season.
- **Expected behavior:** In his last contract year the player is told plainly that June is a renewal vote and what security he needs, and the meter's markers match the bars the board actually uses.
- **Actual behavior:** Before the season the Board shows 'Security 60/100 · Secure · Contract 1 yr · 4-year deal' with a green 'Secure' badge and no warning. After a failed season security goes 60→32 and the review says 'The board has let you go — Your contract expires and the board has chosen not to renew it.' A coach the UI called 'Secure' was let go after one season.
- **Root cause:** securityWord and the meter markers are hard-coded in the UI instead of being derived from playerBoard() (renewAt, sackAt). No UI reads contractYears === 1 as 'final year'.
- **Recommended fix:** Export the player's board bars (sackBarFor(patience) plus 14 when caughtLooking, and PLAYER_RENEW_BAR) and draw them on the meter and in the terms. In the final contract year show a 'Final year — the board votes on renewal in June; you need 38 after the review' callout with the projected security for met, missed and failed. Fix contractLine so 1 year reads as the final year. Optionally give the halfway letter a security line when the projection falls below a bar. *(Verifier's note: The not-renewed outcome needs remaining===0 and no rolling extension. A met season at contractYears 2 with security ≥55 extends the deal, so the trap is mainly a final contract year after a missed or failed season. The fix should still say this explicitly and show renewAt in the final year.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Program.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/SeasonTerms.tsx`, `src/engine/program.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** Players are fired without warning while the UI says they are secure, which is the most frustrating career outcome in a management game.

#### M102. Retire is offered in states where it cannot work: between jobs it sets a farewell to a school that fired you, and after retirement it is a dead button

*Area: ui-program-career · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Retire is offered in states where it cannot work: between jobs it sets a farewell to a school that fired you, and after retirement it is a dead button
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Program.tsx:760 and 887-927 (Retire, rendered unconditionally in the Overview), 713 and 741 (profile header and contract); src/state/store.ts:6924-6938 announceRetirement
- **Problem:** On the market (jobSearch) the profile offers 'Retire after this season · The season plays out as a farewell.' Pressing it sets farewellYear and posts 'Coach — the country knows this is your last year at Bayou State' (the school that fired him). The profile then says 'Your last season — The board meeting in June closes the career', but he has no board. The market has no way to actually end the career, so to retire he must take a new job, which signs him to a full contract (6 years in the test), and coach one 'farewell' season there. After retiring, the coach menu on the legacy screen opens a profile that still says 'Head coach · Bayou State', 'Contract 2 years left' and offers 'Retire after this season', which does nothing because announceRetirement returns early once retiredYear is set.
- **How to reproduce:** Run retire-market.cjs (fired → market → profile → Retire, two taps → take a job). Run legacy2.cjs (retire at the review → legacy → coach menu → Your profile).
- **Expected behavior:** Between jobs: 'Retire now', which closes the career straight to the legacy screen. After retirement: no Retire or contract controls, and the header reads 'Retired'.
- **Actual behavior:** After retire in the market: {farewell:2033, jobSearch:true, offers:4}, inbox 'Coach will step down after the season / ... your last year at Bayou State'. After taking a job: {farewell:2033, team:'Bitterroot Valley', contract:6}, and the profile says 'Your last season'. On the retired profile: 'Head coach · Bayou State | Contract | 2 years left | ... Retirement | Retire after this season | The season plays out as a farewell.'
- **Root cause:** Retire and CoachProfile do not check jobSearch or coach.retiredYear. announceRetirement only distinguishes graded from ungraded seasons. endCareer cannot be reused from the market as is, because it rolls the year (winterWithoutHim + rollYear) and the market is already the new, unplayed year.
- **Recommended fix:** Hide Retire and Resign and show 'Retired in YYYY' when retiredYear is set. When jobSearch is true, change the control to 'Retire now · your career closes here' and back it with a store path that writes the legend and sets retiredYear without rolling the season. In the profile header use 'Between jobs' or 'Retired' and drop the contract tile in both states.
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Program.tsx`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** Players who want to stop after being fired cannot, and a farewell announced on the market silently carries into a new multi-year contract. A dead 'There is no undo' button looks broken.

#### M105. Lineup gate is bypassed after an app kill/relaunch: a card with two catchers and nobody in left field is simmed and played live

*Area: ui-team · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

Then tap Sim game or Play ball.

Optionally run healPositions on load for cards that predate the fix. *(Verifier's note: The fix is right: add a cardGaps branch to unresolvedRosterDecision behind handles(depth,'lineups') and a matching must in Needs.tsx. The comment in swapStarter (store.ts:8762-8768) says manual starts deliberately leave the card broken for the coach to fix, so the hold should send him back to the lineup, not auto-heal it.)*

#### M106. 'Let auto fix it' (the primary button of the gap modal that pops mid-edit) throws away the user's substitution and his whole hand-set batting order

*Area: ui-team · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** 'Let auto fix it' (the primary button of the gap modal that pops mid-edit) throws away the user's substitution and his whole hand-set batting order
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Lineup.tsx:190-197 warnIfBroken, 260-284 tap/tapBench, 733-757 gap Modal; src/state/store.ts:8939 autoLineup → 3513 dealLikeAuto

The modal's filled primary button, 'Let auto fix it', runs autoLineup(): bestNine plus autoBattingOrder re-deal the whole card. That reverts the substitution and the custom batting order, and there is no undo.
- **How to reproduce:** r10-autofix.cjs: seed 11 team 20, Lineup. Swap batters 1↔9 and 2↔8 by taps, giving a hand order of 'Zabriskie:2B Burkhart:3B ... Tillman:CF'. Tap bench catcher Rollins, then the LF row. The modal appears; tap 'Let auto fix it'.
- **Expected behavior:** Fixing the hole keeps the man the coach just put in and keeps his batting order (relabel or move one man only). Alternatively, the button is clearly named and confirms that it resets the card. Ideally no modal fires during an in-progress edit, since the pinned callout already says the card is broken and the exit gate re-raises the modal.
- **Actual behavior:** after sub: 'Zabriskie:2B Burkhart:3B Sherwood:RF Santos:1B Rollins:C Anderton:SS Prescott:C Archambault:DH Tillman:CF'. After 'Let auto fix it': 'Tillman:CF Archambault:DH Sherwood:RF Santos:1B Hodgkins:LF Anderton:SS Prescott:C Burkhart:3B Zabriskie:2B'. That is the original auto card: Rollins is benched again and the hand order is gone.
- **Root cause:** Lineup.tsx tap()/tapBench() call warnIfBroken() right after swapStarter. The Modal's action/onClose (Lineup.tsx:747-754) calls autoLineup(), which is dealLikeAuto (store.ts:3513-3540): bestNine(team) re-picks the nine by merit and autoBattingOrder re-orders it. healPositions alone would have repaired the labels.
- **Recommended fix:** Do not open the modal from manual moves. Keep the pinned callout (Lineup.tsx:589-602) and let the exit gate (gateTick) raise the modal. Make the repair action label-only: call healPositions(team.lineup) on the current nine (or assign the newcomer the missing spot) instead of autoLineup. If a full re-deal stays available, name it 'Reset to auto lineup' and confirm it. *(Verifier's note: Lowest-risk fix: give the modal a label-only repair (healPositions on the current nine, keeping the order), or rename the button 'Reset to auto lineup'. Removing the mid-edit modal goes against documented intent.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Lineup.tsx`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** Coaches lose careful lineup work on the most frequent edit (pinch substitutions), and the modal makes the two-tap grammar feel broken.

#### M107. The pinned pick bar never shows what the next tap does: the instruction is ellipsised away on a 412px phone

*Area: ui-team · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The pinned pick bar never shows what the next tap does: the instruction is ellipsised away on a 412px phone
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Lineup.tsx:348-364 (selection/hint); src/ui/design/screens.css:643 .pb-pickhint__text

Only 'Moving Harlan Leighton…' is visible, and at Larger text even the name is cut ('Moving Harlan …').

#### M108. Stats › Fielding table is unreadable on a 360px phone: the Player column collapses to 42px ('Ta…', 'Seco…')

*Area: ui-team · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Stats › Fielding table is unreadable on a 360px phone: the Player column collapses to 42px ('Ta…', 'Seco…')

- **Problem:** The fielding table uses four fixed-px numeric columns (36/28/48/52px) beside a Face(32) player cell in a CSS grid with no horizontal scroll or reflow. On small phones the only identifying column gets almost no width, so every name and position is cut to 2-4 characters. On a Pixel 7 it is still cut ('Tadeo Ho…', 'Marco W…').
- **How to reproduce:** matrix.cjs with PHONE=small: Team > Stats > Fielding after 3 simmed weeks.

### LOW (174)

#### L1. Back gesture throws on WebViews older than Chrome 92 (Array.prototype.at in nav.newest), and Capacitor's WebView gate is left at 60 with no error page

*Area: android-release · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Back gesture throws on WebViews older than Chrome 92 (Array.prototype.at in nav.newest), and Capacitor's WebView gate is left at 60 with no error page
- **Location:** src/state/nav.ts:104 newest() `levels(s).at(-1)` (called by peelNewest and by App.tsx:424 peek() on every native back/backStart event); also src/state/store.ts:4393 stepBack and src/engine/strategy.ts:410; capacitor.config.ts (no android.minWebViewVersion / server.errorPath)
- **Problem:** minSdk 24 admits devices whose WebView may be old. The bundle's real floors: Chrome 80 to parse at all (48 optional-chaining sites survive Vite's chrome87 target) and Chrome 92 for Array.prototype.at in the back-navigation path. Capacitor's default minWebViewVersion is 60 and, with no errorPath, it only logs 'System WebView is not supported' and loads anyway (Bridge.java:105, 305-313).
- **How to reproduce:** agents/android-release/oldwebview.cjs: dev server, init script deletes Array.prototype.at; start a career, open the settings overlay, call nav.peelNewest() (what BackPlugin 'back' -> App.tsx backCommit/guardedPeel runs).
- **Expected behavior:** Back closes the overlay, or the app tells the user to update Android System WebView.
- **Actual behavior:** Modern: {result:'peeled', overlay:null}. Without .at: {threw:'TypeError: levels(...).at is not a function', overlay:'settings'} - every back gesture throws and nothing closes. Below Chrome 80 the module fails to parse, main.tsx never runs and the boot splash (index.html:41-53, removed only by main.tsx) stays on screen forever.
- **Root cause:** ES2022 lib in tsconfig allows .at(); Vite/esbuild lower syntax only, not built-ins; no runtime gate configured.
- **Recommended fix:** capacitor.config.ts: android.minWebViewVersion: 92 (or the real floor) and server.errorPath: 'webview.html' (a static page in public/ asking the user to update Android System WebView); replace `.at(-1)` with `[arr.length - 1]` in nav.ts/store.ts/strategy.ts; set vite build.target explicitly to the declared floor. *(Verifier's note: The cheap fix is replacing the three .at(-1) calls with index access. Setting android.minWebViewVersion plus errorPath is the safety net for the parse floor (optional chaining, Chrome 80).)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/nav.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/strategy.ts`, `capacitor.config.ts`, `vite.config.ts`
- **Risk:** Small population (Android 7-9 devices with stale WebView), but the failure is total and silent.

#### L2. God mode purchase page shows Google Play's raw codes in red ('USER_CANCELED', 'ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED'), treats a cancel as an error, and shows nothing for a pending purchase

*Area: android-release · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** God mode purchase page shows Google Play's raw codes in red ('USER_CANCELED', 'ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED'), treats a cancel as an error, and shows nothing for a pending purchase
- **Location:** src/state/billing.ts:132 (store.error -> error: e.message verbatim), 155-171 buyGodMode; src/ui/screens/Settings.tsx:296-302
- **Problem:** cordova-plugin-purchase v13 resolves order() with an error object and routes every failure, including a plain user cancel, through store.triggerError -> the app's store.error handler, which copies the plugin's message into a negative Callout. A pending purchase (cash/slow payment methods) raises no handler at all.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/android-release/billing-harness.cjs <cancel|already|pending|offline>: drives the real Settings > God mode page on the dev server with the REAL node_modules/cordova-plugin-purchase/www/store.js and a scripted window.cordova.exec that answers like cc.fovea.PurchasePlugin (cancel = '6777006|USER_CANCELED', PurchasePlugin.java:698-701).
- **Expected behavior:** Backing out of the Play sheet leaves the page as it was; already-owned triggers a restore; a pending payment says it is pending.
- **Actual behavior:** Cancel: red callout 'USER_CANCELED' above the buy button (shots/billing/cancel.png). Already owned: 'ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED', not unlocked. Pending: page identical to before, button re-enabled, no message (purchase only unlocks when Play later confirms). Offline at launch: product query fails and init never resolves, so a store build shows 'Arrives with the store listing.' with no buy or restore button.
- **Root cause:** store.js:2470-2480 `if (ret && 'isError' in ret) CdvPurchase.store.triggerError(ret)` for any order failure; billing.ts:132 shows e.message raw; no `.pending()` subscription; Settings.tsx:300 uses one fallback sentence for 'not reachable' and 'not created yet'.
- **Recommended fix:** In the store.error handler ignore code 6777006 (CdvPurchase.ErrorCode.PAYMENT_CANCELLED); on ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED call restorePurchases(); map other codes to plain copy. Add `.pending(() => patch({ pending: true }))` to the when() chain and render a pending note. Distinguish 'Play unreachable' from 'not on sale yet' in Settings.tsx:296-300. *(Verifier's note: In the store.error handler, ignore code CdvPurchase.ErrorCode.PAYMENT_CANCELLED (6777006). Call restorePurchases() on ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED and map other codes to plain copy. Add .pending() to the when() chain and render a note.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/billing.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Settings.tsx`, `tests/billing.test.ts`
- **Risk:** A normal cancel looks like a failure with a developer string; pending buyers may pay twice-attempt or ask for refunds.

#### L3. A refunded or revoked God mode purchase is never taken back: the device entitlement is write-once

*Area: android-release · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** A refunded or revoked God mode purchase is never taken back: the device entitlement is write-once
- **Location:** src/ui/App.tsx:383-393 (owned callback only ever writes godMode: true); src/state/billing.ts:98-108 (nowOwned; no not-owned path); src/state/devicePrefs.ts:186
- **Problem:** After a refund Google Play stops returning the purchase and the plugin marks the product not owned, but the app ignores that; DevicePrefs.godMode stays true forever. Buy, request a refund (Play grants many automatically within 48 h), keep the paid feature.
- **How to reproduce:** billing-harness.cjs refund: prefs.godMode=true, scripted queryPurchases returns [] at launch.
- **Expected behavior:** Product decision, made consciously; Play's guidance is to revoke entitlements for voided purchases.
- **Actual behavior:** CdvPurchase store.get('god_mode').owned === false, yet the page shows 'Unlocked' and prefs.godMode remains true.
- **Root cause:** The entitlement is cached once on approval and never reconciled with later store state.
- **Recommended fix:** After a successful receipt load (e.g. store.when().receiptsReady, or after initialize's getPurchases succeeded with the adapter ready), if the product is not owned clear prefs.godMode (optionally only after two consecutive confirmations to avoid false negatives); leave existing sandbox careers alone. Or keep the current behaviour and record it as an accepted risk.
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/App.tsx`, `src/state/billing.ts`, `src/state/devicePrefs.ts`
- **Risk:** Revenue leak via refund; low abuse effort.

#### L4. allowBackup=true with no backup rules: careers and the God mode entitlement go to the user's Google backup and are restored on reinstall, contradicting the privacy policy and the listing

*Area: android-release · Evidence: code-reviewed · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** allowBackup=true with no backup rules: careers and the God mode entitlement go to the user's Google backup and are restored on reinstall, contradicting the privacy policy and the listing
- **Location:** generated android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:4 (merged APK manifest: allowBackup=true, no dataExtractionRules/fullBackupContent); docs/privacy.md:9-10, 21-22; docs/16-store-listing.md:45
- **Problem:** Android Auto Backup and device-to-device transfer include getDir() directories, i.e. the WebView's app_webview/ (IndexedDB saves and the Local Storage holding playball.prefs.v1 with godMode). The policy says data 'never leaves it' and 'If you uninstall the app, this data is deleted with it'; the listing says 'Your saves never leave your phone.' Backup is good for players, but the text is wrong and the behaviour is unmanaged.
- **How to reproduce:** aapt2 dump xmltree --file AndroidManifest.xml app-debug.apk -> application allowBackup=true; no dataExtractionRules or fullBackupContent attribute.
- **Expected behavior:** Either backup is intended (copy says so, rules scope it to the save data) or it is disabled.
- **Actual behavior:** Implicit full backup; docs claim the opposite. Saves are 2.1-2.7 MB each (performance agent, years12-casual.out), so a player with roughly nine or more copies exceeds the 25 MB Auto Backup quota and the whole backup is skipped silently.
- **Root cause:** Capacitor template default left untouched; the generated manifest is never patched.
- **Recommended fix:** Decide: keep backup and fix the copy (see copyChanges), adding a data_extraction_rules.xml/backup rules via apk.cjs that include only the WebView data and exclude caches; or set allowBackup=false and keep the copy. Either way patch it from apk.cjs since android/ is regenerated. *(Verifier's note: Make a deliberate choice and enforce it from apk.cjs: either allowBackup=false, or data_extraction_rules.xml scoped to app_webview plus corrected privacy and listing copy saying data can be included in the user's own Android device backup.)*
- **Files affected:** `scripts/apk.cjs`, `docs/privacy.md`, `docs/16-store-listing.md`
- **Risk:** Privacy policy and store text inaccurate at review time; uncontrolled backup size and contents.

#### L5. The LAN-exposed dev server serves every file under the project root, including .git/ and wherever android/keystore.properties (the signing passwords) is kept

*Area: android-release · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The LAN-exposed dev server serves every file under the project root, including .git/ and wherever android/keystore.properties (the signing passwords) is kept
- **Location:** vite.config.ts:37, 60 (server/preview host: true); scripts/apk.cjs:17-32, 125 (default keystore.properties inside android/); node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-BK3b2jBa.js:63488 (default fs.deny ['.env','.env.*','*.{crt,pem}'])
- **Problem:** `npm run dev` binds all interfaces on purpose (phone testing over Wi-Fi) and Vite 5.4.21 serves any file under the root that is not in its small deny list. The release script's default location for the store/key passwords, android/keystore.properties, is inside that root, as would be a relative storeFile. The same file lives in the generated android/ directory that the docs describe regenerating with `cap add`, which deletes it.
- **How to reproduce:** curl against the running dev server: /.git/config -> 200 (repository config), /scripts/apk.cjs -> 200, /dist/index.html (a gitignored directory like android/) -> 200, /@fs/etc/hostname -> 403. So /android/keystore.properties is served whenever it exists, to anyone on the same network while `npm run dev` runs.
- **Expected behavior:** Signing secrets are never reachable over HTTP and live outside regenerated directories.
- **Actual behavior:** Served with 200; the default secrets path is inside the served tree. npm audit lists vite <=6.4.2 'server.fs.deny bypass on Windows alternate paths' (GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff, high), and the project builds on Windows.
- **Root cause:** host: true + default fs.deny + secrets path inside the project.
- **Recommended fix:** Default KEYSTORE_PROPERTIES to a path outside the repository (e.g. ~/.playball/keystore.properties) and refuse one under ROOT; add server.fs.deny entries for '**/keystore.properties', '**/*.jks', '**/*.keystore', '**/.git/**'; bind the dev server to localhost unless an env var opts in; upgrade Vite. No secrets are committed: git grep and `git log -S storePassword` over all history found only the placeholder lines in scripts/apk.cjs:22-25.
- **Files affected:** `vite.config.ts`, `scripts/apk.cjs`, `.claude/launch.json`
- **Risk:** Upload-key passwords readable on a shared network (they still need the keystore file, and Play App Signing allows an upload-key reset); passwords lost if the shell is regenerated.

#### L6. Docs call `npm run apk` 'the store build', but it is a debuggable, debug-signed APK in which the God mode entitlement can be flipped from chrome://inspect

*Area: android-release · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Docs call `npm run apk` 'the store build', but it is a debuggable, debug-signed APK in which the God mode entitlement can be flipped from chrome://inspect
- **Location:** docs/TESTING_SHORTCUTS.md:28; docs/07-v1-plan.md:1549; scripts/apk.cjs:160 (assembleDebug unless 'release'/'bundle'); node_modules/@capacitor/android/.../CapConfig.java:245, 286

It also shares the applicationId com.playball.dynasty with the Play build but a different signature, so moving a phone from a sideloaded build to the Play build forces an uninstall, which deletes every career in IndexedDB.

#### L7. tests/churn-probe.ts and tests/season-soak.ts never sign a recruit, so the README's turnover and title-concentration figures were measured in an all-walk-on league

*Area: balance-realism · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** tests/churn-probe.ts and tests/season-soak.ts never sign a recruit, so the README's turnover and title-concentration figures were measured in an all-walk-on league
- **Location:** tests/churn-probe.ts:39-50, tests/season-soak.ts:214-229; README.md:33; docs/05-systems-reference.md:4700 (§21.3), :5047 (§26.3), §42 tuning table; docs/06-backlog.md §F
- **Problem:** Both yearly loops call departAndDevelop + fillRosters with no recruiting window. fillRosters only enrols prospects whose signedBy is set, so nobody ever signs and every hole becomes a walk-on. This is the same harness defect §71.2 documents for climb-probe and headlessYear. Several balance claims are quoted from these two probes: the README's 'measured over thirty seasons, six of the top twelve programmes turn over' (§42, via churn-probe); 'ten distinct champions in thirty years against a real-world sixteen' (§21.3, backlog §F, and the soak's years/5 alarm); and 'mean 9.4' distinct champions (§26.3).
- **How to reproduce:** cd $D && YEARS=5 npx tsx churn-walkons.ts. It copies churn-probe's loop exactly and prints the walk-on share and the number of signed prospects each year.
- **Expected behavior:** A probe that measures the shipped world signs about 640-680 of 720 prospects a winter, as tests/calibration-seasons.test.ts asserts with signed > 400.
- **Actual behavior:** 0 of 720 prospects are signed in every year, and walk-ons go from 5.6% → 22.5% → 48.7% → 76.0% → 100% of the 2,208 rostered men by year 5. The real yearly loop (store-driven) gives different numbers: 10, 14 and 11 distinct champions in 16 seasons, and 16 in 25, 12 in 21 and 14 in 20, where the docs say ten in thirty. Top-12 prestige turnover is 5-7 by year 16 and 7-8 by years 20-25. So the README's direction is right, but its number and its source are not.
- **Root cause:** The two probes reassemble the offseason from engine parts. The engine has no recruiting driver: aiTargets/closeWeek run from the store or from headlessYear's recruitWindow.
- **Recommended fix:** Run headlessYear's recruitWindow, or the store, inside both probes; assert lastSigned > 400 per winter as calibration-seasons does; then re-measure and update README.md:33, §21.3, §26.3, §42 and backlog §F. The soak's structural June checks are still valid and can stay as they are. *(Verifier's note: Run carousel-probe's recruitWindow, which already exists in tests/carousel-probe.ts, inside both loops, and assert more than 400 signings per winter. The soak's structural June checks stay valid.)*
- **Files affected:** `tests/churn-probe.ts`, `tests/season-soak.ts`, `README.md`, `docs/05-systems-reference.md`, `docs/06-backlog.md`
- **Risk:** Title concentration and pecking-order movement in the shipped game have no guard, and the open balance question in §F is being argued from a world the game never produces.

#### L8. When a starter is hurt, startableSlot gives his turn to the next rotation arm, who then starts twice a week on a single day of rest

*Area: balance-realism · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** When a starter is hurt, startableSlot gives his turn to the next rotation arm, who then starts twice a week on a single day of rest
- **Location:** src/engine/season.ts:2054-2086 (startableSlot), :1975-1981 (recoveryGap)
- **Problem:** The walk only considers rotation arms in slot order and never a bullpen arm. recoveryGap lets an arm that threw 31-45 pitches start again two days later. So when #3 is out, #4 takes the Sunday start and then his own Tuesday start, every week.
- **How to reproduce:** cd $D && SEED=4242 TEAM=CDA npx tsx ace-wrap.ts, which tracks one fresh-world regular season a game day at a time. Also: SEEDS=20080,4242,12161 npx tsx heavy-arms.ts.
- **Expected behavior:** A hurt starter's turn goes to a spot starter from the bullpen, rotation arms make 11-12 starts in 45 games, and no starter routinely pitches on one day off.
- **Actual behavior:** At CDA, #3 Fielding is hurt from day 20. From then on #4 Dahlgren starts d27 and d29, d34 and d36, … every Sunday and Tuesday, ending with 20 GS and 97.7 IP against 11/11/3 for the others. In three fresh worlds, 2 of 288 programs have an 18-20-start arm (the GS histogram is otherwise 11:820, 12:271). In the store-driven runs, the season's busiest arm reaches 18-24 GS (for example HUD's Castellanos: 24 GS, 120.7 IP in 56 team games). Three of 48 league-seasons produce 155-168 IP with 17-18 wins, against a typical league leader of 100-120 IP. Those three are the only seasons that beat the seeded 158-IP record.
- **Root cause:** startableSlot's fallback cycles `(slot + i) % rot.length` over rotation arms only. recoveryGap is keyed to the last outing's pitch count, so a fatigued arm's short Sunday outing makes him 'ready' again on Tuesday.
- **Recommended fix:** When the slot's man is unavailable, try the best-rested bullpen arm as a spot starter before wrapping to another rotation arm. Also require a starter's full recovery (for example at least 4 days) before a start, whatever the last outing's pitch count. *(Verifier's note: Root cause: playGame reads currentDay(season) after simNextDay has already advanced dayIndex (season.ts:2739 vs 2245-2253 and restedFirst at 2117). Pass the game's own day into these calls (opts.day ?? currentDay) so rest is measured against the date the game is played. Also check the store's managed-game path (store.ts:8480) for the same ordering. A spot-starter fallback from the bullpen is an optional realism improvement, not the fix. Add a sim-level test: after a 100+ pitch outing, no arm starts within recoveryGap days in simNextDay.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/season.ts`
- **Risk:** Unrealistic workload lines and records, and an arm starting on one day off is extra exposure to injury and fatigue.

#### L9. Walking the offseason rail back from the portal step (or resigning or retiring after it) books portal arrivals' season at their old school as a season at yours

*Area: career-program · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **How to reproduce:** walkback.ts (seed 515, Mobile Bay, casual, so the staff works the portal): play to the portal step (arrivals: Brady Lassiter, Harvey Bonilla). goPhase('awards'), then press Continue back to the portal. Compare season.careers rows for the year.
- **Expected behavior:** Walking the rail back and forth leaves the archive unchanged, and a transfer's previous season is never filed under the new school.
- **Actual behavior:** '2027 career rows 23 -> 25; NEW ROW MOB Brady Lassiter ab52 ... rows: ["2027:MOB"]; NEW ROW MOB Harvey Bonilla ab35 ... rows: ["2027:MOB"]'.
- **Root cause:** archiveSeason archives the user's current roster, which after the portal step includes men who were not on it during the season. It is reached again by the walk-back and by the exits that call winterWithoutHim.
- **Recommended fix:** Guard bookTheYear behind a per-year flag (e.g. `season.bookedYear === year`), the way leagueWinter is guarded by furthestPhase. Or have archiveSeason skip players whose season stats were not compiled for this team (track the team on BattingSeason, or skip men flagged as portal arrivals this year).
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/season.ts`
- **Risk:** Player career pages and the hall ballot (MIN_SEASONS = 2) can count a season played elsewhere, which can make a one-year transfer hall-eligible.

#### L11. The wire's 'chasing the book' story assumes a 45-game season, so games left and pace are wrong on 34- and 56-game schedules

*Area: code-quality-tests · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The wire's 'chasing the book' story assumes a 45-game season, so games left and pace are wrong on 34- and 56-game schedules
- **Location:** src/engine/wire.ts:470-477 (recordChase). The same season-length literal appears at wire.ts:420-421 (offseason news fades at 1100 results), records.ts:118 (frozen-record text, shown at RecordBook.tsx:153-154) and SeasonReview.tsx:140/147 (hard-coded '20' and 'Thirty-two')
- **Problem:** recordChase cuts off at `gp >= 45`, computes pace as `(value / gp) * 45`, and prints `${45 - gp} games left`, instead of reading seasonLength(season.config). In a 34-game world the brief overstates the games left and the pace (x1.32). In a 56-game world it stops reporting at game 45 with 11 games still to play, and understates the pace, which mutes real chases. Standings.tsx already imports CONF_ADVANCE/CONF_FIELD on the stated principle that a rule is 'the engine's, not a number typed into a sentence'. These places break that principle.
- **How to reproduce:** `npx tsx chaseProbe.ts` (scratch dir): createSeason with configForRules({length:'short'}), simNextDay until team 0 has played 28, set records.seasonHR to the league leader + 2 so a chase triggers, then call wire(season, 200).
- **Expected behavior:** '... 14 home runs, 6 games left' with a pace of about 17 (34-game schedule).
- **Actual behavior:** 'Ryland Montes is chasing the book: 14 home runs, 17 games left' with detail 'His pace says 23.'
- **Root cause:** The season length is a literal 45 in three expressions, written before the 34/56-game rules existed.
- **Recommended fix:** `const total = seasonLength(season.config);` and use it for the cutoff, the pace and the text. Scale the offseason-news fade by the schedule. Build SeasonReview's numbers from NATIONAL_BIDS and conferenceIds(season).length * CONF_ADVANCE. Reword the frozen record text (see copyChanges). *(Verifier's note: Use `const total = seasonLength(season.config)` for all three expressions. The 1100-result fade in offseasonNews is approximate prose and lower priority. The records.ts frozen text ('A 45-game season cannot hold 58') is still true for 34 and 56 games, so only its wording is off.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/wire.ts`, `src/engine/records.ts`, `src/ui/screens/SeasonReview.tsx`
- **Risk:** Wrong numbers in a news story, and spurious or missing record chases, in any career not on the standard schedule.

#### L12. The board meeting uses a third ordinal helper that has diverged from the other two: '21th straight June in the field'

*Area: code-quality-tests · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The board meeting uses a third ordinal helper that has diverged from the other two: '21th straight June in the field'
- **Location:** src/engine/program.ts:2321-2322 (ORDINAL table plus a `${n}th` fallback), used in boardWords at program.ts:2373 and 2387. The correct helpers are src/ui/words.ts:48 and src/ui/format.ts:58.
- **Problem:** Three ordinal() implementations exist. The engine's copy spells 1-10 as words and falls back to `${n}th` for everything else. That produces '21th', '22th' and '23th', and the style flips from 'Tenth' to '11th'.
- **How to reproduce:** `npx tsx ordinalProbe.ts` (scratch dir) calls boardWords with a 'met' verdict and n-1 prior 'national' finishes.
- **Expected behavior:** '21st straight June in the field.' (ui/words.ts ordinal returns 21st/22nd/23rd)
- **Actual behavior:** '21th straight June in the field', '22th ...', '23th ...'. Also 'Tenth' at 10 but '11th' at 11.
- **Root cause:** A local helper was copied instead of shared (the engine cannot import ui/words.ts), and the copy only ever handled 1-10 properly.
- **Recommended fix:** Move one ordinal into the engine (or a shared util both layers import), use it in boardWords, and delete the other two. Pick one style, words or numerals, for these lines. *(Verifier's note: Spell the line out instead. For example, for n > 10, write 'Another June in the national field (${n} straight)', or use one shared numeric ordinal (the words.ts logic) moved into an engine util.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/program.ts`, `src/ui/words.ts`, `src/ui/format.ts`
- **Risk:** Visible grammar errors in the season-review board message for long-running powerhouse dynasties (21 or more straight national-field Junes).

#### L13. The habits test cannot detect a missing increment for the 'wire' or 'pen' habit

*Area: code-quality-tests · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** The habits test cannot detect a missing increment for the 'wire' or 'pen' habit
- **Location:** tests/habits.test.ts:36-56 ('is fed by something the game actually does')
- **Problem:** The test claims that every earned badge's habit is incremented by the game. It actually checks only that the quoted habit name appears anywhere in store.ts or Wire.tsx. 'wire' appears in store.ts as a tab id and an inbox kind (976, 3703, 5183), and 'pen' appears as a building key (2547). The check therefore passes even when every noteHabit('wire') and noteHabit('pen') call is removed, so the Newsman and Pen Hand badges could become unearnable without the test failing.
- **How to reproduce:** Run the test's logic on the sources with the increments deleted: a node one-liner (in my commands) removes `noteHabit('wire')` from Wire.tsx:89 and both `get().noteHabit('pen');` from store.ts:8580/8589, then evaluates `sources.includes("'wire'")` and `includes("'pen'")`.
- **Expected behavior:** The check fails when the increment is gone.
- **Actual behavior:** 'increments removed: pen x2, wire x1' and both includes() checks still return true.
- **Root cause:** A substring grep stands in for a behavioural check.
- **Recommended fix:** Drive the behaviour instead. Open the Wire screen through the store (or call the same noteHabit path the screen calls) and make a pitching change via bringIn/visitMound, then assert coach.habits.wire and coach.habits.pen increase. At minimum, grep for `noteHabit('x')` / `note(habits, 'x'`. *(Verifier's note: The minimal change is to grep for `noteHabit('${habit}')` or `note(habits, '${habit}'` instead of the bare quoted key, which is still crude but no longer collides.)*
- **Files affected:** `tests/habits.test.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Wire.tsx`
- **Risk:** A refactor that drops a habit increment ships with green tests and a badge nobody can earn.

Keep a small, deliberate set of architecture lints (engine isolation, single history writer), resolve their paths with import.meta.url, and move navprobe3 out of the product test suite. *(Verifier's note: Some of these are deliberate architecture lints ('App is the ledger and nothing else writes history'), which are reasonable to keep as source checks. #### L15. Timing-sensitive tests: real-time sleeps under vitest's default 5 s timeout, and whole seasons simulated at collection time

*Area: code-quality-tests · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Timing-sensitive tests: real-time sleeps under vitest's default 5 s timeout, and whole seasons simulated at collection time
- **Location:** Real sleeps after store work in async tests: tests/backNav.test.ts:222-246 (start() then 180/250 ms), tests/nav-trail.test.ts:117-160 (4 x 250 ms), tests/nav-pf.test.ts:138, tests/history-sync.test.ts:1376, tests/navprobe3.test.ts (real timers, 10 s limits). No testTimeout is set (vite.config.ts:25-27). Collection-time simulation: tests/progression.test.ts:63-66, 176-186 (5 seasons), 305-320 (8 seasons x 96 programs), 759-775 (7 x 96); tests/calibration-seasons.test.ts:198 (5 seasons in a describe body)
- **Problem:** Async tests run start() (a 96-team world), then wait on real setTimeout sleeps, inside the default 5,000 ms timeout. Under CPU contention these tests run within a few hundred ms of the limit. vite.config.ts:13-24 already records an aggregate-only failure caused by this. Heavy describe-body setup runs during collection, so filtering with -t or .skip does not avoid it.
- **How to reproduce:** With the machine under load (load average 13.4 on 4 CPUs): `npx vitest run tests/backNav.test.ts tests/nav-trail.test.ts tests/nav-pf.test.ts --reporter=verbose` and `npx vitest run tests/progression.test.ts -t "projects on signing day|projects the men themselves|agrees with what the NEEDS tab"`.
- **Expected behavior:** Timer-based assertions use fake timers, and heavy store tests run with an explicit generous timeout. Running 3 filtered tests should not simulate about 20 world-seasons.
- **Actual behavior:** Passing tests ran close to the limit: 'nav-pf ... does it in June as well 4715ms', 'backNav ... still claims a blocking card 4202ms', 'nav-trail ... keeps setScreen synchronous 3618ms'. The 3 filtered progression tests took 123.6 s, 107.9 s of it collection. Individual synchronous bracket tests ran 13-52 s each; they cannot time out only because vitest cannot interrupt synchronous work.
- **Root cause:** Real timers are used where fake timers would do. There is no project timeout policy. Expensive fixtures are built in describe bodies instead of lazily in beforeAll or a shared cached fixture.
- **Recommended fix:** Use vi.useFakeTimers() + advanceTimersByTimeAsync for the 180/250 ms waits. Set test.testTimeout (for example 30 s) or split store-heavy files into a separate vitest project with its own timeout. Move world-building into beforeAll with explicit hook timeouts, or a memoized fixture module shared across files. *(Verifier's note: Almost all of the measured time is start() building a 96-team world under CPU contention. The 180-250 ms sleeps are a small share, so fake timers alone would not move these tests away from the 5 s limit. An explicit testTimeout, or a cached world fixture, is the change that matters.)*
- **Files affected:** `tests/backNav.test.ts`, `tests/nav-trail.test.ts`, `tests/nav-pf.test.ts`, `tests/history-sync.test.ts`, `tests/navprobe3.test.ts`, `tests/progression.test.ts`, `tests/calibration-seasons.test.ts`, `vite.config.ts`
- **Risk:** Intermittent red CI on slower or shared runners, and slow targeted runs that discourage running tests at all (the full suite is 836 s).

#### L20. Record-chase stories hardcode a 45-game season: wrong 'games left' and pace in short and long worlds, and '1 games left'

*Area: copy-generated · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Record-chase stories hardcode a 45-game season: wrong 'games left' and pace in short and long worlds, and '1 games left'
- **Location:** src/engine/wire.ts:470-479 (recordChase.consider)
- **Problem:** `gp >= 45`, `pace = value/gp*45` and `${45 - gp} games left` ignore season.config. A short world has 34 games and a long world 56, so the paper reports games remaining after the season has ended (short), or stops reporting with 12 games left (long). The count also is not pluralised, so gp 44 prints '1 games left'.
- **How to reproduce:** SEED=31337 YEARS=5 MODE=casual LENGTH=short npx tsx --import ./register.mjs gen.ts → out/s31337-casual-short-5y/wire.txt; and npx tsx --import ./register.mjs probe2.ts (game 44, strikeout mark set just above the leader's pace).
- **Expected behavior:** Games left = seasonLength(config) − regular-season games played, with a correct plural.
- **Actual behavior:** Short world, day 34 (regular season over): 'Dillon Lennox is chasing the book: 14 home runs, 11 games left / His pace says 19.' Standard world: 'Benicio Macgregor is chasing the book: 95 strikeouts, 1 games left'.
- **Root cause:** Hardcoded 45 at wire.ts:470-477 (records.ts:218 BOOK_SEASON_GAMES has the same assumption).
- **Recommended fix:** const games = seasonLength(season.config); use regularRecord() for gp; `${plural(games - gp, 'game')} left`; pace = value/gp*games. *(Verifier's note: There is no seasonLength() helper. Derive the regular-season length from the config (e.g. count the user team's games in season.schedule, or compute it from seriesGames(config)), use regularRecord() for gp, and pluralise. BOOK_SEASON_GAMES (records.ts:218) carries the same 45 assumption for record scaling.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/wire.ts`
- **Risk:** Wrong numbers on the front page in every short or long world, all season.

#### L22. Alumni pro-career lines misstate counts: big-league retirement counts every pro season, 'A third year' repeats for years 4+, low-minors releases told 'Further than most ever get'

*Area: copy-generated · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Alumni pro-career lines misstate counts: big-league retirement counts every pro season, 'A third year' repeats for years 4+, low-minors releases told 'Further than most ever get'
- **Location:** src/engine/legacy.ts:565 (retirement line), 276 (minorSummer), 543 (release line); store.ts:6476-6485 (alumni retirement letter reuses the line)
- **Problem:** climb() sets proYears = age (all professional summers, including minor-league and abroad years) and prints 'Retired after N years in the big leagues'. minorSummer returns 'A third year at X' for any yearsThere >= 3. The release line says 'Further than most ever get' even for a man released after four years in rookie ball. The player card headline counts Show seasons correctly ('2 seasons in The Show'), so the card contradicts itself, and the retirement line is also the body of the 'ends his pro career' inbox letter.
- **How to reproduce:** npx tsx probes.ts (6,000 synthetic drafted careers through proCareer), plus the alumni.txt dumps from gen.ts.
- **Expected behavior:** 'Retired after 2 years in the big leagues', 'A fourth year at double-A', and a release line that matches the level reached.
- **Actual behavior:** Every one of the 1,010 big-league retirements printed the wrong count, e.g. 'Man 15 r16: "Retired after 9 years in the big leagues. A career." — seasons at THE SHOW: 2'. 374 careers printed 'A third year at …' for a 4th+ year. Samples include 'Rookie ball: Released after 4 seasons. Further than most ever get.'
- **Root cause:** legacy.ts:563-566 uses proYears (total) instead of a count of summers at LEVELS.length-1. minorSummer has no branch for yearsThere > 3. The release line is not level-aware.
- **Recommended fix:** Track showYears in climb() and print it. Print `Year ${n} at ${where}` (or an ordinal) when n >= 3. Branch the release copy on level, e.g. level <= 1 → `Released after ${age} seasons in the low minors.` *(Verifier's note: The third sub-claim is weak: 'Released after 4 seasons. Further than most ever get.' plausibly refers to how long he lasted, not the level he reached, so the level-aware release copy is a nice-to-have rather than a defect. The real defects are the big-league year count and the 'third year' repeat.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/legacy.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** Factually wrong career summaries on alumni cards and in the inbox.

#### L23. Rankings letter announces a fall out of the top 10 as 'Into the top 25 … the country has noticed', and congratulates a 2-10 team

*Area: copy-generated · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Rankings letter announces a fall out of the top 10 as 'Into the top 25 … the country has noticed', and congratulates a 2-10 team
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:3846-3862 (seasonNews, 'THE POLL')
- **Problem:** Each rung (1, 10, 25) is keyed separately per year, and the scan posts the best rung the team holds today. A team that reached the top 10 and later slips to 11–25 gets a new 'Into the top 25' letter. The body always says the country has noticed, including for losing records that the RPI ranks inside 25 early in the season.
- **How to reproduce:** NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node pw-letter.cjs (seed 4242, team 5, simWeek until 2 letters). Also the gen.ts s777 run in 2031.
- **Expected behavior:** No letter for a lower rung once a higher one has been announced this year; tone that matches the record.
- **Actual behavior:** Inbox (newest first): 'Into the top 25 — Coach — 15-5, and the country has noticed…' posted after 'Into the top 10 — Coach — 11-1…'. s777 run: 'Into the top 25 — Coach — 2-10, and the country has noticed. I bought a paper just to read it out loud.'
- **Root cause:** `const at = [1,10,25].find(n => rank <= n)` with key `rpi-${at}` has no memory of a better rung already reached.
- **Recommended fix:** Skip the post when the inbox already holds `${year}-rpi-1` or `${year}-rpi-10` for a better rung (or keep a bestRung field). For a losing record, use e.g. `Coach — ${w}-${l}, but the schedule has been brutal and the RPI likes us.`
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** Misleading, upbeat mail about a decline; erodes trust in the assistant's letters.

#### L28. Play-by-play direction text contradicts where the ball went: homers default to 'deep left', and the runner-advance groundout always says 'to the right side'

*Area: copy-generated · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Play-by-play direction text contradicts where the ball went: homers default to 'deep left', and the runner-advance groundout always says 'to the right side'
- **Location:** src/engine/game.ts:1374-1375 (HR direction from fielder.pos), 2251 (resolveOut right-side branch); landingFor 1921 also reads fielder.pos
- **Problem:** Outs are narrated via standingAt(fld, fielder) (the spot the man is actually standing at), but the home-run line reads fielder.pos, the man's own card label, and maps anything that is not exactly 'RF'/'CF' to 'left'. Left-handed hitters' homers are therefore announced to the opposite field about 70% of the time. The runner-moves-up groundout returns 'grounds out to the right side, runner moves up.' whoever fielded it.
- **How to reproduce:** npx tsx --import ./register.mjs hr2.ts (two store-driven seasons, raw replay logs); npx tsx probes.ts (resolveOut with SS/3B/P fielders).
- **Expected behavior:** Direction follows the spray lane (lefties pull to right); groundout names the fielder.
- **Actual behavior:** Lefty homers: left 39, right 9, center 8; righty: left 77, right 15, center 16. resolveOut with fielder SS / 3B / P → 'grounds out to the right side, runner moves up.'
- **Root cause:** HR narration skips standingAt(); the right-side branch ignores `where`.
- **Recommended fix:** `const spot = standingAt(fld, fielder).pos` for the HR direction (and pass the same to landingFor); in resolveOut use `grounds out to ${where}; the runner moves up.` or allow the branch only for 1B/2B fielders. Also write '4-run' homers as 'a grand slam' and hyphenate 'a 3-run shot'. *(Verifier's note: The main cause is not standingAt. fielderFor() can return an infielder, the pitcher or the catcher for a homer: lines go to the infield 32% of the time, and ground or popup homers exist. Every one of those maps to 'left', including 1B/2B on the right side. Derive the direction from the same x that landingFor uses (sign of the spot x, e.g. |x| < 0.15 → center), so the narration and the field view share one source. Using standingAt() is a secondary refinement.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/game.ts`
- **Risk:** Narration that contradicts the field view and the hitter's handedness.
