#### L45. Reduced motion is not honoured by confirm dialogs, and the in-app 'Full' motion setting cannot restore sheets under the OS setting

*Area: design-system-a11y · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Reduced motion is not honoured by confirm dialogs, and the in-app 'Full' motion setting cannot restore sheets under the OS setting
- **Location:** src/ui/design/screens.css:305-333 (.pb-dialog-host pb-fade, .pb-dialog pb-rise, .pb-dialog.is-nudged pb-nudge - only a [data-motion='reduced'] rule, no @media); screens.css:87, 128 and components.css:524-527, 1017, screens.css:727 (@media reduce rules without :root:not([data-motion='full'])); src/ui/screens/Lineup.tsx:163-164 (row glide checks only matchMedia)
- **Problem:** With Settings > Motion = System and Android 'Remove animations' on (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), every Modal (delete save, injury, June seed, end-the-week warnings) still fades in, rises 24px and plays the shake 'nudge'. Conversely, choosing Motion = Full ('Every slide and fade, whatever your phone says') does not bring back the sheet rise, tips or button press transitions while the OS asks for reduced motion. The lineup row swap glide ignores Motion = Reduced.
- **How to reproduce:** NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node scratchpad/agents/design-system-a11y/motion.cjs (context reducedMotion: 'reduce'; prefs motion system/reduced/full; opens the Season plan sheet and the Saves delete confirm).
- **Expected behavior:** System: dialogs and sheets do not animate when the OS reduces motion. Full: everything animates. Reduced: nothing animates (including the lineup glide).
- **Actual behavior:** motion.cjs: 'motion pref = system | sheet: none | confirm dialog: {dialog:"pb-rise",host:"pb-fade"}'; 'motion pref = full | sheet: {sheet:"none",host:"none"} | confirm dialog: pb-rise'. june.cjs: 'june modal animation under reduced motion: pb-rise'.
- **Root cause:** screens.css:333 only covers :root[data-motion='reduced']; there is no @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block for .pb-dialog-host/.pb-dialog. The sheet/tip/btn/verdict media blocks lack the :root:not([data-motion='full']) guard that the fulloverlay, terms and live-bar blocks use. Lineup.tsx:163 computes 'still' from matchMedia only, unlike PositionPicker.tsx:55 / predictiveBack.ts:48 which read data-motion first.
- **Recommended fix:** Add '@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { :root:not([data-motion="full"]) :is(.pb-dialog-host, .pb-dialog, .pb-dialog.is-nudged) { animation: none; } }' next to screens.css:333; prefix the media rules at screens.css:87, 128, 727 and components.css:524-527, 1017 with :root:not([data-motion='full']); in Lineup.tsx reuse the data-motion-aware helper (e.g. export wantsMotion from celebrate.ts) instead of matchMedia.
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/design/screens.css`, `src/ui/design/components.css`, `src/ui/screens/Lineup.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Settings.tsx`
- **Risk:** Vestibular-sensitive players still get motion and a shake on the dialogs that ask them to confirm things; the Settings copy for System and Full is untrue.

#### L46. Dark-theme primary button labels miss AA for 20 of 96 schools (4.30-4.47); dimmed button meta drops to 3.92

*Area: design-system-a11y · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Dark-theme primary button labels miss AA for 20 of 96 schools (4.30-4.47); dimmed button meta drops to 3.92
- **Location:** src/ui/accent.ts:299 and :282 (raisedDk tuned with ratio(c, WHITE) >= 4.6) vs src/ui/design/tokens.css:127 and :164 (dark --on-command: #f4f8f4); src/ui/design/screens.css:841 (.pb-home__act small { opacity: .85 })
- **Problem:** In dark mode every .pb-btn--primary (Done, Play ball, Save a copy, Sim to my game...) paints #f4f8f4 text on --command = --school-command-dk. accent.ts walks that fill until WHITE reaches 4.6:1, but the label colour is the slightly darker cream, so 20 schools land below 4.5:1 for 15px/600 text (not 'large'). Separately the Home bar's meta line ('4 games left') is drawn at opacity .85 on the tonal accent-soft fill, measured 3.92:1 in dark for the default test school.
- **How to reproduce:** cd scratchpad/agents/design-system-a11y && npx tsx dscontrast.ts (all 96 schools against design/tokens.css values); runtime: NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node tokens-rt.cjs (PTA, dark): primary 'Done' color rgb(244,248,244) on rgb(57,126,142), 15px 600. season.cjs mid-today dark audit.
- **Expected behavior:** >= 4.5:1 for every primary label in both themes and for all secondary text.
- **Actual behavior:** dscontrast.ts: 'D on-command on command-dk worst 4.30 PTA #2b5f6b fails 20 PTA 4.30, SAV 4.40, OKE 4.42, RID 4.47, SUT 4.35, SLS 4.44...'. season.cjs: '"4 games left","ratio":3.92,"fs":11,"fg":"rgb(132, 150, 194)","bg":"rgb(34,42,63)","op":0.85'.
- **Root cause:** The tuning target (WHITE) and the painted ink (--on-command #f4f8f4) disagree; opacity is used to de-emphasise text that already sits near the 4.5 floor.
- **Recommended fix:** Tune against the real ink: change accent.ts:282/299 to ratio(c, rgb('#f4f8f4')) >= 4.6, or set dark --on-command to #ffffff in design/tokens.css:127/164. Remove opacity:.85 from .pb-home__act small (use --ink-muted / a tuned colour instead). *(Verifier's note: tests/contrast.test.ts:259 checks '#ffffff' on accentRaisedDk, not #f4f8f4. That is why the test passes.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/accent.ts`, `src/ui/design/tokens.css`, `src/ui/design/screens.css`
- **Risk:** Hard-to-read primary commands for a fifth of the schools in dark mode; fails automated accessibility scanners.

#### L47. tests/contrast.test.ts guards the legacy palette, which the app no longer paints; the live palette breaks the test's own floors

*Area: design-system-a11y · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** tests/contrast.test.ts guards the legacy palette, which the app no longer paints; the live palette breaks the test's own floors
- **Location:** tests/contrast.test.ts:52-68 (LIGHT/DARK hard-coded from src/ui/tokens.css), :170-178 (card edge >= 1.5), :352-357 (only checks prototype-frame.css); runtime values come from src/ui/design/tokens.css:16-134 and its alias block :194-214 (':root:not(#_)')
- **Problem:** The test asserts contrast for paper #1c231d, ink #e4eae4, line #3a463c, mute #646a64, alert #e0655e etc. from tokens.css. design/tokens.css re-points every one of those names (--paper -> --surface #151f19, --line #28352c, --dim -> --ink-muted, --mute -> --ink-disabled #7f8a82, --alert -> --negative #ef7d76) with an id-weight selector, so none of the asserted pairs are what users see, and no design-system pair (--on-command on --school-command-dk, --ink-muted on --surface-raised, accent on accent-soft, badges) is tested. The 'separates a card from the page' rule it encodes (>= 1.5) is violated at runtime in both themes. It also only scans prototype-frame.css for raw whites - a file of which 20 of 2,717 rules ever match.
- **How to reproduce:** cd scratchpad/agents/design-system-a11y && npx tsx edges.ts; NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node tokens-rt.cjs (computed --paper #151f19, --line #28352c in dark).
- **Expected behavior:** The contrast test reads the token values the app actually resolves (design/tokens.css, both theme blocks) and covers the design-system pairs.
- **Actual behavior:** edges.ts: 'TEST light line on paper 1.51' vs 'RUNTIME light --line on --surface 1.25' / on --bg 1.17; 'TEST dark line on paper 1.62' vs 'RUNTIME dark --line on --surface 1.32' / on --surface-raised (sheets) 1.19; 'TEST light mute on paper 5.54' vs runtime 3.58. The test passes; the failures in the finding above (4.30 on-command) are invisible to it.
- **Root cause:** The design system replaced the palette by aliasing legacy names in design/tokens.css instead of editing tokens.css; the test kept its hard-coded copies of the old values.
- **Recommended fix:** Parse design/tokens.css (light :root block and the [data-theme='dark'] block) in the test instead of literals; add pairs for --on-command on --command / --school-command-dk for all 96 schools, --accent on --accent-soft, --ink-muted on --surface/--surface-raised/--surface-sunken, each badge tone on its -soft, and either raise dark --line (e.g. #3a463c) or lower the stated edge floor deliberately. *(Verifier's note: Overstated in one place: the test does cover the runtime school palettes from accentPalette() (accentDk on accentSoftDk, accentDeep on accentSoft, white on accentRaisedDk, and others), and those feed the design-system --accent, --accent-soft and --command. The real gap is the fixed surface/ink/line literals, plus the on-command pair being checked with #ffffff instead of the #f4f8f4 that is actually painted. Whether the lighter design-system line is a defect is a design choice; the stale test is the defect.)*
- **Files affected:** `tests/contrast.test.ts`, `src/ui/design/tokens.css`, `src/ui/tokens.css`, `src/ui/minimal-ui.css`
- **Risk:** Future palette regressions (the class of bug the test was written for after the 1.04:1 --navy incident) ship green.

#### L48. Three competing token layers and ~540 kB of legacy CSS of which <1% of rules ever match

*Area: design-system-a11y · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Three competing token layers and ~540 kB of legacy CSS of which <1% of rules ever match
- **Location:** src/main.tsx:7-31 import order; src/ui/tokens.css:14-137, src/ui/minimal-ui.css:17-76, src/ui/design/tokens.css:16-214; src/ui/prototype.css, prototype-frame.css, program.css, minimal-ui.css, rounded-ui.css; src/ui/design/screens.css:818-825; screens.css:651-663 vs 675-687
- **Problem:** --paper/--ink/--line/--dim/--radius-* are each defined three times with different values (ink #1d201d / #102019 / #102019; dark paper #1c231d / #151f19 / #151f19; line #ced4cb / #e1e8e2 / #e1e8e2; radii 8-10-14 / 13-18-26 / 12-16-24) and the winner is decided by load order plus a ':root:not(#_)' id-weight hack. Every in-season screen now renders design-system (pb-) markup only, so the legacy layers are almost entirely dead: at runtime across 17 tab screens, 12 overlays, the player card and the live game in both themes, prototype-frame.css matched 20 of 2,717 rules, prototype.css 7/1,001, program.css 2/310, minimal-ui.css 12/240, rounded-ui.css 3/39 (the live remainder serves App frame classes, GuidedStretch's guide-mask, BigMoment, Manage's ballpark-scene/hr-splash, GodSheet and app-crash). Legacy global rules still leak into the design system (rounded-ui.css:28 and minimal-ui.css:80 round every button; minimal-ui.css:910 sets every input to min-height 44px/font-size from --ts), forcing guard rules (components.css:12-15) and !important (139 in prototype-frame.css, 78 in minimal-ui.css). Smaller defects: .pb-todo redefines --ts (the global legacy text-scale multiplier) as a colour (screens.css:818-825), so any legacy calc(...*var(--ts)) inside a to-do would compute invalid; the board-goals block is duplicated verbatim (screens.css:651-663 and 675-687); dead design-system blocks remain (.pb-staff*, .pb-project*, .pb-facility*, .pb-budget*, .pb-ceremony/.pb-cabinet/.pb-verdict - 50 unreferenced classes in components.css, 21 in screens.css). Comments contradict reality: main.tsx says minimal-ui.css is 'Keep this last' and rounded-ui.css claims 'Every corner in the app comes from one of the three tokens in tokens.css'.
- **How to reproduce:** cd scratchpad/agents/design-system-a11y && node deadcss.cjs && node deadrules.cjs (static: 1,573 of 3,208 classes unreferenced; 459 kB of 754 kB of rule source unreachable); NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node csscov2.cjs (runtime selector-match coverage).
- **Expected behavior:** One token source, legacy layers deleted or reduced to the handful of live classes, no id-weight overrides.
- **Actual behavior:** csscov2.cjs: 'prototype-frame.css rules 2717 matched 20 bytes 346626 matchedBytes 1901 0.5%' ... 'TOTAL bytes 816100 matched 118528 14.5%' (draft.css/terms.css read 0 because offseason screens were not visited in that run). Computed tokens at runtime equal design/tokens.css values (tokens-rt.cjs).
- **Root cause:** Each visual pass (tabletop -> minimal-ui -> design system) was layered on top of the previous one rather than replacing it; the design system aliases legacy names instead of retiring them.
- **Recommended fix:** Move the ~20 live legacy classes (app-frame, playball-app, app-content, offseason-frame, postseason-frame, header-god, guide-mask*, big-moment-card, title-year, program-level-track, facility-art*, ballpark-scene, hr-splash, god-sheet, app-crash, avatar, screen-surface) into a small design/legacy.css, delete prototype.css, prototype-frame.css, program.css, minimal-ui.css and rounded-ui.css (re-test the guided tour, BigMoment, Manage, God sheet), drop the token blocks from tokens.css except --ts/motion/keyframes, remove the ':root:not(#_)' alias once nothing reads the legacy names, rename the .pb-todo locals (--todo-ink/--todo-soft), delete the duplicate board-goals block and the unreferenced pb- blocks, and fix the main.tsx / rounded-ui.css / docs/MINIMAL_UI_REWORK.md comments. Add a test that fails when a design/*.css class is unreferenced in src. *(Verifier's note: The .pb-todo --ts clash is latent: no rule inside a to-do reads the legacy --ts today. Dead-class detection is static token matching with dynamic-prefix tolerance, so treat the exact percentages as estimates.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/main.tsx`, `src/ui/tokens.css`, `src/ui/minimal-ui.css`, `src/ui/design/tokens.css`, `src/ui/prototype.css`, `src/ui/prototype-frame.css`, `src/ui/program.css`, `src/ui/rounded-ui.css`, `src/ui/design/screens.css`, `src/ui/design/components.css`
- **Risk:** Every future style change must out-specify dead rules; contradictory tokens already defeated the contrast test (finding above); ~66% of the shipped stylesheet text is parsed on every cold start of a low-end Android WebView for nothing.

- **Expected behavior:** >= 48x48dp touch area (Android guidance; the app's own --size-touch), and never below WCAG 2.2's 24px minimum without spacing.

- **Root cause:** Component heights were tuned visually per screen (comments in docs/05 cite strips 'a bit big') without a shared minimum; --size-touch is only used by .pb-btn (default size).
- **Recommended fix:** Give the small controls invisible hit area instead of visible height: e.g. .pb-wheel__weeks button { min-height: 24px } with the 8x4 pill inside, .pb-wheel__rail > button { width: 44px; height: 44px; margin: -8px }, .pb-back/.pb-seg__opt/.pb-btn--sm/.pb-link/.pb-todo__btn/.pb-rc-view/.pb-chip/.pb-phases__btn min-height: var(--size-touch) or a ::before { inset: -4px } hit-slop; keep the visual sizes. *(Verifier's note: One root-cause detail is wrong: --size-touch is used by .pb-btn (components.css:46) and also by components.css:501, 807 and 815, not only by .pb-btn.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/design/screens.css`, `src/ui/design/components.css`, `src/ui/design/recruiting.css`, `src/ui/GameWheel.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Today.tsx`, `src/ui/components/ui/data.tsx`
- **Risk:** Mis-taps on the Home wheel and recruiting filters, harder use for players with motor impairments; Play pre-launch accessibility report warnings.

#### L50. Screen-reader semantics: bracket games read as an unlabelled run of numbers, clickable table rows lose their button role, coach menu is a role=menu without menu behaviour

*Area: design-system-a11y · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Screen-reader semantics: bracket games read as an unlabelled run of numbers, clickable table rows lose their button role, coach menu is a role=menu without menu behaviour
- **Location:** src/ui/components/ui/data.tsx:462-484 (BracketMatch; label prop never passed by src/ui/DoubleElimMap.tsx:121-128); data.tsx:133-135 (<button role="row">); src/ui/Chrome.tsx:85-140 (CoachMenuButton, role="menu" at :123)
- **Problem:** Each played bracket game is a button whose accessible name is its raw text: seeds, 'You' and scores concatenated ('Final 1 Bayou State You 9 8 Gulfport 0'); the winner check icon is aria-hidden and elimination is shown only by grey text, so TalkBack cannot tell who won or which number is a seed. Interactive Table rows (standings, rankings) are <button role="row">, exposed as role row with an empty name, so nothing announces that they open the team card. The coach menu sets aria-haspopup=menu/role=menu/menuitem but focus stays on the trigger, ArrowDown does nothing, Tab lands on the full-screen scrim first, and Escape does not close it.
- **How to reproduce:** NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node scratchpad/agents/design-system-a11y/june2.cjs (bracket AX names); rows.cjs (standings rows AX); a11y1.cjs (coach menu keyboard).
- **Expected behavior:** Bracket game name such as 'Final: Bayou State, seed 1, 9 - Gulfport, seed 8, 0. Bayou State won.'; table rows announced as actionable with the team name; a menu that takes focus, supports arrows and closes on Escape (or plain buttons without menu roles).
- **Actual behavior:** june2.log: 'bracket AX button names: ["Final 1 Bayou State You 9 8 Gulfport 0", "Final 4 Mobile Bay 0 5 Thibodaux State 1", ...]'; rows.cjs: '{"role":"row","name":"","props":"invalid=\"false\" focusable=true"}' for button.pb-table__row; a11y1.cjs: 'coach menu open; focus = BUTTON.pb-coachmenu__btn', 'after ArrowDown focus = BUTTON.pb-coachmenu__btn', 'after Tab focus = BUTTON.pb-menu-scrim "Close coach menu"', 'after Escape menu open? true'.
- **Root cause:** BracketMatch only sets aria-label when a label is passed, and DoubleElimMap's SlotMatch never builds one; Table overrides the button's implicit role with role=row; CoachMenuButton uses useBackLayer (Android back) but not useDialogFocus or roving focus.
- **Recommended fix:** In SlotMatch build label = `${status}: ${name(a)} seed ${aSeed}, ${scoreA}; ${name(b)} seed ${bSeed}, ${scoreB}${winner ? `. ${name(winner)} won` : ''}` and pass it to BracketMatch; render interactive rows as <div role="row"> containing a cell with a real <button> (or role="row" + aria-label + tabIndex with onKeyDown) so the action is announced; in CoachMenuButton focus the first menuitem on open, handle ArrowUp/Down/Escape (or drop role=menu and use a simple disclosure with useDialogFocus).
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/components/ui/data.tsx`, `src/ui/DoubleElimMap.tsx`, `src/ui/Chrome.tsx`
- **Risk:** Blind players cannot follow the postseason bracket or discover that standings rows open team cards.

#### L51. Irreversible 'Delete it' confirmation is styled as the school-colour primary command

*Area: design-system-a11y · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Irreversible 'Delete it' confirmation is styled as the school-colour primary command
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Saves.tsx:215-230 (Modal tone="clay", action="Delete it"); src/ui/Modal.tsx:139-141 (action button always pb-btn--primary)
- **Problem:** Deleting a save (which can close the career being played) uses the same filled school-colour button as 'Let's go', 'Done' and 'Play ball'. The design system has .pb-btn--danger (used by Draft.tsx:540 and the god-mode controls) but Modal cannot render it; tone='clay' only recolours the small icon.
- **How to reproduce:** NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node scratchpad/agents/design-system-a11y/a11y1.cjs: Settings > Saved careers > trash icon.
- **Expected behavior:** Destructive confirm uses the danger treatment consistently with Draft/god mode.
- **Actual behavior:** a11y1.cjs: primary background 'rgb(61, 75, 113)' (the school navy), primaryText 'Delete it'. Screenshot shots/a11y/delete-modal.png.

#### L52. A managed game skips the day's pre-game injury and classroom roll: men hurt 'before the game' play all of it

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** A managed game skips the day's pre-game injury and classroom roll: men hurt 'before the game' play all of it
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts startManagedGame (~8418-8540) builds the card before the day's rolls; endManagedGame (~8715) runs simNextDay(season,{hold}) only after the game; season.ts simNextDay (2697-2735) rolls the classroom and rollHurtsFor before the day's games
- **Problem:** In a simulated day, simNextDay suspends classroom failures (every 7th day index) and runs rollHurtsFor for every team playing, and only then plays the games, so a man hurt that day misses the game. For the coached game, startManagedGame builds both cards (coverFor at the current clock) before those rolls exist. The rolls run inside endManagedGame's simNextDay after the final out. The rolls are deterministic, so the same man is hurt either way, but in a managed game he (and the opponent's hurt men) play the whole game first. dayInTheLegs is also applied before the roll in the managed path (after it in playGame), so the injury strain differs.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/game-sim/injparity.ts (seed 2024; teams 7 and 40). Run 1 simulates day by day and finds the first pre-game injury to the nine. Run 2 uses the same world and manages that day's game.
- **Expected behavior:** The same man misses the game whether it is simulated or managed.
- **Actual behavior:** Team 7: 'SIMULATED: day 34 Keaton Duplantis hurt (a tight hamstring) before the game; in that day's box: false' / 'MANAGED: day 34: Keaton Duplantis in the starting nine true; batted 5 AB; after the game he is injury until index 24'. Team 40: William Ardmore, the same pattern (6 AB).
- **Root cause:** The day's pre-game passes live inside simNextDay, which the managed flow only calls with `hold` after the game.
- **Recommended fix:** Split simNextDay into a pre-game step (classroom + rollHurtsFor for the day's games) and a play step. Call the pre-game step in startManagedGame/manageBracketGame before coverFor/startableSlot and before the journal anchor (it takes no draws), and have the held simNextDay skip it.
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/season.ts`
- **Risk:** Managing a game is a small edge: it never loses a man to that day's roll. Injury notices arrive after a game the man played in, and managed and simulated seasons diverge.

#### L53. "Sim the rest" during your own defensive half leaves that half manual: a gassed starter is never pulled

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** "Sim the rest" during your own defensive half leaves that half manual: a gassed starter is never pulled
- **Location:** src/engine/liveGame.ts:446-449 finish() sets auto=true, but the open half was created with manualDefense/manualOffense=true (liveGame.ts:315-322) and game.ts:1019/1026/1027/1028 read those captured flags
- **Problem:** finish() only affects halves opened after it. The half in progress keeps manualDefense (no maybeChangePitcher or maybeMoundVisit) or manualOffense (no automatic steals, bunts or pinch hits) until its third out. If the coach sims the rest while his tired starter is on the mound, nobody makes the change until the inning ends.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/game-sim/finishparity.ts: 300 live games, managing home. Pitch 'pitch' until our starter is past the bench's own hook (pitchBudget + 4 + HOOK) in the field, then finish().
- **Expected behavior:** After the hand-over, the bench makes the change the computer would make on the next batter.
- **Actual behavior:** 'cases ... 275; starter kept facing batters after the hand-over in 275 of them; 1182 extra batters; worst 76 pitches past the hook'.
- **Root cause:** The manual flags are closure parameters of createHalfInning, captured when the half opened. Only the `delegate` object is read on every plate appearance.
- **Recommended fix:** In finish(), also set benchCoach.pitching = true (the delegate the half already reads on every PA). Optionally close and reopen the current half's manual offence by passing a mutable flags object the way `delegate` is passed. *(Verifier's note: In finish(), also set benchCoach.pitching = true (the delegate object is read on every plate appearance), or call live.setBenchCoach(true) in store.autoFinish before finish(). Note that the journal records 'coach' actions, so if the store calls setBenchCoach it must journal that too, or the fix must live inside the engine's finish() so the replay stays exact.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/liveGame.ts`, `src/engine/game.ts`
- **Risk:** Simming a game from the field can hand the opponent a big inning off an exhausted starter, so a simmed game is not equivalent to a simulated one.

#### L54. A two-way reliever's entry sends the DH, who has already batted, back to the bench, and he can re-enter as a pinch hitter

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** A two-way reliever's entry sends the DH, who has already batted, back to the bench, and he can re-enter as a pinch hitter
- **Location:** src/engine/game.ts:530 coverPitcher (`this.benchTonight = [...this.benchTonight.filter((b) => b !== cover), dhMan]`); consumers liveGame.ts:420-424 benchAvailable and game.ts:2569-2571 maybePinchHit
- **Problem:** When a two-way man standing in the field comes in to pitch mid-game, coverPitcher ends the DH's night ('the DH's night ends') but pushes him onto benchTonight, and he is not added to usedBench. Both the manager's bench list and the AI's maybePinchHit then offer him, so a player removed from the game re-enters. That breaks the stated 'once out, out for good' rule. (The pre-game version at game.ts:419 is fine, because there the DH has not played.)
- **How to reproduce:** agents/game-sim/twoway_reentry.ts. makeTwoWay man in LF and in the bullpen, managing home. Play until the DH has batted, changePitcher(two-way man), then pinch-hit with the removed DH.
- **Expected behavior:** The removed DH is not offered and pinchHit refuses him.
- **Actual behavior:** 'brought in two-way Justin Nordstrom from LF: true; removed DH Martin Engelhardt (batted 1 AB) offered on the bench again: true' / 'pinch-hit accepted: true ... PA before 2 after one more call 3; in order now: true'.
- **Root cause:** coverPitcher reuses the pre-game seat-the-DH logic, which deliberately keeps the DH available, at a point where he has already appeared.
- **Recommended fix:** In coverPitcher, push dhMan into usedBench (or skip re-adding him to benchTonight) when he has a batting line. Keep the pre-game behaviour at game.ts:419. Extend tests/twoway.test.ts 'a two-way reliever taking the ball' to assert he is not available. *(Verifier's note: In coverPitcher, push dhMan into usedBench when he has a batting line, or always mid-game. Keep the pre-game path at game.ts:419 unchanged.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/game.ts`, `src/engine/liveGame.ts`
- **Risk:** Rare: it needs a two-way arm in the pen (god mode makeTwoWayOf, or a two-way starter moved to the pen). When it happens, it is an illegal re-entry in both managed and AI games.

#### L55. Two June games on one calendar day overwrite each other in season.boxScores, so player game logs lose games

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Two June games on one calendar day overwrite each other in season.boxScores, so player game logs lose games
- **Location:** src/engine/season.ts:2550 recordResult (`season.boxScores[today] = box`, keyed by calendar day); readers src/ui/screens/Player.tsx:173 gameLogFor, src/ui/screens/Draft.tsx:160 spotsPlayed
- **Problem:** stepDoubleElim lets a night boundary move by a round (documented in doubleElim.ts), so the coached program can play two bracket games on the same postseason day. The day-keyed store keeps only the second box. The bracket screen is unaffected because it reads the box attached to the slot, but the player card's game log and the Draft screen's position tally both iterate season.boxScores.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/game-sim/junebox.ts (8 worlds, simSeason + runPostseason with captureBoxFor set to a top team).
- **Expected behavior:** Every game the coached team plays appears in its men's game logs.
- **Actual behavior:** 'June box scores lost to a same-day overwrite: 7', e.g. 'world 0: BAY played 11 June games, 9 June boxes kept; days with two games: 82x2 102x2'.
- **Root cause:** BoxScore storage is keyed by day, while postseason days can hold two games for one team.
- **Recommended fix:** Key boxScores by `${day}:${home}:${away}` (or store an array per day), and update the readers (Today/Schedule look up by day and would need the game's key). *(Verifier's note: Store boxes per game, e.g. Record<number, BoxScore[]> or a `${day}:${home}:${away}` key. Update wire.ts:591-594, the Today/Schedule lookups by day, Player gameLogFor and Draft spotsPlayed. The save sanitizer at store.ts:9942 must accept the old shape.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/season.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Player.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Draft.tsx`
- **Risk:** A deep June run shows a game log with fewer games than the season line's G and drops the two decisive games' lines.

#### L56. Swapping relievers before the first one throws a pitch records a phantom appearance (G+1, 0 BF)

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Swapping relievers before the first one throws a pitch records a phantom appearance (G+1, 0 BF)
- **Location:** src/engine/liveGame.ts:385-386 (decision().outing calls fld().pitchLine(pitcher), which creates a line); season.ts foldSide (s.g += 1 for every pitching line)
- **Problem:** Rendering the dugout card reads pending.outing, and that creates a pitching line for the man on the mound. If the coach brings in X and then, before X faces anyone, brings in Y, X keeps an empty line, and foldSide credits him with a game. The same applies to a starter lifted before his first batter, who gets G and GS with 0 BF. recordResult already ignores 0/0 lines for rest, and so does the box.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/game-sim/phantom.ts: changePitcher(X) -> read pending -> changePitcher(Y) -> finish -> recordResult.
- **Expected behavior:** No appearance for an arm that faced nobody, or the engine forbids the second change until X faces a batter.
- **Actual behavior:** 'Kwame Carlisle: line exists true, bf 0 outs 0 pitches 0' / 'season G for Kwame Carlisle: 0 -> 1'.
- **Root cause:** pitchLine() is a get-or-create used by a read-only reporting path.
- **Recommended fix:** In decision() read fld().pitching.get(pitcher.id) without creating it, and/or skip 0-BF/0-out lines in foldSide like recordResult and pitchingLines do. *(Verifier's note: Make decision() read-only with fld().pitching.get(pitcher.id)?.outs ?? 0, and skip lines with bf === 0 && outs === 0 in foldSide. Optionally require the new pitcher to face one batter before another change, which is the real rule.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/liveGame.ts`, `src/engine/season.ts`
- **Risk:** Small inflation of G/GS for relievers in managed games.

#### L57. RBI credited on a ground-into-double-play

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** RBI credited on a ground-into-double-play
- **Location:** src/engine/game.ts:1411 (`bLine.rbi += errored ? 0 : counted`) after resolveOut's double-play branch (game.ts:2171-2201) scores the man from third
- **Problem:** Official scoring (rule 9.04(b)(1), which NCAA follows) gives no RBI when the batter grounds into a force double play. The engine credits every run that crosses on a non-error play.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/game-sim/gidp.ts (1,500 games, season seed 8).
- **Expected behavior:** No RBI for the batter on a GIDP.
- **Actual behavior:** 'GIDP 1595, GIDP with a run scoring 56', e.g. game rng 46: 'Horacio Thackery grounds into a double play. / Faustino Monroy scores from third.'
- **Root cause:** resolveOut does not tell the caller that the play was a double play, so the RBI rule cannot distinguish it.
- **Recommended fix:** Return a `doublePlay: true` flag from resolveOut's DP branch and skip the RBI for it. *(Verifier's note: Return `doublePlay: true` from the DP branch and skip the RBI at line 1411 when it is set.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/game.ts`
- **Risk:** About 1.7 extra RBIs per team per season, feeding the RBI leaderboards and record book.

#### L58. Pinch hitters always take the vacated glove: 203 non-catchers a season finish games catching, and there is no defensive substitution

*Area: game-sim · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Pinch hitters always take the vacated glove: 203 non-catchers a season finish games catching, and there is no defensive substitution
- **Location:** src/engine/game.ts:2555-2604 maybePinchHit (chooses the best bat regardless of position); TeamState.pinchHit game.ts:581-601 (sub takes the outgoing man's spot); no defensive-replacement path in game.ts or liveGame.ts
- **Problem:** The AI picks a pinch hitter purely on platoon-adjusted bat value. The pinch hitter then stays at the replaced man's position for the rest of the game, because no defensive replacement or double switch exists. Pinch-hitting for a catcher leaves an outfielder catching with the CATCHER_TAX of -26 to his fielding ratings. The human dugout offers Pinch hit and Bullpen only, so a coach who pinch-hits for his catcher cannot put the backup catcher back in.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/game-sim/catchers.ts (seed 11, full season, 4,320 team-games).
- **Expected behavior:** Pinch hitters are either chosen with the position in mind, or replaced defensively next half by a man who can play there.
- **Actual behavior:** Pinch hitters by cover tier at their final spot [own, natural, stretch, deep]: 193, 391, 598, 568. 'pinch hitter left to catch: 203', e.g. 'Saginaw State Ironsides: pinch hitter Leopoldo Saunders (RF) finished the game catching'.
- **Root cause:** Substitution is modelled for the bat only.
- **Recommended fix:** In maybePinchHit, prefer bats who can cover the outgoing spot (coverTier <= 1), or never pinch-hit for the catcher without a bench catcher. Add a defensive replacement step at the start of the next defensive half (AI and a dugout 'Defensive sub' row). *(Verifier's note: Smallest fix: in maybePinchHit, skip the catcher's spot unless a bench man with coverTier(h,'C') <= 1 remains. Prefer bats that can cover the outgoing spot. A defensive-sub action is a feature request.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/game.ts`, `src/engine/liveGame.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx`
- **Risk:** Late-inning defences are much worse than intended, and a managed coach is surprised by an outfielder catching the 9th with no way to fix it.

#### L59. Android system font size is applied as WebView text zoom on top of the in-app text size, and fixed-height pieces clip from 1.3x: the Home game card loses its last line, and from 1.5x the Text size control hides 'Larger', June's game buttons cut their labels and the live-game gauge label runs into its bar

*Area: gap-android-display-matrix · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Android system font size is applied as WebView text zoom on top of the in-app text size, and fixed-height pieces clip from 1.3x: the Home game card loses its last line, and from 1.5x the Text size control hides 'Larger', June's game buttons cut their labels and the live-game gauge label runs into its bar
- **Location:** native/android/com/playball/dynasty/MainActivity.java (no setTextZoom); Capacitor Bridge (no setTextZoom). Chromium AwSettings.updateFontScaleLocked (textZoom = Configuration.fontScale*100 unless the embedder set it), aw_settings.cc:611 SetTextZoomFactor, Blink font_builder.cc:313 and style_builder_converter.cc:2205 (font-size and every non-normal line-height multiplied by TextZoomFactor). Affected CSS: src/ui/design/screens.css:759 (.pb-wheel__slot height:168px) with src/ui/GameWheel.tsx:29 (CARD_H = 168), screens.css:775 (.pb-gcard overflow:hidden); src/ui/design/components.css:81-92 (.pb-seg overflow-x:auto, scrollbar hidden; .pb-seg__opt flex:1 0 auto; nowrap) used by Settings.tsx:176-182 (Text size); screens.css:223 (.pb-gauge grid-template-columns:70px ...)
- **Problem:** MainActivity never calls WebSettings.setTextZoom, so the WebView turns the user's Android font size into Blink text zoom. Every computed font-size and every px, em or number line-height is multiplied, but widths, heights, paddings and em boxes are not. This multiplier stacks on top of the in-app Text size (--pb-ts / --ts): 'Larger' plus system 1.3 is 1.69x. The two scales also behave differently. The in-app scale leaves px line-heights alone, while text zoom scales them, so layouts checked at in-app Larger do not predict the system path. Example: the Home wheel card fits at in-app Larger (content 166 px in a 168 px box) but overflows at system 1.3 (188 px).
- **How to reproduce:** Faithful text-zoom emulation in Playwright: agents/gap-android-display-matrix/tz-init.js measures each element's computed font-size and line-height and reapplies both multiplied by k through a MutationObserver, leaving boxes untouched. The matrix runs k = 1, 1.15, 1.3, 1.5 and 2 at in-app Normal and Larger across Home, live game 2D/3D (dugout, picker, final), June (next game, Bracket, modals), all six offseason steps plus the keep sheet, recruiting (board, sheet, filters), the Office rooms, Settings pages, Saves, Start, New career steps 0-4, the offer sheet and the god editors (sA/sB/sD/sE.cjs). Re-measured with the real fonts (FONT=dm for DM Sans online, FONT=roboto for the offline Android fallback) in probe-fixed.cjs, probe-labels.cjs and the dm- matrix pass (hardclips.py).
- **Expected behavior:** At Android font sizes up to the common 1.3 step, and ideally the Android 14+ 1.5-2.0 steps, no text is clipped or overlapped, and every option of the Text size control can be seen.
- **Actual behavior:** k=1.15: no defects with real fonts. k=1.3 on Pixel 7, DM Sans and Roboto alike: the front Home game card's content is 188 px in a 168 px box, so its last line ('Away · Midweek game', the series stakes and the Rival tag) is cut by the card border. At in-app Larger with k=1 it fits (166 px). 360 px phone at k=1.3: the Settings > Display Text size control shows only Small, Normal and Large, and 'Larger' sits behind an unhinted horizontal swipe (scrollW 334 > clientW 294). k=1.5 on 412: the same 'Larger' option is hidden. June 'Sim this game' / 'Play this game' are hard-clipped with no ellipsis (+2/+8 px; +22/+28 px at in-app Larger plus 1.3). The live-game 'Confidence' label runs 10-17 px into its stamina/confidence bar. k=2: the Home action labels are hard-clipped (+24 px) and the 3D/2D scoreboard pill's '1st' overlaps the base icon. Everything that scrolls (offseason steps, recruiting, rooms, settings, sheets, god editors, New career) reflows correctly at every k with real fonts. The first pass with the sandbox's wide DejaVu fallback overstated width clipping (for example it hid 'Larger' at 360 px even at k=1); those width results were discarded and re-measured with DM Sans and Roboto.
- **Root cause:** The WebView's text zoom is left at its default (AwSettings derives it from Configuration.fontScale), while the Home wheel and the live gauge use fixed px boxes: a 168 px slot hard-coded in CSS and in GameWheel's CARD_H physics, and a 70 px label column. Text zoom grows the text and its line-heights but not those boxes. Even an em-based box would not grow, because Blink resolves em lengths against the unzoomed specified size. The segmented control relies on overflow-x:auto with the scrollbar hidden, so an option that no longer fits quietly leaves the visible area.
- **Recommended fix:** Pick one scale. Recommended: in MainActivity.onCreate, after super.onCreate, call getBridge().getWebView().getSettings().setTextZoom(100). On first launch, seed the in-app Text size from getResources().getConfiguration().fontScale (for example 1.15 maps to Large and 1.3 or more maps to Larger), passed through a small plugin method or an injected global. The app's own four steps then remain the only multiplier and get tested as such. If system text zoom is kept instead: size the wheel slot from the measured front card (ResizeObserver on .pb-gcard.is-front feeding CARD_H) instead of 168 px, change .pb-gauge to grid-template-columns:auto minmax(0,1fr), and let .pb-seg wrap (flex-wrap:wrap) or add an edge fade to show it scrolls. *(Verifier's note: The evidence comes from emulation, not a real Android WebView, so one on-device check at 1.3x is advisable. The recommended fix, setTextZoom(100) plus seeding the in-app Text size from fontScale, is sound.)*
- **Files affected:** `native/android/com/playball/dynasty/MainActivity.java`, `src/ui/design/screens.css`, `src/ui/GameWheel.tsx`, `src/ui/design/components.css`, `src/ui/screens/Settings.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Postseason.tsx`
- **Risk:** Users who raise the system font size, a large share of older players, see clipped series stakes on every Home visit from 1.3x, and from 1.5x (Android 14+) clipped June buttons and a hidden 'Larger' option. The defect is cosmetic, not functional, but it hits the main screen.

#### L60. In landscape with the soft keyboard up, tab screens keep the app bar, top tabs and bottom tab bar (about 167 px), leaving 31-45 px of content: a Colleges search shows no results while typing

*Area: gap-android-display-matrix · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** In landscape with the soft keyboard up, tab screens keep the app bar, top tabs and bottom tab bar (about 167 px), leaving 31-45 px of content: a Colleges search shows no results while typing
- **Location:** src/ui/design/components.css:511-514 (.pb-tabbar always rendered, 56 px buttons + 12 px padding), :482 (.pb-appbar), :495 (.pb-toptabs); src/ui/screens/Colleges.tsx:51 (SearchField inside the tab frame); Capacitor SystemBars.java:199-211 (on WebView 140 and later the WebView parent is padded by the IME inset, so the page shrinks)
- **Problem:** When the IME opens, Capacitor 8 pads the WebView parent by the keyboard height, so the page gets shorter. Overlays and the New career, Saves and god editor screens cope: the focused field stays visible and the submit can be reached by scrolling. Tab screens, though, keep all of their fixed chrome. In phone landscape the remaining height (about 198-212 px) leaves a 31-45 px content strip, so the Colleges search box is half visible and none of its filtered results can be seen while typing.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/gap-android-display-matrix/kb.cjs: focus each input, shrink the viewport by the keyboard height (portrait 412x915 minus 330, 360x640 minus 290, landscape 867x388 minus 190, 915x412 minus 200), scroll the focused element into view the way Chromium does, then record the field and submit rects, the scroller height and hit-testing.
- **Expected behavior:** While typing, the field and at least a few results stay visible. The bottom navigation hides while an input has focus, as on native Android.
- **Actual behavior:** colleges land-867: scroller 'app-content pb-framemain' h=31 px (land-915: 45 px). portrait-360: 183 px (fine). New career name, Saves 'Save a copy' and the god Program fields stay visible in every case. 'Save a copy' drops below the fold at 360 and in landscape but can be reached by scrolling.
- **Root cause:** The frame's chrome rows (tokens.css .app-frame flex column; .pb-appbar, .pb-toptabs, .pb-tabbar) never collapse when the visual height collapses. Nothing listens for the IME, for example through visualViewport or a :focus-within rule.
- **Recommended fix:** Hide the tab bar while an editable field has focus inside the frame, for example .app-frame:has(input:focus, textarea:focus, select:focus) .pb-tabbar { display: none; }, and optionally the top tabs below max-height:420px. Locking portrait (android-release finding) removes the worst case. *(Verifier's note: Mostly subsumed by the orientation-lock fix. The residual case is landscape-capable large screens and multi-window. Hiding the tab bar with .app-frame:has(:focus) is an adequate fix.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/design/components.css`, `src/ui/screens/Colleges.tsx`, `src/ui/components/ui/controls.tsx`
- **Risk:** Searching colleges, or typing into any future tab-screen field, in landscape gives no visible feedback.

#### L61. Turning Sound off during a live game leaves the crowd loop playing until the game ends (and turning it on mid-game never starts it)

*Area: gap-android-lifecycle-media · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Turning Sound off during a live game leaves the crowd loop playing until the game ends (and turning it on mid-game never starts it)
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx:325-339 (crowd effect keyed only on liveOn); src/ui/sound.ts crowdStart/crowdLeverage/crowdSwell
- **Problem:** Settings opens as an overlay over the dugout (Manage.tsx:467 onSettings → openOverlay('settings')). One-shot sfx() check the preference at call time and fall silent at once. The crowd bed, however, is a looping AudioBufferSource started once by crowdStart(). The only code that stops it is the effect cleanup and the !liveOn branch, which re-run only when liveOn changes. crowdLeverage/crowdSwell keep modulating the bed's gain with no preference check. The reverse also holds: with Sound off at the first pitch crowdStart() returns early, so turning Sound on mid-game gives bat and glove sounds but no crowd for the rest of the game. Preloading is also skipped for the session, so the first few cracks load on demand, about 150-250 ms late in Chromium.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/gap-android-lifecycle-media/media.cjs: `node media.cjs soundoff-midgame` starts a managed game, plays 4 tactics, opens Settings > Sound over the dugout, toggles the real 'Sound' switch, waits, closes and plays 4 more. `node media.cjs soundoff-launch` is the same with Sound off at launch, toggled on mid-game.
- **Expected behavior:** Muting stops the crowd within the fade (crowdStop), and un-muting starts it.
- **Actual behavior:** soundoff-midgame: after the switch (prefs sound:false), the looping source stays active ('activeLoops=1') through the next 4 plays to the end of the run, with no 'stop' logged; the plays log vibrate only, with no one-shots. soundoff-launch: after switching Sound on, one-shots fetch and play but activeLoops stays 0.
- **Root cause:** `useEffect(() => { if (!liveOn) { crowdStop(); return; } … crowdStart(); return () => crowdStop(); }, [liveOn]);` has no dependency on the sound preference. sound.ts has no subscription to preference changes.
- **Recommended fix:** Have Settings' put() for `sound` call crowdStop() when turning off (export a setSoundEnabled(on) in sound.ts that stops the bed and, when on, re-runs preloadSfx()). Alternatively add a prefs-version or sound value from a small store or event to the Manage crowd effect's dependency list so it restarts or stops the bed. Make crowdLeverage/crowdSwell no-ops when the preference is off.
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx`, `src/ui/sound.ts`
- **Risk:** A player who mutes mid-game (on a bus, a call coming in) keeps hearing stadium noise until the final out and may assume the mute is broken.

#### L62. AI lineups depend on the device language: localeCompare name tie-break in bestNine changes who plays, and the same world diverges by year 2 under lt-LT

*Area: gap-android-lifecycle-media · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** AI lineups depend on the device language: localeCompare name tie-break in bestNine changes who plays, and the same world diverges by year 2 under lt-LT
- **Location:** src/engine/depthChart.ts:416-419 (bestNine rank tie-break); also strategy.ts:474, recruiting.ts:646, program.ts:2485/2634/2640/2658/2738, season.ts:3023, staffProjects.ts:92/255
- **Problem:** Engine tie-breaks call String.prototype.localeCompare with no locale. That uses the WebView's default ICU locale, which is the phone's language. Collation differs by language. In lt-LT 'Y' sorts between I and J (Yandel < Vincent). In cs-CZ and sk-SK 'CH' sorts after H (the CHC/CHS/CHK abbreviations move past DLT, and names like Christian and Chase move). In da-DK and nb-NO 'Aa' sorts as Å, at the end. On exact merit ties, bestNine therefore fields a different man depending on the device language. The world and its results then diverge, which breaks the 'every player gets the same ninety six programs' design (state/world.ts:10-11). The same save also plays forward differently on two phones, and the test baselines quietly assume an English locale.
- **How to reproduce:** 1) Pair census: agents/gap-android-lifecycle-media/loc-pairs.mts: of the 96 abbreviations, 45 pairs flip under cs-CZ and 62 under lt-LT; of 1,500 player names, 6,689 pairs flip under lt-LT and 2,784 under cs-CZ. 2) Outcome: locale-years.mts runs createSeason(4242) → simSeason → runPostseason → tests/headlessYear for 3 years with the default locale overridden (LOC=en-US|cs-CZ|lt-LT). 3) Site attribution: locale-sites.mts logs every comparison whose sign differs from en-US. 4) Browser confirmation (idb8.cjs): in a Playwright context with locale cs-CZ, 'CHC'.localeCompare('DLT') = 1 (en-US: -1); with lt-LT, 'YUM'.localeCompare('MOB') = -1 (en-US: 1).
- **Expected behavior:** Identical seasons regardless of the phone's language.
- **Actual behavior:** en-US and cs-CZ were identical for 3 years with this seed. lt-LT matched in year 1, then year 2 gave results hash e7594ee9aa vs 1e81d6c84f and national champion team 24 vs 12, and year 3 gave champion 14 vs 26 and a different lineups hash. All flipped comparisons came from depthChart.ts:419 (e.g. 'Yandel Danforth vs Vincent Clarendon', 'Yoel Bonaventure vs Owen Goodwin').
- **Root cause:** `const rank = (spot) => (a, b) => merit(b, spot) - merit(a, spot) || Number(inNine.has(b.id)) - Number(inNine.has(a.id)) || a.name.localeCompare(b.name);` takes the locale from the environment. The other call sites have the same pattern.
- **Recommended fix:** Replace engine tie-breaks with a locale-independent comparison: `a.name < b.name ? -1 : a.name > b.name ? 1 : 0`, or `localeCompare(b, 'en-US')`. Prefer comparing ids (String(a.id)) for players and abbr byte order for teams, so a rename cannot reorder either. Add a lint rule banning bare localeCompare in src/engine.
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/depthChart.ts`, `src/engine/strategy.ts`, `src/engine/recruiting.ts`, `src/engine/program.ts`, `src/engine/season.ts`, `src/engine/staffProjects.ts`
- **Risk:** Low player-visible impact, but it breaks cross-device determinism. The dynasty forks from what the same seed or save does elsewhere, and tests could fail on a CI box in another locale.

#### L63. Start's 'latest' Resume trusts the wall clock: a clock set back between saves opens the older career

*Area: gap-android-lifecycle-media · Evidence: code-reviewed · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Start's 'latest' Resume trusts the wall clock: a clock set back between saves opens the older career
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/Start.tsx:52-54; src/state/persistence.ts:501 (savedAt: Date.now()), :787 (list sort)
- **Problem:** The front door's Resume card picks `[...saves].sort((a, b) => b.savedAt - a.savedAt)[0]`, and savedAt is Date.now() at write time. The Saves list sorts the same way. If the device clock moves backwards between saves, the career the player actually played last sorts below an older one. Causes include a manual change, a dead-battery clock reset later corrected, or a wrong network time. Resume then opens the wrong dynasty, and 'saved N min ago' clamps to 'just now'.
- **How to reproduce:** Code path: save career A at clock T, set the clock to T−2h, play career B (autosave at T−2h+ε), return to Start. latest = A because A.savedAt > B.savedAt.
- **Expected behavior:** Resume opens the career most recently played on this device.
- **Actual behavior:** It opens whichever save carries the larger wall-clock timestamp.
- **Root cause:** Ordering uses only wall-clock time, with no monotonic tie-breaker.
- **Recommended fix:** Keep a monotonically increasing write counter in localStorage (or in a small IDB meta row) and stamp each save with `seq`. Sort by seq first and savedAt second. Alternatively remember the last loaded or saved slot id in localStorage and prefer it for Resume. *(Verifier's note: Could reasonably be rated POLISH. The simplest fix is to remember the last loaded slot in localStorage and prefer it for Resume.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/Start.tsx`, `src/state/persistence.ts`
- **Risk:** An occasional wrong-career resume. No data is lost, since the other career stays in Saves.

#### L64. God-mode renames cut emoji in half: names are truncated by UTF-16 code unit and save a lone surrogate

*Area: gap-edge-extremes · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** God-mode renames cut emoji in half: names are truncated by UTF-16 code unit and save a lone surrogate
- **Location:** src/engine/godMode.ts:167-168 renameProgram; same pattern at godMode.ts:90 (player name), godMode.ts:231 (staff name), src/state/store.ts:9706 godSetCoachMore (coach name)
- **Problem:** Every god-mode name edit is cleaned with `.trim().slice(0, 40)` (nickname `.slice(0, 30)`). `String.prototype.slice` counts UTF-16 code units, so when an emoji (two code units) straddles the limit, only its high surrogate is kept. The god `Field` input has no maxLength, so nothing stops a long name first. The broken string goes into `record.def.school` / `team.name` and is autosaved, so the bad character stays for the rest of the career and appears wherever the name is printed.
- **How to reproduce:** NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules node scratchpad/agents/gap-edge-extremes/e04-names.cjs. In a god-mode career, call godRenameProgram(userTeam, 'Big 🐻🐻🐻 State 🔥🔥🔥 University 🦅🦅🦅 Tech', '🦅🦅'). In the UI: God control center > Program > School, paste that name and tap away.
- **Expected behavior:** The name is cut at a whole character (grapheme), e.g. 'Big 🐻🐻🐻 State 🔥🔥🔥 University 🦅🦅', or a longer name is refused with a counter.
- **Actual behavior:** Stored school = 'Big 🐻🐻🐻 State 🔥🔥🔥 University 🦅🦅\ud83e', and the lone-surrogate check returns true. A lone surrogate prints as a replacement glyph or tofu, and it becomes U+FFFD if the name is ever text-encoded.
- **Root cause:** Truncation by code unit (`slice(0, N)`) instead of by code point or grapheme, plus no maxLength on the god Field input (ui/god/controls.tsx Field).
- **Recommended fix:** Truncate by code points (`Array.from(s).slice(0, 40).join('')`) or graphemes (`Intl.Segmenter`) in renameProgram, the player/staff name patches and godSetCoachMore. Also give the god Field a maxLength and a character counter. *(Verifier's note: One small correction: renaming again does fix it if the new name is shorter or contains no emoji. Truncate by code point, e.g. Array.from(s).slice(0,N).join(''), or by grapheme with Intl.Segmenter, in all four places.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/godMode.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/god/controls.tsx`
- **Risk:** Cosmetic but permanent: a corrupted school or coach name in a sandbox save (renaming again only repeats the cut). It only hits god mode, which is paid.

#### L65. Coach habit-badge thresholds use the constant WORLD_SEED, so every career gets identical 'hidden, per-save' thresholds

*Area: gap-player-attributes · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Coach habit-badge thresholds use the constant WORLD_SEED, so every career gets identical 'hidden, per-save' thresholds
- **Location:** src/state/store.ts:5759 (settleSeason / board meeting) -> habits.ts:91 badgeThreshold
- **Problem:** habits.ts and data/badges.ts say thresholds are 'seeded per save' and 'different in every save' so they cannot be farmed. But the store calls earnedBadges(coach.habits, coach.badges, WORLD_SEED), and WORLD_SEED is the constant 2027. Careers actually start on careerSeed() (random, NewGame.tsx:112), so the career's own seed is ignored.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/gap-player-attributes/twoway.ts (seed 36): the printed thresholds WORLD_SEED vs this career's seed are ironman 136/113, penhand 108/78, smallball 191/149, newsman 78/63, youth 13/16. The coach earned 'youth' after the 2nd year with freshmen=15, below this save's own seeded threshold of 16.
- **Expected behavior:** badgeThreshold(id, season.seed), so the number differs between careers.
- **Actual behavior:** The same thresholds in every career (e.g. Plays the kids always at 13 freshmen-seasons, The pen always at 108).
- **Root cause:** WORLD_SEED was passed where the career seed (season.seed) was intended.
- **Recommended fix:** store.ts:5759: `earnedBadges(coach.habits ?? {}, coach.badges ?? [], season.seed ?? WORLD_SEED)`. Add a habits test that two different seeds produce different thresholds through the store path. *(Verifier's note: Use `season.seed ?? WORLD_SEED` at store.ts:5759.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/habits.ts`, `src/state/world.ts`
- **Risk:** The anti-farming design is defeated once one player publishes the numbers. Low gameplay impact.

#### L66. RUBBER ARM has no measurable effect in simulated games (exactly zero with the standard and quick hooks)

*Area: gap-player-attributes · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** RUBBER ARM has no measurable effect in simulated games (exactly zero with the standard and quick hooks)
- **Location:** src/engine/game.ts:1185 fatigueMultiplier(..., fatigueBonus) vs game.ts:2685 maybeChangePitcher; strategy.ts:171 HOOK
- **Problem:** The badge only changes the fatigue slope past pitchBudget. But the sim pulls a pitcher at budget + 4 + HOOK, and HOOK is -15 / 0 / +18. Under 'quick' no plate appearance ever starts past budget. Under 'standard' a pitcher is at most a few pitches past it, where the slope difference is about 0.2%. The earn rule (110 pitches per game) is unreachable for nearly all arms for the same reason.
- **How to reproduce:** npx tsx rubber.ts (3000 games per hook, gold rubberArm on every pitcher vs none).
- **Expected behavior:** Fewer runs late in starts from badged arms, as the copy 'Loses less off his stuff past his pitch count' promises.
- **Actual behavior:** quick: 0 of 7543 outings end past budget, RA change 0.00%. standard: RA change 0.00% (identical box scores). patient: +0.04%. ab.ts N=8000: rubberArm every metric +0.0%.
- **Root cause:** The badge acts on a regime the pull logic almost never allows. Only a user who leaves a tiring arm in during a managed game can see it.
- **Recommended fix:** Have the badge extend the hook window as well (e.g. budget * (1 + size) in maybeChangePitcher and in the earn rule), or fold it into pitchBudget, so badged arms actually pitch deeper.
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/game.ts`, `src/engine/badges.ts`, `src/engine/ratings.ts`
- **Risk:** Badge promises an effect players will not see. Low impact.

#### L67. A two-way man's arm is outside his ceiling, his grade and his card: potential, overall and the card face read the bat only

*Area: gap-player-attributes · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** A two-way man's arm is outside his ceiling, his grade and his card: potential, overall and the card face read the bat only
- **Location:** src/engine/ratings.ts:745 ceilingReading / respectCeiling; development.ts:96 develop; ui/screens/PlayerHub.tsx:371 and 628; Roster.tsx:150/190; Manage.tsx:736; TeamCard.tsx:353
- **Problem:** Potential, the badge cap and the 'ceiling respected' rule all go through overallOf, which reads a two-way man as a hitter (bat only). develop() grows the arm by the same delta as the bat whatever its own level. So arms routinely end up above the printed ceiling. Several arm contexts also show and sort by the bat number, contrary to armValue's own docstring. Affected: Roster 'Pitchers' view, the live-game bullpen picker, and TeamCard's pitchers table.
- **How to reproduce:** npx tsx ai2w.ts (seed 777, 6 winters): Whitman Smallwood SO bat 49 arm 62 pot 55; Chase Castro FR bat 25 arm 38 pot 28; Carson Quesada bat 21 arm 37 pot 29, starting 15 games. Playwright ui2w.cjs (injected SO two-way, bat 49 / arm 60 / pot 49): Roster Pitchers view row reads '57 Tobias Twoway RF/SP Sophomore Pot. D 49 Now'. The card face reads 'Rating 49 Potential D', and its Ratings row lists only Contact/Power/Speed.
- **Expected behavior:** Ceiling and grade measured on max(bat, arm) (as draft rows already do, progression.ts:587). Arm contexts show armValue. The card face shows both halves.
- **Actual behavior:** The arm can exceed potential (62 vs 55). Pitchers views and the bullpen picker show the bat rating. The card hides the arm number.
- **Root cause:** ceilingReading/respectCeiling and develop's gap use overallOf only. UI call sites use overallOf where armValue is meant.
- **Recommended fix:** ceilingReading: for isTwoWay use Math.max(overallOf(p), armValue(p)), and compute the develop gap per half. Use armValue in Roster view==='arm', Manage bullpen picker rows and TeamCard pitchers table. Show 'Bat N · Arm M' on the PlayerHub face and ratingsLine for two-way men.
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/ratings.ts`, `src/engine/development.ts`, `src/ui/screens/PlayerHub.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Roster.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Manage.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/TeamCard.tsx`
- **Risk:** A two-way man is mis-graded (D grade on a B arm), and he is mis-ranked wherever pitchers are compared. Rare (1-10 in the country), so impact is low.

#### L68. Held badges can exceed badgeCap after a bust arc lowers potential ('3 of 2')

*Area: gap-player-attributes · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Held badges can exceed badgeCap after a bust arc lowers potential ('3 of 2')
- **Location:** src/engine/badges.ts:345 badgeCap; development.ts:86-91 arc reveal; PlayerHub.tsx:661, Player.tsx:466
- **Problem:** The cap is checked only when a badge is granted. A later bust arc lowers potential by up to 3 a year, which drops his grade and cap, but held badges are never trimmed. The card then prints e.g. '3 of 2 · his potential sets how many he can hold'.
- **How to reproduce:** census.ts seed 777, 10 winters: 0-2 players per year over cap, e.g. 'y4 Marshall Burnside holds 3 > cap 2 (pot 61)', 'y2 Timothy Hathaway holds 5 > cap 4 (pot 84)'.
- **Expected behavior:** Count never exceeds the cap shown, or the card explains it.
- **Actual behavior:** 'N of M' with N > M.
- **Root cause:** The cap is a function of the current potential, which can fall.
- **Recommended fix:** Freeze the cap at the highest potential reached (store a peak), or display max(held, cap). *(Verifier's note: Severity is arguably POLISH (display only). The cleanest fix is to compute the cap from a stored peak or scouted potential, which matches badgeCap's docstring.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/badges.ts`, `src/engine/development.ts`, `src/ui/screens/PlayerHub.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/Player.tsx`
- **Risk:** Cosmetic confusion on a few cards.

#### L70. A redshirted underclassman who is drafted and talked back keeps his redshirt flag, sits a second whole season, and still moves up a class

*Area: gap-player-lifecycle-trace · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** A redshirted underclassman who is drafted and talked back keeps his redshirt flag, sits a second whole season, and still moves up a class
- **Location:** src/engine/progression.ts:577 (departure is decided before the redshirt is banked at :621) and :840 reinstate; src/state/store.ts keepPlayer (calls reinstate); src/engine/depthChart.ts:75 available()
- **Problem:** departAndDevelop decides departure (line 577) before it reads the redshirt flag and calls bankRedshirt (line 621). A redshirted sophomore aged 21 at the draft (an 18-year-old arrival after his redshirt season, or any 19-year-old arrival) can be drafted. If the coach keeps him, reinstate bumps his class (SO to JR) and develops him at full growth, but never calls bankRedshirt. redshirt stays true and redshirtsUsed stays 0. available() returns false for a redshirt, so he cannot play at all the next season.
- **How to reproduce:** agents/gap-player-lifecycle-trace/probe-redshirt-drafted.ts (setState-level edits, disclosed): Full career; at day 0 setRedshirt(true) on a sophomore bat aged 20; raise his ratings to 95 so clubs draft him; finish the season and June through store actions; nextPhase to 'draft'; set board.spent very negative so the coach can afford the case; keepPlayer(id, 'role', 5000); roll the year; sim the next season.
- **Expected behavior:** The season he sat is banked as his redshirt (no class bump, redshirtsUsed = 1, flag cleared), the same as a redshirt who is not drafted, and he plays the next season.
- **Actual behavior:** Seed 77: 'keepPlayer -> stayed; class=JR; redshirt=true; redshirtsUsed=0', then 'new year 2028: class=JR redshirt=true available(day0)=false', then 'next season: g=0 ab=0; still redshirt=true'. The coach paid to keep a second-round pick who then cannot play for a second straight year.
- **Root cause:** reinstate() (progression.ts:840) duplicates only half of the survivor path: the class bump and develop. It skips the redshirt branch (sat → bankRedshirt, no class bump). The departure check also runs before that branch.
- **Recommended fix:** In reinstate, mirror the survivor path: if p.redshirt is true, call bankRedshirt(p), skip the class bump and use REDSHIRT_GROWTH; otherwise bump the class as now. Alternatively, have departAndDevelop bank the redshirt before the departure check. The same function serves rivalKeeps, so both paths are fixed. *(Verifier's note: Fix in reinstate: if p.redshirt, call bankRedshirt (no class bump, REDSHIRT_GROWTH); otherwise bump the class. Alternatively, bank the redshirt before the departure decision. Note that the leftover flag also counts against MAX_REDSHIRTS the next season.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/progression.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`
- **Risk:** Rare: it needs a redshirted, age-eligible underclassman who is drafted and then kept. When it happens the player is silently lost for a full season after the coach paid draft-retention budget for him, and the rule that a redshirt does not advance a class is broken.

#### L71. During the winter the player card's career table shows the season just played under next year's class, labelled '· so far'

*Area: gap-player-lifecycle-trace · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** During the winter the player card's career table shows the season just played under next year's class, labelled '· so far'
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/PlayerHub.tsx:579 careerYears; src/engine/season.ts:522 liveCareerYear; src/ui/screens/Player.tsx:934-940 SeasonTable
- **Problem:** archiveSeason runs at the draft step, before departAndDevelop, so the archive correctly files the year under the class he played it at. careerYears then replaces that archived row with a 'live' row whenever the man is on the roster. In the winter the live row is rebuilt from the same season books, but with p.classYear already bumped by departAndDevelop. The finished year is shown as the next class, and SeasonTable adds '· so far' to a season that is over. For a portal arrival, the live row is also built against the coached program, so his old school's stats appear under the coached program's name (the walk-back variant of this is already known).
- **How to reproduce:** Playwright: agents/gap-player-lifecycle-trace/ui-probe2.cjs (pixel7, dev server): sim season 1 and June, nextPhase to 'draft', open a returning junior's card and go to Career. Headless: trace.ts compares liveCareerYear(...).classYear with season.careers[id] at every draft step.
- **Expected behavior:** Between the draft step and the year roll, the card shows the archived row (classYear as played, no 'so far'), or a live row only while the season is in progress.
- **Actual behavior:** Diego Kaminski (archive '2027:SO') is shown as 'Junior · so far' for 2027 (ui-probe2 output: career page class labels ["Left field · Junior · Age 20","Junior · so far","Junior · so far"]). trace.ts flagged it every winter for every survivor who played: '[2028] 5-star: player card (careerYears) shows 2028 as SO; archive says FR', and the same for the 1-star, the 4-star bat and the best SO bat, in each of 3 winters.
- **Root cause:** careerYears always prefers liveCareerYear for isOurs, and liveCareerYear reads the mutated player object (class already advanced) without checking whether the season is complete and archived.
- **Recommended fix:** In careerYears, use the live row only when the year is not yet archived (archived.some(y => y.year === live.year) → use the archived row), or only while !seasonComplete(season). Mark 'so far' only for a season in progress. *(Verifier's note: In careerYears, return live = null (and keep the archived row) when archived.some(y => y.year === live.year) or when seasonComplete(season).)*
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/PlayerHub.tsx`, `src/engine/season.ts`, `src/ui/screens/Player.tsx`
- **Risk:** Cosmetic and self-healing at the year roll, but every winter it misstates every returning player's history on the screen where the coach is making draft and portal decisions.

#### L73. Every pipeline cools 4 points every winter, even one that was worked or signed from all year

*Area: gap-program-levers · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Every pipeline cools 4 points every winter, even one that was worked or signed from all year
- **Location:** src/engine/economy.ts:534-544 agePipelines (idle at :539); src/state/store.ts:5951 (agePipelines(..., year + 1)); src/engine/staffProjects.ts:346 (lastWorkedYear: year); src/state/store.ts:6503 (addPipelineSigning(..., year + 1) runs after aging)
- **Problem:** agePipelines cools a state by 4 when idle = year - max(lastSignedYear, lastWorkedYear) > 0. The roll calls it with year + 1, but season work stamps lastWorkedYear = the current year, so idle is always >= 1. Signings are stamped year + 1, but only after aging has already run, so they are aged one roll later anyway. Contrary to docs/05 §63.4 ('an idle year cools a market by 4') and the function comment ('cool when a staff stops signing from them'), no state is ever exempt. 'Maintain pipeline' cannot hold a state.
- **How to reproduce:** npx tsx full.ts 4242 5 3: Ohio is worked by the coordinator every week of every season.
- **Expected behavior:** A state worked (or signed from) during the season keeps its strength through the roll; only idle states cool.
- **Actual behavior:** Ohio 78 at season end -> 74 after the roll (worked in 2027); 100 -> 96 (worked in 2028); 100 -> 96 (worked in 2029). stored lastWorkedYear 2027 when aged at 2028. season1.ts: Michigan 100 -> 96 after a full season of Build work.
- **Root cause:** Off-by-one between the year the work and signings are stamped with and the year agePipelines is asked about (year + 1).
- **Recommended fix:** In rollYear call agePipelines(eco, year) (the season just played), or compute idle as year - 1 - lastActive and decay only when idle > 0. Add a test: a state with lastWorkedYear = Y aged at Y + 1 keeps its strength.
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/economy.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/staffProjects.ts`, `tests/economy.test.ts`
- **Risk:** Small: 4 points a year off every relationship. But the Maintain kind is pointless as named, and the Network room's history ('Last signing or project 2029') contradicts the drop.

#### L74. Facilities room previews leave out the building-count rung, which adds training, appeal and injury protection on top

*Area: gap-program-levers · Evidence: both · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Facilities room previews leave out the building-count rung, which adds training, appeal and injury protection on top
- **Location:** src/ui/screens/ProgramRooms.tsx:674-705 facilityRows; src/state/store.ts:3196-3204 leagueWinter, 3613-3617 applyCoachMods, 419-420 userRecruitingPitch; src/engine/recruitingPlan.ts:118-128; src/engine/economy.ts:570-575 FACILITIES
- **Problem:** Each building card previews only facilityEffectAt(building, level). The engine also applies FACILITIES[eco.facilities], the legacy rung keyed on how many buildings exist: +3/+6/+9 training to both bats and arms, +0.06/0.13/0.20 recruit appeal, x0.96/0.93/0.86 injuries. A first build therefore does far more than its card says, and an upgrade (which never moves the rung) does exactly what it says. That skews the build-vs-upgrade decision. The guard is labelled 'Arm injury risk' but applies to every hitter's daily injury roll too (season.ts:1934).
- **How to reproduce:** net.cjs (Playwright, pixel7): with the cage built, the Clubhouse card reads 'Appeal to recruits +12% / Hitter and pitcher training +1 / Arm injury risk -3%'. dev.ts prints the training inputs leagueWinter actually passes.
- **Expected behavior:** The card shows what building or upgrading changes, including the rung step.
- **Actual behavior:** Building the cage alone (preview 'Hitter training +4', no pitcher or injury rows): trainingBat 27 (+7), trainingArm 23 (+3, pitchers too), injuries x0.96, appeal +0.10 instead of +0.04. Adding the clubhouse as a second building: the rung moves 3->6 training, 0.06->0.13 appeal and 0.96->0.93 injuries; the card shows +1 / +12% / -3%.
- **Root cause:** Two facility models are layered (the legacy count rung and the per-building levels), and the preview reads only the second.
- **Recommended fix:** Fold the rung into facilityEffects (so the preview's facilityEffectAt delta includes the rung step when level 0->1 increases the count), or retire FACILITIES[] from the four readers. Rename 'Arm injury risk' to 'Injury risk'.
- **Files affected:** `src/ui/screens/ProgramRooms.tsx`, `src/engine/economy.ts`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/engine/recruitingPlan.ts`
- **Risk:** The coach misjudges builds vs upgrades; the copy understates the first build by 2-3x.

#### L76. Money and point levers for development and game nights are below perception, though sold with point values

*Area: gap-program-levers · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** Money and point levers for development and game nights are below perception, though sold with point values
- **Location:** src/engine/progression.ts:536-539 (growth = 1 + (training-20)/500); src/engine/game.ts:355-356 (coachOffMult/DefMult 1bp per point); src/engine/economy.ts:371-391 staffBonus, 413-423 devBonus; src/ui/StaffCandidateDialog.tsx:41-70; src/ui/screens/ProgramRooms.tsx:684-688
- **Problem:** Measured on identical worlds. Every returning man gains about +3.39 OVR a winter on his own. A Hitting Barn L1 ($620k, shown as 'Hitter training +4') adds +0.054 OVR per hitter per winter. All three buildings at L3 plus two elite teaching assistants (~$4.6M of builds plus ~$900k/yr wages) add +0.26 bat / +0.33 arm. Training skill 99 adds +0.51. On game nights, OFFENSE+DEFENSE at the 99 cap moved W% by +0.4 points over 6,000 games (within noise), and a typical game-side hitting coach ('+10 to your offense') moved RS/G by +0.02 (se 0.05). The 'Game specialist' assistant shape is effectively dominated. By contrast, season work (+2-5 points on three men's attribute) and pipelines (+12-39% interest) are strong.
- **How to reproduce:** npx tsx dev.ts (development A/B, 8 seeds x 4 teams); npx tsx devbase.ts (baseline); npx tsx skills.ts 6000 (coach mods A/B with simGame).
- **Expected behavior:** A lever priced like a season of budget, or sold as '+10 to your offense', produces an effect a player can notice over a few seasons.
- **Actual behavior:** See numbers above; docs/05 table row 23 confirms the 1bp/point design, so this is calibration rather than a wiring bug.
- **Root cause:** Deliberately small multipliers on a calibrated engine ('a light thumb on the scale'), but the money and UI framing present them as substantial.
- **Recommended fix:** Either raise the channels (for example growth 1+(t-20)/200, coach mods 3-5bp/pt, and re-run the goldens) or have the cards state the outcome ('about +0.1 overall a winter per hitter') so the choice is informed. *(Verifier's note: Narrow to the framing: state the outcome on the cards (e.g. 'about +0.05 overall per hitter a winter'). Do not recalibrate the coach game mods, which are documented as intentionally small.)*
- **Files affected:** `src/engine/progression.ts`, `src/engine/game.ts`, `src/engine/economy.ts`, `src/ui/StaffCandidateDialog.tsx`, `src/ui/screens/ProgramRooms.tsx`
- **Risk:** Spending decisions feel meaningless and the staff-shape decision collapses; there is no corruption risk.

#### L77. A 'Cold' pipeline already gives about 75% of an established pipeline's interest edge

*Area: gap-program-levers · Evidence: runtime-tested · verifier: **confirmed***

- **Issue:** A 'Cold' pipeline already gives about 75% of an established pipeline's interest edge

- **Problem:** Any nonzero strength switches on 55% of the pipeline edge at once. A state at 1-34 strength (labelled COLD, with the Network room's 'Pipeline' marker at 35) gets most of the interest boost an ESTABLISHED one does. Only the reach bonus waits for 60. The tier names suggest nothing happens below 35.
